name: Faith & Flame: the Provençal Tribunal

covenants.name: Tolosa Paratge
covenants.notes:
Votes and standing. Tolosa Paratge has nine votes at Tribunal, cast by faction. Most of the Tribunal believes it is destroying itself and has tacitly agreed, out of decorum, to let it settle its own affairs and see what is left; individual magi act on their opinions only behind the scenes. Renaud of Stella Durus worries for his pater Cyprian, and the Coenobium has always admired the covenant's style. Each faction wants the Coenobium, and the Ostal des Exiles, on its side. A new covenant that ignores the factions is ignored in turn; one that backs the wrong side may face Wizard's War. Its civil war may come before the Tribunal of 1221 if anyone brings a case.

The founding year is not given: the covenant was one of the four that made up the Tribunal when the regional Tribunals were set up in 773.
covenants.summary:
An old, cosmopolitan covenant in a regio under the city of Toulouse, on an island in the ghost of a holy lake: nine magi of five Houses, a lone follower of Verditius among magi of Jerbiton, Flambeau, Criamon and Ex Miscellanea. It has outlasted centuries of Hermetic politics, but the crusade has split it in two, and Wizard's Wars between its own members have killed two magi and left the rest afraid. Its magi guard the city's genius loci and think of themselves as the city's servants; when the citizens turned on each other, madness and death came to the covenant too.

It was founded in the Order's first generation as a Diedne covenant, among the four with which the Val-Negra Tribunal began, large for its day, with six or more magi for two centuries, and rumoured to excel at spirit magic, which gave it a faintly sinister name. Its refusal to admit Quaesitors after the mysterious death of the Tribunal's senior Tremere maga was among the first sparks of the Schism War. In that war Flambeau magi stormed it and slew its magi, and held the site until the Gorgiastic Cathar Anaïs arrived and rebuilt it as a covenant of many Houses. As the city grew the regio grew harder to reach, but the covenant rose in power and fame. Some think Anaïs's teaching, popular among the grogs, helped shape Cathar doctrine; others think the debt runs the other way. Its lineage of Gorgiastic Cathars, theurgical dualists, lives on here, and the survivors of Berinor joined it in 1210.

A run of brilliant magi made it famous for culture and urbanity and for a quiet hand in the growth of Toulouse's institutions, the capitouls above all. Its magi kept ties with every power in the walls (guilds, bishop, capitouls, count), and the good of the city and the covenant held them together even when their meddling crossed. The leader, Augustus, a senior Quaesitor, saw that nobody looked too hard at their dealings with mundanes as long as the covenant and the Order came to no harm. Through the crusade it stayed loyal to the city and would serve no foreign master.

In the weeks before de Montfort's death in 1218, Bishop Foulques persuaded Augustus that the city would fall, and he asked the Gorgiastic Cathars to leave for their own safety. They refused; one, Marc, called it betrayal of everything the covenant stood for and declared Wizard's War on him, a thing almost unheard of between covenant mates. Augustus did not take a Cathar pacifist seriously, but Marc, sure that Augustus was in a demon's grip, killed him in a muddled quarrel in the tower. A month later Carolus St. Tropez declared Wizard's War on Marc, who did not resist, and killed him. Mariola was made leader, but she did nothing, and the covenant broke into the Blacks, who side with the Cathars, and the Whites, who would expel the heretics for bringing ruin on their sodales. The Blacks are the stronger and hold the island; the Whites plot in the city to take it back, by appeal at the Tribunal of 1221 or by Wizard's War.

A narrow path winds up the cliffs of a small rocky island to red brick townhouses round an eight-storey octagonal tower of black stone. A few covenfolk and some magi live on the island; many prefer the city. Summoned by a few lines of Occitan verse, an enchanted boat rows between the island's jetty and the last rooftop on the shore. The covenant keeps an inn in the city, thirty houses and some eighty covenfolk, many of them artisans or labourers in Toulouse. Beneath three of the houses lie well-equipped laboratories, despite the Dominion, and several magi keep sanctums in the city, working on the island by day and sleeping in Toulouse.

Its people, the Tolosates, are proud of their place among the first covenants of the Order (few dare mention that it was Diedne then). Newcomers must serve ten years before full membership unless they were apprenticed and gauntleted here; visiting magi use Organization Lore: Tolosa Paratge in place of Etiquette; guests must be invited before crossing the lake; and hundreds of other customs go unmentioned to newcomers because the residents think them ordinary, sometimes with awkward or dangerous results. 'Paratge' means something like gentility: its magi are proud of Occitan language, poetry and culture, and famous across the Order as patrons of artists, poets, troubadours and original minds. Many a performer has been rowed to the impossible island to sing, and woke in his own bed afterwards wondering if he had dreamed it, beside a heavy purse of silver. Those apprenticed here wear a small silver flower, members a gold one, and members who were also apprenticed here a jewelled flower of gold and silver.

Its covenfolk are split evenly between the factions. Most live in the city; about six grogs and a dozen covenfolk are besieged in the regio, their friends outside plot a rescue and may seek help from magi outside the city or by Redcap, and covenfolk of both sides brawl in the streets, drawing citizens into the fighting.
covenants.what_matters:
Votes: 9 at Tribunal, divided between the factions
Vis: none named in the book
Income: an inn in Toulouse, thirty houses, and the trades of some eighty covenfolk in the city
Library: the covenant's old collection (no books named); a borrowed text is stuck there since the split
Laboratories: on the island, and under three of its city houses despite the Dominion
Enchantment: Adam Carpentiere's boom at Pont-Vieux tames the Garonne and props up the fading regio
Enchantment: a boat that answers a short Occitan poem and rows between the last roof and the island
Treasure: rumoured to hide a legendary hoard, perhaps the gold Quintus Caepio tried to steal
Customs: ten years' service before full membership; guests by invitation only; flowers of silver, gold or both by rank
Customs: Organization Lore: Tolosa Paratge stands in for Etiquette for visiting magi
Boon: Regio; Urban; Prestige (one of the Tribunal's oldest and most cultured covenants)
Hook: Fractured Council (Whites against Blacks); Heretics (the Gorgiastic Cathars); Weak Aura (the regio is fading)
Hook: City; Mundane Politics (ties to count, bishop, capitouls and guilds); Rebellious Covenfolk (fighting in the streets)
Tension: the Blacks hold the regio; the Whites, too afraid to enter it, blockade it from labs in the city
Tension: both sides deprive each other of magical resources, against the Code, but nobody has brought a case
Tension: St. Tropez killed Marc in a lawful Wizard's War and may seek martyrdom before he is convicted of anything
Tension: the Black faction may ask Stella Durus, through Cyprian's filius Renaud, to join it; the Whites may use Mariola's letters with Jean Marie of Stella Durus to keep it neutral or win it
covenants.secrets:
The regio is tied to the prosperity of Toulouse as well as to the river: the city's conquest and strife weakened it, and the magi's feud mirrors the city's. Healing the city (a university, or championing Occitan learning) is the only lasting cure.
Bishop Foulques came to the island as a gifted young troubadour; his memory of it may have been altered by magic, or he may think it a dream.
Mariola is rumoured to be an initiate of the Matres & Matrones.
Raimond of the Blacks believes he will drown in the Garonne and fears no other death.
Adam joined the Whites over his debts to the Jewish moneylenders of Cahors and an old grudge against the Gorgiastics, who opposed his boom.

covenants.name: Ostal des Exiles
covenants.notes:
Votes and standing. The Ostal counts six votes in the Tribunal's reckoning, but the Tribunal has not recognised it, and its recognition is an open question for 1221. It weighs every covenant by what it could give the cause and what it could take in return, courts Stella Durus for Renaud's experience, and will press at Glanum, with the other faidits, for licence to defend themselves and to win back what the crusade took, looking for support from Garus and Castra Solis's milites. Aedes Mercurii thinks it draws crusaders' eyes to the Order; Castra Solis admires its spirit but would rather fold its magi into quieter covenants; the Coenobium would temper its zeal or bring it under its own direction; both factions of Tolosa Paratge would like its help.

The founding year is not given; the covenant took shape after the Tribunal of 1214.
covenants.summary:
The House of the Exiles: the newest covenant of Provence, hidden in the caves under Castle d'Aguilar, where magi whose covenants the war destroyed have gathered. As the faidits are a force in the region's politics, so these Hermetic faidits have lost labs, libraries and homes; older magi have left for other Tribunals, but younger ones will not. Shocked by the ruin of Mistridge, Windgraven and Lariander, they formed the covenant after the Tribunal of 1214 to defend their homeland and Occitan civilisation. They welcome new Spring covenants as allies and recruit hard for the defence of the county against the northerners. More than outcasts, they may be outlaws: they are ready to meddle with mundanes to stop the south's destruction, even at the risk of a Wizard's March, though any blow they strike will be subtle, for they know what bringing ruin on one's sodales means.

The grotto was known to the Order of old as a mithraeum and a vis source. Garsenda of Lariander survived the destruction of her covenant at Montgey in 1211; after Tres destroyed Mistridge in a Wizard's War, Rixenda was the first to take shelter at Aguilar; and in Gilbert of Flambeau, a magnetic figure, the exiles found both unity and purpose: resistance to the northerners whatever it costs. The Tribunal has not recognised the covenant. It does not formally owe the lords of Termes allegiance, but they know it is there and tolerate it. It is a clearing house for any magus willing to fight the crusade: four magi keep sanctums here, but the number present runs as high as eight or nine. It is an important centre of the Knights of the Green Stone, where that cult is used.

Seven magi are members, four of them the leading figures. The covenfolk are mostly seasoned fighters, with few women or children, since many of the refugee women are celibate Cathars; if the covenant is to last, that must change. Few grogs live in the dark caves; most lodge in the villages round about. The turb drills constantly, backed by companions who are mostly faidits, minor lords, knights and serjeants, well horsed and armed, ready to risk everything for their homeland. Some of the maimed defenders of Bram serve as grogs, and Pons de Morlhon is among the companions.
covenants.what_matters:
Votes: 6 counted at Tribunal, though the covenant is not yet recognised
Vis: the grotto was a known vis source of old (Art and amount not given)
Aura: Magic 3 in the grottoes; the Flambeau mithraeum within (Magic 5) lies inside their Aegis, untouched
Library: next to nothing; the exiles' libraries burned with their covenants
Boon: Natural Fortress (caves under a six-towered castle the crusaders passed by); Veteran Fighters; Hidden Ways
Hook: Refugee; War Zone; Gender Imbalance (few women and children); Hermetic Politics (unrecognised)
Mundane: shelters under the faidits of Aguilar and the lords of Termes, who tolerate them
Allies: the Knights of the Green Stone, led by Gilbert, with links to the cult in the Rhine and Normandy
Tension: Gilbert's vengeance against Rixenda's hope of acceptance by the Tribunal
Tension: Popilia hates all Cathars, Gorgiastics included, while Rixenda and Garsenda sympathise with them
Tension: none of the exiles has forgiven Tres for Mistridge
Tension: the Flambeau of the mithraeum may soon find them and must decide what to do
Tension: the Coenobium hates Gilbert for leaving House Jerbiton for Flambeau
covenants.secrets:
Garsenda roused the villagers of Montgey, with the demesoilles, to massacre the crusader column in 1211, and so brought the crusaders down on Lariander. She dreads the Order learning she brought ruin on her sodales.
Gilbert may be a mystagogue of the Knights of the Green Stone; Garsenda met him through an esoteric cult, perhaps the same.
Gilbert has boasted that he would fight a second Schism War for his homeland even if the Grand Tribunal condemned him.

covenants.name: Castra Solis
covenants.notes:
Votes and politics. Castra Solis holds 17 votes, with the Praeco's and the Presiding Quaesitor's besides. The Coenobium is its firm ally, and together they can carry almost anything, though both know the smaller covenants must not be driven to walk out. Bellaquin counts it a staunch friend, Stella Durus usually follows Renaud's lead toward it, Ara Maxima Nova follows it or abstains, and the Ostal des Exiles thinks it misguided; Aedes Mercurii hates it and works against it at every turn. In private its magi think Aedes Mercurii a liability too big to fight openly but apt to wreck itself. At the 1221 Tribunal the faidits and refugees will seek the approval and backing of Garus and his milites.

The milites are Flambeau, mostly Hoplites, who stayed at Castra Solis after each war and have sworn a chivalric oath of service before Garus; under him they see themselves as knights serving a liege. The Mithraians of the House are mostly Christian; some have fought in the Reconquista in secret. They are split over the milites but united in contempt for the Mercurian Flambeau and their pretensions; the pious here think the Mercurian flamen at Tribunal blasphemous.
covenants.summary:
The domus magna of House Flambeau, whose device is a flaming yellow sun, and one of the strongest covenants in the Tribunal. It is the home of every kind of warrior magus the House breeds, from soldierly Mithraians to knightly milites, and its seventeen magi are mostly Flambeau. Its outlook is still northern, and Primus Garus sets most of its course: it backs the crusade and the Church, its attitudes are very Christian and its aims very political. It is generous to those who work with it and deeply distrusts Tytali, refusing help to any new covenant with many of them.

Kaeso, a Christian wizard who joined House Flambeau in 809, drew his strength from an old underground temple of Mithras in the hills by the Garonne. Though he sat at Tribunal for Val-Negra and spent his years in the mountains beside Apromor, his master, and the Founder, he raised there the Hoplites, soldier magi first known for hurling Pilum of Fire from behind a mighty Parma; fighting the sahirs of Iberia, merciful Kaeso made 'join or die' mean 'join', bringing many foes into the House. He rose to the inner circle of the Legion of Mithras, and most Hoplites followed him into the cult.

In the 840s raids on the western coast grew, and by 850 the Flambeau took the Norse raiders and their vitkir for an organised Order of Odin. Kaeso fortified his temple near Bordeaux with the House's backing and named the camp Castra Solis, the camp of the sun, under a sun quartered in four. Bordeaux fell to the pagans two years later; the Hoplites, unsure how far the Code let them strike at mundanes and unwilling to burn the city, were ambushed again and again by the rune wizards, and Kaeso was among the dead. In 855 the survivors built a true stronghold, Sinapis, in Anjou, and Castra Solis became a mobile camp of tents, seen from outside as Sinapis's offshoot. The war smouldered for over a century; the Hoplites' outposts, warded with the Aegis, became covenants counted as part of Castra Solis, Mimizan among them. The Hoplites told the Grand Tribunal of 997 of the raiders' three coastal settlements burned and the vikings gone. By then magi of other Houses, Tremere and Guernicus above all and one notable Greek maga of Merinita, had joined them, but the Diedne, who suffered from the raids, would not fight beside such pious Mithraians, deepening the Hoplites' suspicion of them.

When the Schism War opened with the Diedne's capture of the portals at Harco and the assault on Val-Negra, the Primus returned to Castra Solis to direct the House and seemed to abandon Val-Negra; most of the Gascon Diedne fled, many burning their sites behind them. Peace came at last, the new Primus stayed and built, and Castra Solis became the domus magna. When the Normandy Tribunal split in 1103, it led the faction that joined the enlarged Provençal Tribunal, bringing the magi of Sinapis, who gave up their site, Mimizan and other small covenants. It has been stable and powerful ever since, and hosted the bitter Tribunal of 1214 when Toulouse was besieged.

Its magi range from the newly gauntleted to the frail Primus. In the last twenty years two older magi of House Guernicus who lived here, each Presiding Quaesitor in turn and both younger than Garus, have died, and everyone, Garus included, expects him to be next. The Praeco Dama and her filia Marie are members though they live at Mimizan and near Poitiers; Beatrice of Guernicus is registered here but lives in the Arelat.
covenants.what_matters:
Votes: 17 at Tribunal, plus the votes of the Praeco and (if Beatrice is confirmed) the Presiding Quaesitor
Library: a fine collection with a military bent (described in Houses of Hermes: Societates; no books named in Faith & Flame)
Enchantments: many devices kept to defend the House when needed
Vis: Rebecca's personal source, 5 pawns of Corpus each spring equinox from afterbirth rendered at a hillside shrine
Vis: Dama carries 15 pawns of Faerie Vim in three gold rings and can raise 25 more within a week through her cult
Vis: Rebecca keeps 15 pawns of Corpus in a string of animal skulls
Income: the House's sponsorship of tourneys on the covenant's fields
Chapters: Mimizan (Dama and Rebecca) and the manor near Poitiers (Marie); Beatrice's sanctum at Glanum counts as a small chapter too
Portal: none; the Primus never thought one needed
Boon: Aura (Magic 3); Manor House; Prestige (domus magna); Veteran Fighters (the milites); Famous Resident (the Primus)
Hook: House Covenant; Chapter House; Hermetic Politics; Superiors (the House looks to it)
Cult: the Legion of Mithras, whose inner circle under Marcus Minor truly leads the covenant; services in its mithraeum (Divine 4) are near-sacraments
Tension: Aedes Mercurii claims Val-Negra's legacy and the title of domus magna, and Flammarcus means to be Primus when Garus dies
Tension: Garus is ancient and the succession is open; Garus is not of the Legion's inner circle
Tension: Beatrice has fallen out with Garus, or with a society of the Arelat, and keeps away
Tension: Dama is openly pagan, which unsettles the pious magi
Tension: Marie's push to carry the Tribunal's border into Poitou and Aquitaine
Tension: the faidits want the milites' backing, even open magic, against the crusaders
Hook: Garus owns one of the old Redcap lanterns that light the way through Val-Negra's regio
covenants.secrets:
The mithraeum under the covenant is Kaeso's copy; the true temple lies secret under Bordeaux.
Dama, the Praeco, killed the Presiding Quaesitors Senex (1210) and Tibaut (1219); her familiar Maju is becoming a demon (see her sheet and the Serpent's Venom).
Tibaut's lab notes on Senex's last inquiry are in his sanctum here; Senex told no one where he went.
Dama won the Chief Redcap Alazais's tacit support by secretly making a Longevity Ritual for her mundane companion, and counts on the covenant's weight to bury any motion against her.

covenants.name: Tres' Band
covenants.notes: The book gives no founding year, aura or season for the band; the section the Tribunal chapter points to for Tres is missing from Faith & Flame. Its two other magi are unnamed.
covenants.summary:
A roving covenant in all but name: the notorious rusticanus Tres Ex Miscellanea, his two filii, also rusticani, and their custodes, gone to ground in the moors and woods near Bazas since the Tribunal of 1214. Tres leads a ragtag following of outcasts and opportunist routiers from the northern armies, and came back to the Tribunal of his birth seeking vengeance.

In the winter of 1209 he declared Wizard's War on every magus of Mistridge, the famed tower on a precipice in the Val du Bosque; some say to avenge Windgraven, others that its proud magi had refused him hospitality and treated him as a hedge wizard. With his two fellow rusticani, a host of mercenaries carrying magic weapons of his own making, and magical siege engines, he levelled the conjured tower and killed its defenders. At the Tribunal of 1214 he was charged with arming hirelings and calling them grogs; many deplored it, but the war was justly declared and no ruling barred grogs from it, so the vote went narrowly his way. He wisely vanished before Mistridge's friends could take revenge.

The band holds three votes it never casts: it does not attend Tribunal and opposes nearly everything the Order does. It is aloof toward new covenants at first, and over many seasons comes to hate those that lord it over the mundanes around them, which it sets out to dissuade; it would rather not teach the lesson of Mistridge again but would not shrink from it.
covenants.what_matters:
Votes: 3, never used; the band does not attend Tribunal
Craft: Tres's magic weapons and siege engines; some think one of them struck down Simon de Montfort at Toulouse in 1218
Boon: Hedge Tradition (the rusticani, an Ex Miscellanea tradition of craft magic)
Hook: Constantly Mobile; Infamous (Mistridge); Hermetic Politics
Tension: the friends of Mistridge want revenge; the Ostal des Exiles, made of Mistridge's survivors, has not forgiven Tres
Tension: hostile to any covenant that makes itself a ruling class over the peasantry

covenants.name: Aedes Mercurii
covenants.notes:
Votes: 18 at Tribunal, the second bloc after the Coenobium (chapter three's table).

Tribunals: it hosted the Tribunal of 1207, where Oxioun of Tytalus spoke at length for keeping out of mundane affairs. In 1214 the meeting moved from Toulouse to Castra Solis, to its anger, and its magi threatened to walk out, which could have voided the Tribunal; Tibaut and the Chief Redcap averted it. If the Tribunal of 1221 decides to act against the crusaders and the Church, the bloc it leads may boycott the 1227 meeting and, with the four covenants a Tribunal needs, ask the 1228 Grand Tribunal to let it secede.

The Cult of Mercury (P13, a note, not a record): the rebirth of the Mercurian religion began at Val-Negra under Priamitus of Mercere with Apromor of Flambeau's support, flourished in the early 900s, and had split into many groups by the Schism War. The cult seeks the 37 Great Rites of the Roman priesthood; a few know non-Hermetic Mercurian rituals, worked only with the most loyal. Promising magi may be invited to join. Its flamen opens each day of Tribunal in masks and coloured robes, speaking for the gods; few take it seriously, the devout of Castra Solis think it blasphemy, yet the flamen have real hidden influence. The initiation into Mercurian Magic, the Consecration of Priamitus, ends at an ancient temple of Mercury such as this one on the Mercuralia, 15 May.

After the Schism War a priest of Janus here, Petrarchus of Guernicus, tried to join the Way of St James to the Via Domitia by a Mercurian ritual into one great road network, and failed.

The book gives no founding year (the split came just before the Schism War; 1003 is assumed) and no season (Autumn is assumed).
covenants.summary:
The Cult of Mercury's covenant in the high Pyrenees, about eighteen magi on two sites joined by a Mercere Portal: the fortress of the Dorsum on Pic du Midi d'Ossau and the Templum in the Cirque de Gavarnie, close by the lost site of Val-Negra. Its device is a fiery dragon devouring its own tail.

On the eve of the Schism War many of Val-Negra's Flambeau, moved by one magus's vision, left the domus magna with magi of other Houses and took over a nearby outpost and Val-Negra's lesser halls across the mountains, among them the great temple of Mercury that gave the covenant its name. When Val-Negra fell its survivors joined them, and Aedes Mercurii declared itself a Provençal covenant. After the war it put about that Val-Negra was gone and its legacy had passed to Aedes Mercurii, and its own heavy losses in the fighting made the claim believable. It is counted among the strongest covenants of the region, though nothing like Val-Negra at its height.

Its magi hold themselves the last unbroken heirs of the Order of Mercury and each serves as a priest (flamen) of a Roman god fitting their magic. For most, the Tremere above all, this is ceremony: naming a patron god is like naming a spell for him, and the few true pagans are thought odd. The priests of Mars, nearly all Flambeau, and of Pluto, mostly Tremere, are the strongest factions; the Verditius keep a small priesthood of Vulcan; Aintza leads that of Janus, Ricardus serves Bacchus, and Midius is High Priest of Mercury and flamen of the Tribunal.

Eleven magi live at the Dorsum and seven at the Templum, and the covenfolk split the same way. The two halves show one face to outsiders but have drifted apart since the war: the Templum's magi keep faith with what they see as the pagan, historical ways of the Order of Mercury, while the Dorsum's are united only by hatred of Castra Solis and their claim to Val-Negra's inheritance.

Politically it is contentious and rebellious, the difficult stepchild of the Tribunal, which many think dangerous fanatics. It leads the conservative bloc of the mountains (with Ara Maxima Nova, Stella Durus and Miniata Sophia), holding that magi have no business in mundane quarrels and should wait out the crusade in their isolation, despises the Mithraian Flambeau of Castra Solis for calling their covenant the domus magna, and fights any new covenant in the region that will not ally with it, though its magi agree on nothing but blocking Castra Solis, so newcomers get mixed answers.
covenants.what_matters:
Site: two sites joined by a Mercere Portal, the Dorsum fortress (aura 5) and the Templum (aura 4, 8 inside the Temple of Mercury)
Vis: the book names no source
Library: the casting notes of the Mercurian ritual Set the Stones of the Via, kept with reverence in the Templum
Library: a copy of the lesser Mercurian ritual Link the Rent Path, unstudied for centuries
Library: many books written by Malfortis, and Ricardus's tractatus
Enchantment: one of the forges of Hephaestus, deep in the Dorsum, kept by Ruberus as priest of Vulcan
Boon: Natural Fortress, Vast and Labyrinthine (the Dorsum), Mystical Portal (the Mercere Portal), Legendary Site (the Temple of Mercury), Ceremonies (the Mercurian rites)
Hook: Fractured Council (Templum against Dorsum); Rival (Castra Solis); Pagans (a few true pagans among its priests); Hermetic Politics (leader of the conservative bloc)
Tension: Flammarcus calls himself Pontifex Maximus and leader, but Oxioun led the covenant at the 1207 Tribunal and Ophilio's word would carry if he chose to use it
Tension: the Dorsum's hatred of Castra Solis against the Templum's pagan traditionalism
Tension: the Mercurians despise the Neo-Mercurian orders of other Tribunals as traitors and fools
Hook: lost outposts at Saint Jean Pied-de-Port (razed 1177, perhaps with a lapis mercurius), north of Girona, and the portal to Val-Negra, abandoned when the Schism War began
Hook: sanctums of magi dead or in Twilight, untouched in the Dorsum's depths
Hook: Priamitus's original ritual scroll may lie hidden in Val-Negra
covenants.secrets:
Protendus works as an unofficial, tacitly approved Quaesitor, against Tytalan influence from the north; he keeps it quiet by oaths enforced with certamen.
Ruberus is secretly a friend of Garus, Primus of Flambeau, and secretly loves Dama, the Praeco.
Flammarcus may stop at nothing to become Primus when Garus dies.

covenants.name: Bellaquin
covenants.notes:
Votes: 5 at Tribunal. Bellaquin likes new covenants: the more the merrier.

Covenfolk: three groups who do not much like each other. The almogavars of the Andorra Company replaced the old turb as custodes when Robert came; the original covenfolk, few, ageing and mildly resentful, stayed on in other roles; and the largest group are Ordino Andorrans working for wages, a few as specialists. Newer magi brought their own shield grogs: Artemis is always guarded by two lean, leather-clad men trained at Coeris whom she calls the Danior, and Antoinette brought back four Scandinavian warrior women from an Itinerarium as sanctum guards, to impress Michael and outdo the Tremere.

Tolomae, the Cathar sympathiser who led the Procrustean League and urged open war on the Church, is called Tolomae of Bellaquin; House Jerbiton cast him out in 1216, and he was Marched and slain early in 1218 (chapter three also calls the Coenobium his former covenant).
covenants.summary:
A Jerbiton covenant of five magi in a large house in the village of Ordino, Andorra: remote, yet deep in both mundane and Hermetic business. Its device is a red plumed hawk holding a scroll within a gold ring.

It was founded in 1016, late in the Schism War, by Flambeau who rebuilt an abandoned castle by magic as a stronghold, the Chateau de Penne in Tarn, high above the Aveyron a day north-north-east of Toulouse. The war ended before it fought, the Flambeau left, and the Jerbiton have held it since. The castle was famed as one of the loveliest seats of the Order. Peasants settled round it, the magi found themselves managing land, then playing at lords over a private fief with vassals and puppet domains granted to friends. Jealous neighbours twice charged them with breaking the Oath, and twice the Tribunal found they had brought no ruin on their sodales; they stayed just inside the Code and were prized as a bridge between mundane and Hermetic society.

In the end their feudal ties caught them between two warring allies. Helping either would break the Code, helping neither would break their oaths, and their compromise, paying scutage to both and selling healing elixirs to both, convinced both sides, egged on by senior churchmen who wanted the magi gone, that Bellaquin had stirred up the war for profit. A surprise assault, helped by a treacherous companion, destroyed the castle and killed several magi; possibly other magi arranged it. Archmagi had advised a fallback, and the survivors took what they could from hidden reserves, destroyed the rest, left the site to mundane proxies and moved to Andorra in 1202. No one brought charges, since the damage fell only on Bellaquin.

Twenty years on it is richer than ever on a smaller scale, and many call it a new covenant that had a quick spring and summer after the old one's winter; its magi hold that nothing broke but the address, and they kept their charter. Locally they pass for kindly rich outsiders who bring distant merchants' trade; in the Order they cultivate an air of casual indifference and some unhealthy stubbornness. No trade happens at the covenant, but it sits at the centre of a merchant network on both sides of the mountains reaching to Germany and Italy, and it banks for magi and mundanes alike: not lending, but moving funds across distances as the Templars do, by magic, to an agreed place at agreed times, or with more effort almost anywhere.

Of the old members only Valgravian remains, with Antoinette, filia of an old member; three died in the attack, two left the Tribunal, and three more have since died or passed into Twilight. Bellaquin has room and wealth for more and would welcome promising young magi.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: nearly 100 pawns in store, and sources yielding about 30 pawns a year (not named)
Income: banking, moving funds for magi and mundanes; a merchant network from Iberia to Germany and Italy
Income: the Andorrans' fairs, where Castra Solis and Ara Maxima Nova send agents to gather news
Defence: an Aegis of the Hearth of the 8th magnitude; the Andorra Company of almogavars; a fortified manor above the town
Laboratories: every magus's lab customised, with one empty lab used as a storeroom
Boon: Wealth, Hermetic Services (banking), Veteran Fighters (the almogavars), Local Ally (the Andorrans)
Hook: Infamous (the fall of its first site); Mundane Politics; Divided Loyalty (three rival groups of covenfolk)
Ambition: a Catalan Tribunal; more magi in the region mean more influence
Tension: Valgravian feels a stranger among the newer members and misses the poets and musicians of old
Tension: Antoinette's hidden love for Captain Michael, and Michael and Artemis's unspoken attraction
covenants.secrets:
Rumour says the Danior are homunculi, less open to Mentem magic, easily mended, and with a bloody habit of twisting Artemis's orders.
Antoinette fears Michael will learn of her affair with Carolus of the Rhine Tribunal during a Jerbiton fosterage at Oculus Septentrionalis.
Other magi may have engineered the fall of the first Bellaquin.

covenants.name: Miniata Sophia
covenants.notes:
Votes: 4 at Tribunal, cast for the most morally apt course or not at all. In 1221 they are expected to side with the conservatives who would wait out the crusade.

Story seeds. Multiplicity of Wisdom: someone after the secrets of Fertility magic (Ancient Magic) may try to find the covenant after meeting its members at Tribunal. The French king may try to seize Niaux in 1226 or 1227 when the Count of Foix resists royal claims, perhaps with inquisitors hunting Cathars, the count's wife being one. Aptly Put: a case the characters must win at Tribunal needs Miniata Sophia's votes, so they must show their cause is the apt one, or their opponents' the base one, by digging at the gathering itself.

Founded about forty years before 1220.
covenants.summary:
A young Criamon covenant of four magi in the cave of Niaux, in the hidden Vicdessos valley about a day's ride south of Foix. Its device is a white hand, fingers raised and spread, on an ochre disc. It was founded about forty years ago by the eremite Leonarda, drawn by the cave's paintings, and announced itself at the Tribunal of 1193, registering its site with the Redcaps as the village of Niaux.

Its magi seldom leave the cave and the hills round it, yet they have come to the last four Tribunals, always voting and arguing with knowledge. They make no alliances and show no leanings: they vote for whatever seems most morally apt, or abstain, and generally hold no opinion of other magi, who mostly return the favour. Some call it an underground reflection of the Cave of Twisting Shadows.

Their Path is their own version of Walking Backwards (see Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults) and live self-sufficiently, troubling the village as little as they can. Each magus in turn spends a season living in Niaux as a guest of the villagers, sharing Parma with a village ambassador and helping with whatever the town needs, keeping magic out of sight and working the most useful spells after dark; that season they do no lab work and wear leper's robes, to hide any Enigmatic stigmata and keep strangers off, which supports the story that they are hermits seeking enlightenment in the cave. Every third day the magus in the village brings supplies to the cave mouth, where another meets them. The season serves newcomers as the Avenue of Surrender and Station of the Service to Harmony, and reminds the rest of that lesson.

The rest of the year they study their Arts, the texts they trade by letter, and the paintings, seeking the magic hidden in the pigments. Leonarda holds the paintings to be an expression of the Enigma and has woven them into three later initiations (the Avenues of Healing, of Adulation and of a Thousand Beautiful Faces, with their Stations). The last Avenue, which ends at the Threshold of Repose, is still ahead of her, and she cannot yet see how the paintings would fit it.

There are no grogs: the Criamon feel no need. Arnaud de Miglos, the local viscount and Foix's vassal, protects the village from his garrisoned castle, and the villagers, who supply the covenfolk mostly at second hand, always pay their taxes promptly and so draw no notice. A few covenfolk are hunters who could fight if they had to and keep watch only as they range; a couple of well-travelled ones fetch things the magi want; and the little community sends out small loads of iron mined in the hills and worked into ingots and rods.
covenants.what_matters:
Income: iron mined in the hills and worked into ingots and rod stock
Library: texts traded by correspondence; the cave paintings themselves, studied as the Enigma
Mystery: the Path of Walking Backwards, with the paintings built into later initiations
Boon: Regio (the painters' cave); Seclusion; Local Ally (Niaux and Arnaud de Miglos)
Hook: Hidden Resources; Missing Aura in the village; Mundane Politics (the French crown's claims on Foix after 1226)
Ally: the Redcap Embeth, who visits twice a year and points interested Criamon to Niaux after vetting them
Rule: an outsider must earn deep trust before visiting even the covenfolk in Niaux; a magus arriving by chance is welcomed but must swear never to reveal the site

covenants.name: Stella Durus
covenants.notes:
Votes and politics. Stella Durus has 5 votes at Tribunal. Busy with their own projects, its magi rarely meddle in others'. They have usually backed Castra Solis, Renaud's domus magna, and act against it only when they must; they let the Coenobium lead so long as it leaves their projects alone; they feel they have escaped notice so far and see no need for the faidits' resistance. Jean Marie's letters keep it close to Bellaquin. It honours Ara Maxima Nova's unspoken claim to the Via Domitia. With Aedes Mercurii, Ara Maxima Nova and Miniata Sophia it is counted among the conservative southern covenants that would wait out the crusade, and that might boycott or secede if the Tribunal moved against the crusaders.

Marcella's research. Her next steps might be: a ritual like Wizard's Communion, needing magi strong in Muto, Rego and the elemental Forms, to bind a lasting link to the Aude's spirit and harvest it as one distils Vim vis, but with a richer yield, at the cost of the daimon's knowing and loathing it; a long negotiation in which an Aspect of the daimon makes a willing sacrifice, strengthening its bond with the town's locus over time while yielding vis through a brief loss of Might; a ritual murder of the river's spirit for a single bolus of vis of the storyguide's choosing; or the search for the Roman watermills of Barbegal, which would set her against the Coenobium, so she would pay others, perhaps the players, in texts and connections to look for her.
covenants.summary:
A small, cosmopolitan Autumn covenant on the outskirts of Narbonne, of Bonisagus, Flambeau, Jerbiton and one far-sighted, ambitious Tytalus. Its device is a shining five-pointed star. Its name speaks of the stars that guide explorers and plays on the senses of durus: hardy, rough and steadfast. Its magi study the region's magical spirits and ancient ruins, and want above all to go unnoticed by Hermetic and mundane politics while the crusade runs its course.

It began as a small estate with an old manor farm beside the Aude. Its magi lived quietly among their neighbours, helping the city grow through the eleventh and twelfth centuries while the covenant recovered from its long-dead founders' part in the Schism War and some ventures against the Moors of Iberia. Marcella of Bonisagus and Jean Marie of Jerbiton are its seniors; Marcella's love of exploration and Jean Marie's taste for a pleasant country life drew Renaud, with his interest in Mithraic sites and troubadours.

Its one real rule is that its members are individuals who have joined for protection and shared resources. Beyond a loose wish to keep the house standing, nothing binds them: they skip council meetings, squabble over who does which chore, and guard their own time. They like being near Narbonne and find the river a good enough moat. Its policy is to hide in plain sight.

Its covenfolk and grogs come from many lands, brought by different magi over the years, and speak half a dozen tongues, the cause of most of their quarrels; Marcella likes the mix and urges them to keep their languages up. Its veteran turb is skilled but bored, and may not drill where it could be seen, so Renaud looks for ways to keep it sharp.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: none named by the book; Marcella and Giacoma seek a way to draw vis from the spirit of the Aude
Income: Jean Marie helps run a relative's shipping company
Library: Bonisagus research on spirits and genii loci, and Jean Marie's Intellego, Mentem, Rego and Vim (no books named)
Aura: Magic 2, in the basements where a mithraeum stood
Boon: Veteran Fighters (the bored turb), Manor House (the villa), Informants (Jean Marie's troubadour contacts)
Hook: Poorly Defensible; Urban (Narbonne at the door); Roman Ruins (the villa and its mithraeum); Fractured Council
Tension: Renaud and Jean Marie want to take in a troubadour; the others fear a wandering storyteller inside the walls
Tension: Ducaru's meddling in noble marriages could bring charges at Tribunal
Tension: the magi skip meetings and bicker over chores
Policy: neutral toward new covenants, unless one takes its resources or settles between the Pyrenees and the counties of Albi, Béziers and Toulouse; it harasses those for at least a season a year
Politics: 5 votes; usually follows Castra Solis through Renaud; would stay out of the crusade; counted in the Pyrenean conservative bloc
covenants.secrets:
Marcella has not yet found how to link a city's people to a daimon, how to call up an Aspect to harvest without the daimon noticing, or how to tap a spirit's locus for vis and leave it undisturbed; she guards her progress closely, and Toulouse's spirit would teach her much, but she will not go there.
If the ritual murder of the Aude's spirit is done, the river will silt up over the years and Narbonne will decline as a port.
Ducaru may have helped Ramon Berenguer IV escape the Templars in 1219, and works toward marriages that will, in time, marry the count's daughters into the royal houses of France, England and Sicily and to Richard of Cornwall.

covenants.name: Ara Maxima Nova
covenants.notes:
Votes and politics. Ara Maxima Nova has 4 votes. To keep the crusaders' eyes off it, it gives Castra Solis no reason to look closely, following its lead or abstaining. Luc thinks the Coenobium a bully to be defied and undermines it quietly. It talks with Aedes Mercurii and sometimes helps it, curious what secrets lie unrecognised in that old covenant; it would side with the faidits only if crusaders threatened it. It sends agents to the Andorran fairs. With Aedes Mercurii, Stella Durus and Miniata Sophia it is counted among the conservative southern covenants that would wait out the crusade.

Story: Ara Maxima Nova might fund a joint expedition to the Hesperides with the players' covenant, built on what the players' magi learn (Ancient Magic). A storm raised by the dragon of the fierce currents could part the ships or wreck them on arrival, leaving the two parties to explore the islands, look for each other and a way home, and perhaps fight over the islands once reunited.

Stella Durus honours its claim to the Via Domitia, and the two are cordial but distant neighbours. The Plaine de la Crau in Arelat, where Heracles stoned the giants Bergion and Ligur, interests it greatly.
covenants.summary:
A Summer covenant grown rich on wine and cork, whose name means New Great Altar and whose device is a wine barrel. Three Merinita and a Gifted Mercere keep their laboratories here and have founded a splinter cult of the Keepers of a Thousand Tales, coloured by the Cult of Heroes and centred on the Via Domitia, the road both Heracles and Hannibal took. The Merinita hope to reach the spirits of vineyards older than Antiquity and learn the Dionysian mysteries from them, tracing how their road to enlightenment runs with the Roman roads and the wanderings of Heracles.

Founded twenty-five years ago by its Merinita, it exists to develop the cult its senior magus made. After studying Heracles' trials in the east and reaching several initiations by experiment, they came west to explore the remaining labours and live nearer Rome. Perpignan's self-governing commune suited them, and so did open access to what is left of the Via Domitia. Their magic soon made them leading producers of wine and cork, with good stock even in years when weather or bad luck ruin others, sold to loyal buyers who ask little; with their mundane duties met, the magi have money to spare.

Secrecy matters above all: they cast the Aegis of the Hearth at night, hidden by Luc's Imaginem, so that even most covenfolk never see it. They do not deny their House but are truly estranged from it. Friendly enough, they stay out of Tribunal politics unless their research is threatened. Their Herculean studies have gone better than the Dionysian, since the hero's tales escaped the purges that pagan mystery cults suffered.

Three customs mark them. They make pilgrimages to Rome, to St. Stephen of the Carriages, a temple of Heracles turned church to save it, the original Ara Maxima, to study its architecture, seek relics, regiones and clues, hampered by the Dominion and wary of the clergy; they hope to rebuild it at the heart of the covenant and collect any art or text on Heracles, their treasure being a huge carved bearded head of the hero, gazing downward, recovered from Roman ruins. They seek the Hesperides: their charter sends a magus with grogs on a quest of up to two years every five years, and they have searched Durenmar, the remains of Alexandria's Museum, Constantinople and the universities of Paris and Montpellier, and would trade generously for a reliable route. And they court the faeries of the region's farms and vineyards; they have found nymphs and satyrs, but none who knows or will share the old rites. They believe ascension lies in retracing Heracles' labours through rituals that mirror them, crimes and penance included, and look for the tomb of Pyrene somewhere to the south-west.

Covenfolk come from peasants seeking a new life in Perpignan, refugees from the Reconquista among them, and, to some dispute, slaves Etienne buys from Arab merchants. Many vineyard and cork workers have no idea whom they serve. A trusted, well-paid inner household tends the magi but is seldom allowed to travel far; only the small, well-trained turb, the foremen and the men who deal with Perpignan's merchants go farther.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: none of its own named by the book; the Ancient Wine Press (Herbam 4, or Infesta 6), the Nemausian Spring (Creo or Aquam 3) and the Abandoned Mine (Terram 2) lie unclaimed in Narbonnais
Vis: the Via Domitia's Heraclean vis (Intellego 6) is on the road it guards, though its magi do not know of it
Income: wine and cork, sold to loyal customers who ask few questions
Library: texts on Heracles, the Dionysian mysteries and the Via Domitia, and Jeanne's faerie journals (no books named)
Treasure: a colossal carved head of Heracles from the ruins of Rome
Charter: a Hesperides quest every five years, one magus and grogs, for no more than two years
Boon: Wealth, Secondary Income (wine and cork), Loyal Covenfolk (the inner household)
Hook: Road (the Via Domitia); Dark Secret (Luc's cult); Ceremonies; Slavery; Hermetic Politics (estranged from House Merinita)
Tension: Jeanne and Luc's wife Miriam quarrel over the cult; Etienne chafes at Luc's neglect of the covenant
Tension: its magi challenge others on the Via Domitia to certamen, which the Coenobium resents
Policy: harasses new magi whose Faerie or Seeker interests overlap its own unless they join the cult; otherwise neutral, so long as the Via Domitia is left open to it
Politics: 4 votes; follows Castra Solis or abstains; Luc quietly works against the Coenobium; counted in the Pyrenean conservative bloc
covenants.secrets:
Luc's cult is the secret behind the covenant; Castra Solis's devout members would quietly move against his resources if they learned of it.
The magi do not know that walking the whole Via Domitia with a lion's skin yields 6 pawns of Intellego; local faeries do, and might sell the knowledge.
Luc's grumbling to Dama about Tibaut's questions, after a certamen he lost to the Quaesitor, warned her of the investigation (see The Serpent's Venom).

covenants.name: The Coenobium Rhodanien
covenants.notes:
The Hermetic toll. Every magus visiting Avignon openly is asked to call at the covenant and say why he has come and how long he will stay, under the rules of hospitality House Jerbiton promotes. The Tribunal's Redcaps, at Alazais's urging, let it be known that a silver florin holding a pawn of vis is expected as a goodwill gift. Those who pay are given a consul as guide, answerable for their conduct in the town, which some visitors find a meddling minder. Those who decline are thought ill-bred and watched by the covenfolk; a guest who flaunts himself or works magic on the townsfolk draws Xiphos or the covenant's hedge allies, and though the Coenobium stops short of Wizard's War, it obstructs such a magus patiently for years, even trumping up charges at Tribunal.

The visitor's code. Guests are offered food, lodging and a laboratory, and the consuls choose a patron for each, usually a Jerbiton. In return a visitor is to: introduce himself properly, ideally sending word ahead by Redcap; bring a small gift, by custom a silver florin holding a pawn of vis; say why he has come and for how long, and tell his patron when he leaves; behave with decorum and restraint, helping his patron if asked; and go at once if asked to. The patron explains these rules, answers for the guest, shields him from harm and inconvenience, and gives him a token gift at parting; the duty is honoured more than rewarded, and a patron may call on other members for help or be let off a season of service.

Membership. Consuls vote; up to a dozen visitors and independent magi are linked to the covenant at any time, among them up to six new Jerbiton resting between stages of their Itinerarium. Guests do not vote, but if they behave well they may ask to use the covenant's resources with the approval of their patron and two other consuls, much as at many Autumn covenants. The First Consul may ask any magus there for help with his resources, though he need not agree. There is no roster of covenfolk: each consul keeps his own servants, kin, grogs, artists and troubadours.

Votes: about 20 at Tribunal, the largest bloc.

Founded: the book gives no year, only the late tenth century, about two centuries ago; it already existed when the Birds of Camargue joined it in 970.
covenants.summary:
The largest covenant of the Tribunal, depending on how many visitors are in at once: a chain of chapter houses along the lower Rhone and east along the coast of Provence, called in the Redcap rolls Mascum Sub Pontem after its original main site, and by most Provençal magi just the Coenobium (Normandy's magi say Coenobium Rhodanien, to tell it from their own small unofficial coenobia). Its device is an arched bridge, and its motto 'Together we rule, divided we fall'.

Late in the tenth century, against Fraxinetum's raids, the heirs of several Provençal covenants and some eremites bound themselves together. Mostly Jerbiton, they used their families and friends among the nobles and the Church to raise William I of Provence's army, which broke the Saracens at Tourtour and took their base in the Maures; they narrowly escaped the Quaesitores' wrath for destroying Fraxinetum, and found the league too useful to dissolve. The Birds of Camargue joined in 970, Barbegal's and Yf's survivors came too, and Anaïs of Jerbiton, last of Portus Cottiae, was among the loudest for a Hermetic hegemony. Since then, by cooperation and nepotism, its magi have gained control of or influence over most magical and mundane resources in the County of Provence, which they justify as insurance against ever again being caught unready by Hermetic aggression.

The heart is urban, at Avignon, with holdings at Arles, at the edge of the Camargue, across southern Provence and as far north as Grenoble; in truth the whole Rhone sustains it, in magic and in trade. Two or more magi are always travelling the river in great barges made by the resident boatwright, smaller boats carry Redcaps on errands, and many of its standing enchantments cover the whole river or work as long as one is afloat on it or a major tributary. Few magi are ever in one place at once, which perhaps helps them tolerate one another.

Over two dozen magi, mostly Jerbiton, are consuls, its voting members; nearly a dozen others are permanent guests, and up to six Redcaps may be staying. Jerbiton and Mercere dominate, but there are Bonisagus (especially Trianomae), Ex Miscellanea, Verditius and even Flambeau; as most belong to loose Societates, Alazais cares less for a magus's House than for an agreeable manner and commitment to the covenant. It is led, unusually, by the unGifted Chief Redcap, Alazais of Mercere, as First Consul, both autocrat and leader, leaving most magi free for their own pursuits much of the year. Its Jerbiton care little for magical power and much for worldly pursuits, with views of Beauty that differ from their housemates' elsewhere.

The covenant fosters rather than supplants the region's masques: witches, cunning men and women, herbalists and faerie doctors who get its protection from the authorities and from other magi, and in return serve as unGifted agents and informants along the coast and the Alpine foothills, harvest and guard vis, make charms for its people, and spread its sway, while the magi keep to the letter of the Code. It welcomes visitors and specialists warmly (see the notes for its toll and code), and would welcome allied chapter houses elsewhere in the Tribunal, but its help comes with the hint of later annexation, and no independent covenant has flourished in southern Provence in over a century.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: Castra Peccaius salt, from a brackish pond in the ruins on the Petit Rhone; 1 to 3 pawns of Corpus a year, dedicated to longevity (+2 to a Longevity Ritual's Creo Corpus total, one pawn a ritual); the land is leased from the Abbey of Psalmody through dependants
Vis: the round sling stones of the Crau, a handful of Terram pawns a year, gathered by grogs as a punishment
Vis: Imaginem in rare murex shells and kermes beetles at Toulon, taken by Aloysius Porphyri
Vis: the Hermetic toll, a silver florin holding a pawn of vis from each visitor to Avignon, which pays the non-Jerbiton specialists
Vis: most vis sources in the region are held by the covenant or guarded by its hedge allies
Trade: the salt vis goes to a research covenant of the Greater Alps for favours to its elders
Income: the Factory at Trinquetaille, magically worked trades, Rhone shipping, and the purple and crimson dyes of Toulon
Library: no books named; each consul keeps his own, with the Mercer House's records
Allies: the masques of the Coenobium, led for it by Lavandarius; the Chief Redcap's network of Redcaps, retired Redcaps and their kin
Allies: the abbot of St André, secretly; Hugh III of Baux through his cousin Marcus; Castra Solis in Tribunal
Boon: Urban; Mercer House; Wealth; Secondary Income; Regional Produce; Informants; Hedge Tradition; Mystical Portal (the arch from Arles to Avignon)
Hook: Hermetic Politics; Contested Resource (the salt pond); Weak Aura (its town sites lie in small lacunae)
Tension: other Jerbiton find its magical grip on nobles, resources and hedge wizards distasteful
Tension: its hegemony unsettles even old allies; some fear it means to dominate the Tribunal after the crusade
Tension: it wants the lost Alpine sites and Barbegal reclaimed, and its few strong auras make it hungry for them
Tension: threaten its salt and the politically aloof magi will hit back hard
Hook: it seeks specialists in wards, transport and weather magic, a non-Tremere certamen champion, and teachers for its apprentices
Hook: a magus who founds a chapter under a consul's patronage may petition for membership, or later declare independence
covenants.secrets:
Alazais never seems to vote in council but pulls the strings behind it, steering the covenant to her own ends.
Dama made a Longevity Ritual for Alazais's lover, a folk witch; that bought the Praeco the Coenobium's tacit support, which she means to spend to bury any inquiry into the Presiding Quaesitors' deaths.
The Coenobium drove Elisii Campi from the Alyscamps by spreading rumours of diabolists; many suspect hoplites it sponsored hunted down the survivors at Portus Termini.
It may use its Balthazarine magi as decoys and scapegoats, and it feeds the nobles' stories of the Baux line's descent from Balthazar.
Aucassin's thugs in the boatmen's guild lately humiliated a Redcap carrying a private message to one of its magi; it wants the utricularii taught to cooperate.
Calais of Bonisagus, a valued guest, is trapped in Ventoux's regio and overdue.

covenants.name: Fraxinetum Redux
covenants.summary: A covenant the Tribunal does not know of.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: scattered sources on the small islands of the south coast, the deserted Diedne site of Yf among them
Income: a share of the pirates' raids on the coast and on Catalan and Genoese shipping
Allies: the corsairs of the Hyères and their spies ashore
Boon: Island; Hunters or Sailors; Spies
Hook: Dark Secret (an undeclared covenant of the raiders' heirs); Rival (the Coenobium)
Tension: discovery could bring the Wizard's War their ancestors suffered
covenants.secrets:
The heirs of Fraxinetum, the raider covenant of Sayyid Shajarat al-Darda and his Tytalan lieutenant Nasr ibn Amaf that the Coenobium destroyed in 975, no longer live in the ash forest of the Maures but on the Hyères islands. They still back mundane raids on the coastal towns of Provence and harry Catalan and Genoese shipping, though Ahmad's ships strike only non-Hermetic vessels and rely on well-placed spies to keep clear of the Coenobium's fleet.

Two Moorish magi live at the pirates' main base among the lavender, and a third has a sanctum aboard one of the larger ships of their shady associates; they also harvest vis scattered over the small islands of the coast, the deserted Diedne site at Yf among them. They have never declared themselves at Tribunal for fear their ancestors' shadow would bring a Wizard's War down on them, and will not oppose new covenants unless someone builds another sea stronghold or takes an island off the south coast.

Never declared: the Tribunal does not know it exists, and it has never voted.
Votes: 3 if it ever declared itself, unused.
Founded: the book gives no year; its magi descend from Fraxinetum (889-975).

tribunals.name: The Provençal Tribunal
tribunals.summary:
The Tribunal of the langue d'oc: by the Grand Tribunal's ruling of 1129 it reaches wherever Occitan is spoken, from the Atlantic coast of Gascony across the Toulousain and the Narbonnais to the Rhône and the Alpine edge of Arelat, and from the Massif Central south into the Pyrenees and beyond them into Catalonia. Its magi, just over a hundred of them, lived quietly apart from the world until lately, in the wild south and the mountain strongholds; the gentle, personal bonds of paratge that bind the southern nobility left them freer than their sodales of the feudal north. The Albigensian Crusade has broken that ease: Mistridge, Lariander, Bentalone and Berinor have fallen in eleven years of war, refugees fill the covenants, and the question of what the Order should do about the crusade divides every council.

Three powers dominate. In the west the pagan Mercurians of Aedes Mercurii and the Mithraic, Christian Flambeau of Castra Solis, the domus magna, each claim to be the true heirs of Val-Negra and of Flambeau himself, and despise one another. In the east the many chapters of the Coenobium, Jerbiton and Redcaps under the Chief Redcap Alazais, smother any rival covenant in its shadow and have grown steadily stronger while the crusade wrecked the rest. Old and proud covenants stand apart from both: Tolosa Paratge, now tearing itself apart over its Cathar magi, and Bellaquin, the bankers of Andorra. Mystery cults matter here more than almost anywhere: the Legion of Mithras, the Cult of Mercury, Matres & Matrones, the Knights of the Green Stone and the Gorgiastic Cathars all reach across covenant lines.

Founding a covenant is easy: magi swear a charter together and a Quaesitor notarises it, and no vote is needed. Covenant oaths can be enforced at Tribunal, and a covenant may be spread over many sites or be no more than magi who meet in council now and then. The result is a land littered with the ruins of covenants that failed. Minutes and proclamations are written in Latin and Occitan both.

The Tribunal meets every seven years. By custom the eldest magus is Praeco: now Dama of Merinita, a maga of great age and power who lives apart from her covenant, Castra Solis, in a small tower near Mimizan, favours female magi, and is heeded even by Aedes Mercurii. A Presiding Quaesitor is chosen at the close of each meeting, with two advisers. Each day of a meeting opens with the rite of the Cult of Mercury's flamen, masked and robed, who speaks for the gods and reads the omens; most magi think it a quaint relic and Castra Solis's pious magi a blasphemy, but the office carries quiet influence. Midius of Flambeau, of Aedes Mercurii, holds it now.

The meeting of 1207, at Aedes Mercurii, spent a day on the Church's war on the Cathars and decided nothing; Oxioun of Tytalus argued for keeping out of mundane affairs. Months later the legate was killed and the crusade proclaimed, and the Traditionalist Presiding Quaesitor Protantus died; Senex held the office by 1210. The meeting of 1214, moved from besieged Toulouse to Castra Solis to the Mercurians' disgust, was the most bitter since the Schism War: charges of mundane interference flew, Normandy magi were accused of meddling and Tytalus of starting the crusade, Tolomae of Jerbiton was put out of the debate for demanding open magical war on the crusaders, and Aedes Mercurii's threat to walk out, which would have left the meeting without a quorum, was headed off only by Tibaut, then acting Presiding Quaesitor, and by the Chief Redcap's threat to suspend all Redcap service. Tres Ex Miscellanea was narrowly acquitted over the destruction of Mistridge.

The next meeting is in summer 1221, at the ruins of Glanum near St-Rémy, chosen by agreement as neutral ground. Its first business is the Presiding Quaesitor: Tibaut died last year, and his filia Beatrice of Guernicus, nominally of Castra Solis but living at Glanum on the edge of the Coenobium's lands, has acted in his place at the Praeco's suggestion. She is presumed to succeed him, but she is young and without standing among the factions, and the choice may be contested. After that the crusade will fill the meeting: the Hermetic faidits want licence to defend themselves and reclaim what they lost, and look to Garus and the milites of Castra Solis; the conservatives led by Aedes Mercurii, with Ara Maxima Nova, Stella Durus and Miniata Sophia, want to keep out of it, and if the Tribunal intervenes they may boycott the meeting of 1227 and ask the Grand Tribunal of 1228 for a Tribunal of their own. Many senior magi are uneasy at the Coenobium's growing reach, and Tolosa Paratge's war may be raised if anyone brings a case.

Votes at the meeting of 1221:
- The Coenobium Rhodanien: about 20
- Aedes Mercurii: 18
- Castra Solis: 17, to which the Praeco's and the Presiding Quaesitor's votes are added
- Tolosa Paratge: 9, split between its Black and White factions
- Ostal des Exiles: 6, although the Tribunal has not yet recognised it
- Bellaquin: 5
- Stella Durus: 5
- Ara Maxima Nova: 4
- Miniata Sophia: 4
- Tres' Band: 3, never cast: the band shuns Tribunal

Stories. The crusade is the background to everything: the Order is split over how to answer it, and the meeting at Glanum in 1221 will argue little else. Beside it run the Six Deadly Spirits in Gascony and the Narbonnais, the followers of the Procrustean League hiding among the faidits, Tolosa Paratge's war with itself and the Coenobium's growing reach. Two stories wait for the storyguide to begin them: the lost covenant of Val-Negra and what its Iron Door holds, and the Pyrenean covenants' threat to seek a Tribunal of their own at the Grand Tribunal of 1228. A smaller hook: Tres' Band, roving in the forests near Bazas, watches how each new covenant treats the common folk, and turns from indifference to hatred against magi who set themselves up as lords.
tribunals.history:
The Roman Provincia. In antiquity the Aquitanians, a Basque people, held what is now Gascony, and Greek traders from Massalia founded Marseilles and Trinquetaille and traded up the rivers with the Celts of Arelat. Rome came in 125 BC and split its Provincia into Novempopulania facing the Atlantic and Narbonensis facing the Mediterranean, and both prospered for five centuries. The one great revolt came in 106 BC, when a governor drained the sacred lake of the Tolosates to take the gold sunk in it; with the Cimbri's help the rebels beat Rome at Arausio in 105 BC, and the treasure was lost and never found.

The coming of Christianity. Tradition says Mary Magdalene and the Virgin landed at Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, and Lazarus became the first bishop of Marseilles. The land kept to the Roman gods until Bishop Sernin of Toulouse was dragged to death behind a bull in 257; his martyrdom broke the Cult of Mercury in the city, which became a centre of the new faith.

Visigothic Septimania. Rome withdrew in 419 and the Visigoths, Arian allies of the empire, settled Narbonensis by treaty in 462, gave up its lands east of the Rhône in 475 for full independence, and took Arles in 472. Their kingdom, named Septimania for its seven cities, ruled from Toulouse until Clovis beat them at Vouillé in 507. The Ostrogoths checked the Franks, and Visigothic kings held the Narbonnais until the 720s. Converted to the mainstream faith by the mid-sixth century, the Goths still kept old customs, and the last Roman flamens of the Cult of Mercury kept secrets that Priamitus and Apromor would later seek.

Franks and Moors. Under the Merovingian Franks a dark age of usurpation, plague and famine fell on the land; Roman cities in Arelat emptied, marshes swallowed old fields, and the lords of Toulouse made themselves dukes all but free of the crown. The Moors took Narbonne in 719 and marched on Toulouse, where Duke Odo of Gascony and Toulouse beat them in 721, buying time for Charles Martel's victory at Tours in 732. The Franks took Septimania in 759 and the Pyrenees by the century's end, but their southern dukes rebelled again and again.

Charlemagne. Charlemagne crushed the southern lords in 770 on his way to Spain. In 778 he besieged the Moor Mirat at Lourdes, who surrendered and was baptised, and on the way home from Spain his rearguard was cut down at the pass of Roncevaux. The deaths of Roland and Bishop Turpin are the troubadours' most beloved tale.

The counts of Toulouse. By the ninth century Toulouse's counts had again slipped free of the distant Frankish throne, reaching their height under Raimond IV, count of St Gilles and marquis of Arelat (1093 to 1105), when Occitan letters and the troubadours flowered. The counts feuded with Foix and with the Trencavel of Carcassonne and Béziers, clashed with the bishops who share justice in Toulouse and with the rising capitouls, and bought popular support with privileges, so that the county is full of knights and ladies holding their own castles. Notaries, heirs of Roman law, appeared in the Narbonnais in the 1140s alongside the consular towns.

Heresy. Cathar belief took root in the tenth century and by 1220 rivals the Church in the south. Bernard of Clairvaux preached against it for one summer in 1145, with success in Albi and Toulouse and scorn in the countryside. The Council of Tours condemned the heretics and those who sheltered them in 1163; churchmen found them heretical at Lombers in 1165 but let them go, and by 1167 they had bishops of their own. The Third Lateran Council called for arms against them in 1179, a legate's army besieged Lavaur in 1181 to little effect, and two legates sent in 1203 found the southern bishops corrupt and immovable. Arnaud Amaury was made legate and Foulques bishop of Toulouse, a see so low he dared not live in it. Dominic of Guzman walked barefoot among the heretics from 1206 to 1208, winning more love than converts.
tribunals.meeting_place: The ruins of Glanum, near St-Rémy (Arelat)

cases.title: The Presiding Quaesitor
cases.charge: Tibaut of Guernicus died in 1219 (some accounts say 1214). His filia Beatrice of Guernicus has acted as Presiding Quaesitor since, at the Praeco's suggestion, and is presumed to take the office; but she is young, has no standing with the factions, has fallen out with Primus Garus, and would hand the office to a better candidate of her House if one appeared. Confirming or replacing her is the first business of the meeting.

cases.title: The deaths of Senex and Tibaut
cases.charge: Presiding Quaesitor Senex vanished in 1210, last seen going into a village to look into something, and was declared lost when he missed the meeting of 1214. Tibaut, who found in Senex's notes that he had been investigating a mystery cult, believed him dead and was himself looking into the Tribunal's cults when he died on the road near Foix. Beatrice suspects foul play but has no proof.
cases.evidence:
Senex's laboratory notes on an unnamed cult
Tibaut's suspicions, shared with Beatrice
Tibaut missed his meeting with Beatrice
Luc of Ara Maxima Nova fought Tibaut in certamen over his questions about the Via Domitia

cases.title: Recognition of the Ostal des Exiles
cases.charge: The House of Exiles, founded since 1214 under Castle d'Aguilar by survivors of Mistridge, Lariander and other fallen covenants, asks to be recognised as a covenant of the Tribunal, with its six votes.

cases.title: The faidits' petition
cases.brought_by: The Hermetic faidits (Ostal des Exiles and refugees)
cases.charge: The magi who lost their covenants to de Montfort's armies ask for licence to defend themselves against the crusaders and to win back their magical power, and want Garus and the milites of Castra Solis behind them, even with open magic. The Mercurian conservatives oppose any intervention in mundane affairs.

cases.title: A Tribunal of the Pyrenees
cases.brought_by: Aedes Mercurii and the conservative covenants
cases.charge: If the Tribunal intervenes against the crusade and the Church, Aedes Mercurii, Ara Maxima Nova, Stella Durus and Miniata Sophia may boycott the meeting of 1227 and, being the four covenants a Tribunal needs, ask the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to make them a Tribunal of their own. Bellaquin dreams of a Catalan Tribunal instead.

cases.title: Tolosa Paratge's civil war
cases.against: The Black and White factions of Tolosa Paratge
cases.charge: Since Marc killed Augustus in Wizard's War in 1218 and St. Tropez killed Marc, the covenant has split: the pro-Cathar Blacks hold the regio, the Whites wait in the city to retake it. Both sides are plainly depriving each other of magical resources, but the Quaesitores have not acted, out of respect for the covenant and because no one has brought a case. The Whites may appeal to the Tribunal in 1221.

cases.title: The Procrustean League's followers
cases.charge: After Tolomae was Marched in 1218, several of his rumoured supporters fled to other covenants or vanished among the faidits of the langue d'oc. Some magi fear his cause will return, embittered by the war.

cases.title: Marie of Merinita and the northern border
cases.charge: Marie keeps a manor at Poitiers, in lands usually held to be Normandy's, as a chapter of Castra Solis, attends Tribunal in Provence, and works to push the Tribunal's border north by spreading southern language and culture through Aquitaine, so that the 1129 rule of the Occitan tongue would carry the land with it.

cases.title: An undeclared covenant in the Hyères
cases.brought_by: (no one: the Tribunal does not know of it)
cases.charge: Secret. Ahmad ibn Nasr of Tytalus and two Moorish magi keep an undeclared covenant among the Hyères islands, backing raids on the coast and harvesting vis on the islands, afraid that Fraxinetum's memory would bring a Wizard's War on them if they declared it. Aucassin of Tytalus lives as an eremite at Beaucaire under a false name. A case can only be brought once someone finds them out.

rulings.title: Founding a covenant
rulings.says: A covenant comes into being when its magi agree on a common aim, write a charter setting out their oath, and swear it together; the swearing is what counts. The one legal step is to have a Quaesitor notarise the charter, which makes it enforceable under the Code, and some groups put this off. No vote or approval of the Tribunal is needed, though it is polite to tell the nearest Mercer House and to send someone to the next meeting to announce the new covenant. A settlement never notarised (Glanum I and II, Portus Termini) was never a recognised covenant. The Provence package records this as its Open founding custom.

rulings.title: Covenant oaths enforceable
rulings.says: A covenant's oath is part of the Peripheral Code here, and a Tribunal can rule on it. As a result many small quarrels within a council, settled elsewhere by certamen or among the members, are brought before the whole Tribunal.

rulings.title: Covenants on many sites
rulings.says: A covenant need not live in one place. Its members may keep separate homes and meet in council only when needed: Castra Solis counts the Praeco at Mimizan and Marie of Merinita at Poitiers as members, and the Coenobium is a chain of chapters along the Rhône and the coast.

rulings.title: Residency
rulings.says: A magus is resident who attended one of the last three meetings, or is voted resident at the first he attends. A magus Gauntleted in the Tribunal is resident until he has missed three meetings in a row. Residency lasts until the magus claims it in another Tribunal or attends and votes at another Tribunal's meeting.

rulings.title: Registering arrivals and departures
rulings.says: Magi who settle in the Tribunal between meetings register either with both the Redcaps and the Praeco, or with their nearest neighbouring covenant, a Redcap guiding them there if they do not know the way. A magus who takes residency elsewhere must first register his leaving with the Provençal Redcaps or the Praeco, before voting at another Tribunal, or he breaks the Peripheral Code.

rulings.title: The border of the Occitan tongue
rulings.says: After quarrels with Normandy over the newly enlarged Tribunal, the Grand Tribunal fixed the border as running wherever the people speak Occitan. Disliked at first, the rule is now embraced as the ground of the Tribunal's claims to vis and other resources, and the Tribunal writes its minutes, proclamations and many other documents in Occitan as well as Latin.

rulings.title: The Praeco
rulings.says: By custom the eldest magus of the Tribunal presides as Praeco.

rulings.title: The Presiding Quaesitor
rulings.says: The Presiding Quaesitor, who runs the meeting, is appointed at the close of each meeting together with two advisers. When the office falls vacant between meetings an acting Presiding Quaesitor serves until the next meeting confirms or replaces him, as Tibaut did for Senex and Beatrice does for Tibaut.

rulings.title: The flamen of Mercury
rulings.says: By ancient tradition a priest of the Cult of Mercury, in mask and robes of office, opens every day of a meeting with a rite, speaking for the gods and reading omens in the Tribunal's ceremonies. The rite goes unchallenged for its age, though few take it seriously.

rulings.title: Val-Negra must not rise again
rulings.says: After the fall of Val-Negra in the Schism War, and the panic over what was found sealed there, the Quaesitores decided in secret that the covenant must never be refounded, and House Flambeau made Castra Solis its domus magna instead. Few magi know the reason, and even the site is now lost.

rulings.title: Fraxinetum's destruction
rulings.says: The magi of the eastern Tribunal who banded together against Fraxinetum's Moorish raiders worked through William I of Provence's army rather than a declared Wizard's War, and narrowly escaped the Quaesitores' censure for destroying a covenant that way. The league they formed became the Coenobium.

rulings.title: Bellaquin and mundane lordship
rulings.says: Twice jealous neighbours charged Bellaquin with breaking its oath by its deep entanglement in feudal affairs; twice the Tribunal found it had brought no ruin on its accusers or the Order. The precedent: even heavy mundane involvement is tolerated so long as it causes no ruin to magi.

rulings.title: No ruling on the Cathars
rulings.says: The meeting at Aedes Mercurii debated the Church's campaign against the Cathars for a whole day and made no decision; the Mercurians' counsel of staying out of mundane affairs prevailed by default. No case has yet been brought against an avowedly Cathar magus.

rulings.title: Grogs in a Wizard's War
rulings.says: Tres Ex Miscellanea armed a company of mercenaries with magical weapons, called them his grogs, and used them and his magical siege engines to level Mistridge's tower. As his Wizard's War had been properly declared, and nothing in the Code forbids using grogs to wage one, the Tribunal acquitted him by a narrow vote. He then went into hiding from Mistridge's friends.

rulings.title: The March of Tolomae
rulings.says: Tolomae, once of the Coenobium and Bellaquin, led the Procrustean League in calling for open war on the Church. Renounced by the Mercurians and the Coenobium, he was cast out of House Jerbiton as orbus in 1216, fled rather than answer a Quaesitor's questions over the murder of the legate Pierre de Castelnau, and early in 1218 was Marched for repeated interference with mundanes and slain.

rulings.title: Glanum held neutral
rulings.says: The ruins of Glanum, agreed as the compromise site for the meeting of 1221, may not be formally resettled until that question is settled. Only Beatrice of Guernicus lives there, as the Coenobium's guest.

rulings.title: The Coenobium's toll and code of hospitality
rulings.says: A local custom of the Coenobium's towns, not a Tribunal ruling, but one every visitor meets. Magi openly visiting Avignon announce themselves and how long they will stay, and are asked to give a silver florin holding a pawn of vis, which pays for the covenant's non-Jerbiton specialists. In return they get food, lodging, laboratory space and a consul as patron, who answers for their conduct and protects them.
