The guest's part: give notice of the visit by Redcap if possible, bring the florin, state the purpose and length of the stay and say when leaving, behave with restraint and help the patron if asked, and go at once if told to. Magi who refuse are thought crass, watched, and quietly obstructed, even with charges at Tribunal. The Coenobium keeps its members' Latin names, and has let no new covenant thrive in southern Provence for over a century unless it joined as a chapter.

diary.title: Regional Tribunals created
diary.details: As the Order grows, the Second Grand Tribunal sets up regional Tribunals, made of covenants that lie near one another rather than of lands with fixed borders. The rules for founding and governing them come out of a quarrel over Val-Negra's charter: Flambeau wanted lordship over every covenant his home helped to found.

diary.title: Val-Negra recognized
diary.details: After years of argument between Flambeau and Guernicus over its charter, the covenant of Val-Negra in the Pyrenees is formally recognized, and a regional Tribunal forms around it. Flambeau is the only Founder to make his home there, though Trianoma and Mercere visit often. Tolosa Paratge, a large Diedne covenant in a lake regio at Toulouse, is one of the four first covenants of the new Tribunal, and most of the region's other covenants belong to House Diedne.

diary.title: Gelon becomes Primus of Verditius
diary.details: Gelon, the first apprentice of Verditius, becomes Primus of his House. He lives for decades at Val-Negra, forging his famous enchanted swords, and his followers go on to found the Confraternity of Roland.

diary.title: Kaeso joins House Flambeau
diary.details: The Christian wizard Kaeso, whose power rests on an old underground temple of Mithras by the Garonne, joins House Flambeau. Training under Apromor and Flambeau in the Pyrenees, he forms the Hoplites, soldier-magi who hurl Pilum of Fire from behind a strong Parma Magica, and leads many of them into the Legion of Mithras. Many count him the first Hoplite.

diary.title: Apromor becomes Primus of Flambeau
diary.details: Apromor, the Founder's first apprentice, who has drifted from his master's ways, becomes the first Primus of House Flambeau, and Kaeso's Hoplites carry on Flambeau's war against the sahirs of Iberia. Apromor welcomes pagan and non-Hermetic wizards into the Order, works with Priamitus of Mercere to revive the Cult of Mercury from the last Roman priests of the region, and spreads Val-Negra's outposts across the Pyrenees.

diary.title: Portus Cottiae and Yf founded
diary.details: Julius Donnus, an outcast Mercurian of House Flambeau from the Greater Alps, founds Portus Cottiae outside Briançon as a second home for the revived Cult of Mercury, after Harco. It becomes the first Mercer House of the region and grows into a covenant of several sites, with chapter houses at Gap, Chorges and Embrun and a post at Oulx guarding the passes. In the same year Diedne magi found Yf on an island off the coast of Arelat.

diary.title: Lapurdum founded
diary.details: Flambeau magi found Lapurdum where the Adour meets the sea in Gascony, around a mithraeum in what was once a Roman army camp.

diary.title: Campus Elysii founded
diary.details: A small group of spirit masters, necromancers of Ex Miscellanea, settles in the crypts of the Alyscamps at Arles as the covenant of Campus Elysii.

diary.title: Vikings on the Garonne
diary.details: King Pepin II of Aquitaine, seeking freedom from Charles the Bald, is accused of apostasy for letting the Viking Jarl Oscar sail his raiders up the Garonne to Toulouse. Northmen camp all along the western coast, and Marseilles has already been sacked by Arab pirates (838); Byzantine freebooters (849) and Normans based in the Camargue follow. Tales of rune-wizards among the raiders finally draw the magi in, and Flambeau comes to resent how little the Diedne do to help.

diary.title: Castra Solis founded
diary.details: Raids on Gascon villages have grown since 840, and the Flambeau wrongly believe an organized Order of Odin is behind them. Kaeso returns to Bordeaux and fortifies his temple as a covenant, Castra Solis, the encampment of the sun, under the sign of a quartered sun.

diary.title: Bordeaux falls to the Northmen
diary.details: Before the Hoplites can do more than raise hasty defences, the northern pagans take Bordeaux. Unwilling to harm the townsfolk, the magi spend five years trying to end the war by force against the rune-wizards alone, and many die in their traps, Kaeso among them.

diary.title: Sinapis founded
diary.details: With Bordeaux too near the front, the surviving Flambeau build a fortified covenant, Sinapis, further north in Anjou. Castra Solis becomes a camp of tents for quick strikes, and to outsiders it looks like an offshoot of Sinapis.

diary.title: Lapurdum abandoned
diary.details: Worn down by Viking raids and quarrels among its magi, Lapurdum is given up. Its ruins lie somewhere under the city of Bayonne.

diary.title: Seven Tribunals defined
diary.details: The Grand Tribunal draws up seven regional Tribunals. Val-Negra goes to the Iberian Tribunal, along with the mountains and the Basque lands north of them; the bulk of France goes to the West Franks, and a strip from Friesland through Burgundy to Arelat forms the Lotharingian Tribunal.

diary.title: Fraxinetum founded
diary.details: Two Tytalan war-magi, Sayyid Shajarat al-Darda (who called himself a Flambeau, though the House denies him) and his lieutenant Nasr ibn Amaf, settle in the Massif des Maures above St Tropez with a band of Andalusian raiders. Their covenant, named for the ash groves Sayyid planted, stays hidden from the Tribunal for its first century while it backs Moorish attacks on Provençal towns.

diary.title: Barbegal founded
diary.details: Three Verditius mage-smiths found a covenant in the Roman watermill complex of Barbegal, just north of Arles.

diary.title: Lotharingia divided
diary.details: The Grand Tribunal hands the northern covenants of the Lotharingian Tribunal to Normandy or the Rhine. What is left, the Kingdom of Arles along the Rhône and a few covenants in the Toulousain (a Mercer House at Arles, a strong Diedne covenant at Lyon, and a handful of others), comes to be called the Provençal Tribunal.

diary.title: The Birds of Camargue founded
diary.details: Bjornaer magi found a covenant in the marshes at the mouth of the Rhône.

diary.title: Portus Cottiae overrun
diary.details: Berber mountaineers overrun the scattered sites of Portus Cottiae, one of the first Lotharingian covenants to fall to the Saracens. Its magi flee down the Durance; at the motherhouse near Briançon the defenders bring the mountain down on the raiders and bury themselves in their own sancta. The one surviving maga, Anaïs of Jerbiton, reaches Avignon and becomes a loud voice for the Hermetic league that becomes the Coenobium.

diary.title: Yf falls
diary.details: The Diedne covenant of Yf falls to the raids of Fraxinetum. One of its magae later joins the Coenobium to avenge it, but her line dies out shortly before the Schism War.

diary.title: Barbegal abandoned
diary.details: The undefended mills of Barbegal are abandoned under Saracen raiding. The surviving smiths help to found the Rhône covenant of Coenobium Rhodanien.

diary.title: Askelarre founded
diary.details: A coven of Hermetic sorginak, Basque witches spread across the Basque country, founds the covenant of Askelarre.

diary.title: Sorginak join Ex Miscellanea; Donjon Leyre founded
diary.details: A few sorginak at last join House Ex Miscellanea, resented by their hedge sisters and anxious to keep their distance from the Diedne, who had long taken sorginak into their own House. In the same year Donjon Leyre, an early vassal of Montverte, is founded at the fork of the Leyre in the Landes as a base for raids into the Basque Pyrenees.

diary.title: The Birds of Camargue merge into the Coenobium
diary.details: Threatened by Fraxinetum, the Bjornaer of the Birds of Camargue join the wider league of Rhône magi that becomes the Coenobium Rhodanien.

diary.title: Maieul of Cluny captured
diary.details: The Moors of the Massif des Maures capture and ransom Maieul, abbot of Cluny, and push into the foothills of the Alps. The alarm this raises moves the mostly Jerbiton magi of eastern Provence to band together in a pact of mutual defence. Working through their families, churchmen and noble allies, they quietly back the army of William I of Provence, which routs the Moors at Tourtour.

diary.title: Fraxinetum destroyed
diary.details:
William's army takes the Moorish base and the Fraxinetum magi vanish into the forest. The history chapter says the Coenobium Rhodanien, which it calls newly formed (the Birds of Camargue had joined it in 970), destroyed the covenant by Wizard's War; the Arelat chapter says no war was ever openly declared and the league narrowly escaped the Quaesitors' anger for acting through mundane arms. Either way, the victors stay together as a covenant of many sites along the Rhône and the coast. In the same year Anaïs of Toulouse, a renegade Criamon expelled from her House, brings her followers, the Gorgiastic Cathars, into House Ex Miscellanea.

Secrets
The Fraxinetum magi did not perish. Their heirs live on in secret as Fraxinetum Redux on the Hyères islands, never declared to the Tribunal.

diary.title: Grand Tribunal: the Northmen driven out
diary.details: At the Grand Tribunal the Hoplites declare the rune-wizards rooted out of the region after more than a century of war: all three Danish settlements on the coast have been burned. Many of their fortified outposts, such as the tower at Mimizan, later grow into covenants counted as offshoots of Castra Solis. The Diedne, uneasy with the Mithraic piety of the Hoplites, took no part, which deepens Flambeau's suspicion of them.

diary.title: Donjon Leyre falls
diary.details: All the founding magi of Donjon Leyre die fighting in the Schism War, which rages through Gascony as Val-Negra's forces storm the Diedne covenants one after another; many Gascon Diedne burn their own sites and flee.

diary.title: Campus Elysii driven out
diary.details:
The spirit masters of Campus Elysii, who hid underground through the war, are forced out of the Alyscamps when the Coenobium stirs up the townsfolk with tales of diabolists under the necropolis. They try to begin again in a cave network in the Verdon gorge as Portus Termini, but all contact is lost before the next Tribunal and the new covenant is never registered.

Secrets
Many suspect that Hoplites in the Coenobium's pay hunted down the survivors.

diary.title: Askelarre destroyed
diary.details: The sorginak covenant of Askelarre is destroyed in the Schism War. Two of Val-Negra's magi, the Flambeau Leo Augustus and the Tremere Vegetius, die in the attack.

diary.title: The fall of Val-Negra
diary.details:
As the Schism War draws to its close, while its zealous magi are away striking at the Diedne, five Diedne archmagi storm Val-Negra. Of twenty-five magi at the war's start, only four are left. Shortly before the war many of its Flambeau had left, after a vision, to found Aedes Mercurii in Val-Negra's outlying halls; now the survivors join it, and it declares itself a Provençal covenant and the heir of Val-Negra. Many other covenants change to the Provençal Tribunal at this time, partly to keep Tytalus from claiming the spoils of the fallen Diedne. The domus magna of Flambeau moves to Castra Solis, and the Quaesitors strike nine or more Diedne sites from the records. Why Val-Negra was never rebuilt, and even where it stood, is soon forgotten.

Secrets
The Diedne reached the Iron Door in the depths of Val-Negra, and in the fighting the Adulteration of Flambeau was loosed. It killed three defenders and all the attackers before the last two archmagi forced it back and sealed the door with a Hermetic ward, one that breaks if the door is simply opened. The Quaesitors kept it quiet and ruled that Val-Negra must never rise again.

diary.title: Bellaquin founded
diary.details: As the Schism War dies down, Flambeau magi restore an abandoned castle, the Château de Penne in Tarn above the Aveyron, as a stronghold. The war ends before it is needed, and they hand it to House Jerbiton, who make it one of the most admired covenants in the Order and, in time, the lords of a fief of their own.

diary.title: Mistridge founded
diary.details: A covenant is founded in the Val du Bosque, in a tower raised by magic at the brink of a sheer drop.

diary.title: Windgraven founded
diary.details: Necromancers found Windgraven in the squat stone towers of a ruined Visigothic fort on a rocky plateau in the southern part of the County of Toulouse.

diary.title: Filii Sinapis founded
diary.details: Flambeau magi from the abandoned Normandy covenant of Sinapis found Filii Sinapis.

diary.title: Berinor founded
diary.details: Jerbiton magi found Berinor, a small covenant in the County of Toulouse that becomes a patron of troubadours and trobairitz.

diary.title: Gascony joins the Provençal Tribunal
diary.details: When the Normandy Tribunal splits, Castra Solis leads a faction into the enlarged Provençal Tribunal. The magi of Sinapis leave their site to join the domus magna, and smaller covenants of the area, Mimizan among them, come too.

diary.title: Bentalone founded
diary.details: A covenant is founded in a castle in the Toulousain; it stays in Summer for a century.

diary.title: Grand Tribunal: the Occitan border
diary.details: To settle quarrels between Normandy and the newly enlarged Provençal Tribunal, the Grand Tribunal rules that the border between them runs wherever Occitan stops being spoken. Unpopular at first, the rule is soon embraced by the southern magi to secure their claims to vis, and the Tribunal's minutes and proclamations are written in both Latin and Occitan.

diary.title: The Golden Court at Beaucaire
diary.details:
Count Henry II of Provence holds a festival in the meadows north of Beaucaire to mark the reconciliation of the Duke of Narbonne and the King of Aragon. A chronicler praises its hundred thousand knights, its gold sown in the earth and its herds roasted over wax torches.

Secrets
Most of the knights were faeries revelling in the troubadours' spirit of foolishness, and the gold was glamour; the meadow still holds Faerie vis.

diary.title: Saint Jean Pied-de-Port razed
diary.details: When Richard the Lionheart sacks Saint Jean Pied-de-Port, the large outpost Aedes Mercurii kept there is lost; its covenfolk had already fallen under the townsfolk's suspicion of witchcraft.

diary.title: Miniata Sophia founded
diary.details: A Criamon eremite founds Miniata Sophia in the cave system of Niaux, about forty years before 1220. For a decade and more it keeps to itself.

diary.title: Lariander founded
diary.details: Tremere magi found Lariander, a young covenant in a faerie wood near the village of Montgey in the Toulousain.

diary.title: Tribunal: Miniata Sophia announced
diary.details: Miniata Sophia makes itself known at the Tribunal and registers its site, the village of Niaux, with the Redcaps. It has attended every meeting since, voting on each question as seems most apt or abstaining, and making no alliances.

diary.title: Ara Maxima Nova founded
diary.details: Merinita magi who have explored the labours of Heracles in the east come west to follow the rest of his journey and found Ara Maxima Nova among the vineyards outside Perpignan, close to the Via Domitia. Their charter binds them to seek the Hesperides every five years.

diary.title: Windgraven destroyed
diary.details: Magi of Mistridge destroy Windgraven in a properly declared Wizard's War, battering its towers flat with giant stones conjured by magic. Few mourn its necromancers, who were widely thought diabolists, and the war foreshadows Mistridge's own end.

diary.title: Bellaquin falls
diary.details:
Overstretched by its feudal ties, Bellaquin tries to help two warring lords at once and is accused by both of stirring up their war. With churchmen urging them on, and a companion betraying the covenant, they storm the Château de Penne by surprise and kill several magi. The survivors, warned to prepare by archmagi, take their hidden reserves, destroy what they cannot carry and leave the site to their mundane proxies. Since the harm fell only on Bellaquin, no charges are brought.

Secrets
Some suspect other magi had a hand in arranging the mundane attack.

diary.title: Bellaquin moves to Andorra
diary.details: Bellaquin settles in a house in the parish of Ordino in Andorra, keeping its charter but changing its ways: subtler, richer and turned toward banking.

diary.title: Bentalone overrun
diary.details: The book's list of fallen covenants ends Bentalone in 1207: Simon de Montfort's army takes its castle for a Cathar stronghold and storms it in a surprise attack, though his campaigns in the south only begin in 1209.

diary.title: Raimond VI excommunicated
diary.details: In May Count Raimond VI of Toulouse is excommunicated for sheltering heretics. He promises the pope to drive them out, and the sentence is lifted in August.

diary.title: Tribunal at Aedes Mercurii
diary.details: The Tribunal meets at Aedes Mercurii and spends a whole day on the Church's drive against the Cathars, without deciding anything. Oxioun of Tytalus, leader of the host covenant, urges the Order to stay out of mundane affairs, and the Mercurian bloc is content to wait in its mountains, despite the worries of the lowland covenants of the Toulousain, the Narbonnais and the Rhône.

diary.title: Protantus dies; Tibaut chief Quaesitor
diary.details: A few months after the 1207 Tribunal, Protantus, the Traditionalist chief Quaesitor, dies and is followed by the more flexible Tibaut, a Transitionalist with no ties to the Mercurians. Few magi remark the coincidence with the legate's death, but it marks a turning point. The history chapter tells it so; the Gascony chapter names Senex as chief Quaesitor until 1210, with Tibaut acting in his place only from 1214.

diary.title: Interdict in Gascony
diary.details:
Innocent III lays all of King John's lands under interdict. Many Gascon churches close their doors and say no Mass for six years.

Secrets
During the interdict a band of demons, the Six Deadly Spirits, settles in the wild lands of Gascony away from the pilgrim roads, and some linger there still.

diary.title: The legate murdered
diary.details: In January Raimond meets the papal legates at St Gilles, stalls, and threatens them in anger as they leave. At dawn, waiting for the ferry to Arles, the legate Pierre de Castelnau is run through by a knight, forgiving his killer as he dies. Innocent III blames the count and proclaims a crusade; Arnaud Amaury and Bishop Foulques preach it, promising the crusaders a share of heretic lands and release from their debts to Jewish lenders.

diary.title: Raimond joins the crusade
diary.details: As the crusaders muster at Lyon, Raimond is scourged barefoot before a crowd at St Gilles and accepts hard terms. In June he takes the cross himself, robbing the crusade of its main target, which turns on the Trencavel lands instead. Raimond-Roger Trencavel is refused leave to join.

diary.title: The sack of Béziers
diary.details: Béziers refuses to hand over two hundred heretics. When its young men sally against the crusade's camp followers, the rabble surges through the open gate and the knights follow. Asked how to tell the faithful from the heretics, Arnaud Amaury is said to have answered that God would know His own. Fifteen to thirty thousand die, many in the churches.

diary.title: Carcassonne surrenders
diary.details: In August Viscount Raimond-Roger Trencavel leaves Carcassonne to parley and is seized and imprisoned. The city yields; its people are spared but its treasures plundered. Why so strong a city gave in so soon remains a mystery.

diary.title: Simon de Montfort leads the crusade
diary.details: When the great lords go home after their forty days, the legate's council chooses Simon de Montfort, a minor knight of the Île de France, to lead. With his wife Alice, thirty knights and five hundred foot he holds Carcassonne and takes the Trencavel titles of Béziers and Carcassonne, but Pedro II of Aragon will not take his homage. Revolts follow, the abbot of St Gilles is murdered, and de Montfort answers with the atrocity at Bram. In Toulouse Bishop Foulques forms his White Brotherhood against heretics, Jews and moneylenders, and a Black Brotherhood rises against it.

diary.title: Mistridge destroyed
diary.details: The Rusticani magus Tres declares Wizard's War on every magus of Mistridge. With two other magi of his tradition and a company of mercenaries armed with his enchanted weapons, he levels the tower with magical siege engines and kills its defenders. Some say he avenged Windgraven; others that Mistridge had scorned him as a hedge wizard.

diary.title: Minerve and Termes fall
diary.details: When the castle of Aguilar holds out, de Montfort turns to besiege Minerve, where a hundred and thirty-seven Cathars are burned and only three women recant. Termes and more castles follow, making him master of the Trencavel lands. So few heretics have died that the war is plainly one of conquest.

diary.title: Berinor falls; Senex vanishes
diary.details:
Berinor falls when de Montfort's men dispossess the lord who held its castle, and its survivors take refuge at Tolosa Paratge. The same year Senex of Guernicus, the chief Quaesitor, goes into a village to look into something and is never seen again.

Secrets
Senex had begun to look into Dama's cult of the Matres and Matrones. While she was away at an akelarre he slipped into her sanctum at Mimizan; she came back early and caught him there. Her Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus and Maju's venom killed him, Maju devoured the body as a drake, and Dama told no one. In law he had forfeited his immunity by entering her sanctum.

diary.title: Lavaur, and the first siege of Toulouse
diary.details: Pedro II at last accepts de Montfort's homage and tries to broker peace, but the legates' terms are too harsh and the south rises. Lavaur is sacked, sixty Cathars taken at Les Casses are burned, and de Montfort besieges Toulouse. Bishop Foulques tells the faithful to give up the city and their count or share the heretics' fate; they drive him out instead, and the siege fails.

diary.title: Montgey and the fall of Lariander
diary.details:
Peasants and southern knights massacre some three hundred German crusaders marching through a faerie forest near Montgey to Lavaur. In reprisal the crusaders destroy the village, burn the woods and slaughter the Tremere of Lariander, taking their black robes for those of Cathar perfecti. Garsenda of Lariander believes she is the only survivor.

Secrets
Garsenda had stirred the villagers to the ambush, and the white ladies and walking trees the survivors spoke of were real.

diary.title: Battle of St Martin-Lalande
diary.details: Raimond gathers his army against de Montfort's small force, but the crusaders keep raiding and seizing the initiative, and when the southerners finally attack they are routed in open battle.

diary.title: The Children's Crusade; Las Navas de Tolosa
diary.details: Thousands of children and peasants follow a young visionary from the Rhineland through France to Marseilles, sure the sea will open for them. It does not; many board ships for Africa and vanish, feared sold as slaves. In Iberia the Christian kings win the great victory of Las Navas de Tolosa.

diary.title: Battle of Muret
diary.details: Pedro II of Aragon, Raimond and the count of Foix take Muret, ten miles up the Garonne from Toulouse, with a great army. De Montfort crosses the marshes to fall on their flank: Pedro is killed and some ten thousand die in under half an hour, many drowning in the river, where their cries are still heard in flood. Resistance is broken for years, and Raimond seeks redress in Rome.

diary.title: Tribunal at Castra Solis
diary.details: The meeting set for Toulouse moves to Castra Solis, with de Montfort's army outside the city, to the Mercurians' annoyance. It is the most bitter gathering since the Schism War, taken up with the crusade and charges of meddling with mundanes: some blame Normandy magi, some Flambeau blame Tytalus for the crusade itself. Tolomae of Jerbiton calls for open Hermetic resistance and is thrown out of the debate, swearing revenge on the Mercurians and on the Coenobium. Aedes Mercurii threatens to walk out and so void the Tribunal, until Tibaut and the chief Redcap Alazais, who threatens to stop all Redcap service, avert anarchy. Senex is absent, and Tibaut acts as chief Quaesitor.

diary.title: Ruling: Tres acquitted
diary.details: Charges are brought against Tres for arming mercenaries with enchanted weapons, calling them his grogs, and using them to destroy Mistridge. However deplored, it was a lawfully declared Wizard's War and no ruling forbids grogs in one; the vote goes narrowly his way. Tres flees into hiding from Mistridge's friends, and after the meeting the Hermetic faidits begin to gather at Aguilar as the Ostal des Exiles, Rixenda of Mistridge first and Gilbert of Flambeau their leader.

diary.title: De Montfort enters Toulouse; Filii Sinapis abandoned
diary.details: Simon de Montfort enters Toulouse in triumph and takes up residence in the Château Narbonnais. The Waldensians are condemned as heretics, though Innocent III thought them good Christians. Filii Sinapis is abandoned in the wake of the crusade.

diary.title: Tolomae declared orbus; Tibaut confirmed
diary.details: House Jerbiton expels Tolomae of Bellaquin, leader of the Procrustean League, which calls for open war on the Church, and declares him orbus. He is suspected of the legate's murder and flees rather than answer the Quaesitor's questions. With Senex absent two years, Tibaut is confirmed as chief Quaesitor. In Toulouse an autumn rising is put down with great effort, and de Montfort names himself count of Toulouse.

diary.title: Raimond returns to Toulouse
diary.details:
While de Montfort campaigns in the north, Raimond slips back into Toulouse to the citizens' joy. De Montfort finds the gates shut against him and lays siege for months.

Secrets
Tibaut, who found the first threads of Senex's inquiry in his laboratory notes, begins this year to investigate the Tribunal's mystery cults, the Cathars and the sorginak, sharing his suspicions with his filia Beatrice. A letter he sent her lies in the satchel of a Redcap who died of crusaders' wounds along the Via Domitia.

diary.title: Tolomae Marched
diary.details: Early in the year Tolomae is Marched for repeatedly meddling with mundanes, and slain. His suspected supporters scatter among other covenants or hide among the faidits.

diary.title: Simon de Montfort killed
diary.details:
A stone from a siege engine on the walls of Toulouse strikes Simon de Montfort on the head and kills him. Amaury de Montfort claims his titles, and Alice remains a leader of the campaign, but Simon's great domain begins to fall apart.

Secrets
Some suspect the engine was one of those Tres built to destroy Mistridge.

diary.title: Wizard's Wars at Tolosa Paratge
diary.details: In the weeks before de Montfort's death, Augustus of Tolosa Paratge, a senior Quaesitor, is persuaded by Bishop Foulques that Toulouse will fall and asks the covenant's Gorgiastic Cathars to leave for their safety. They refuse; Marc declares Wizard's War on him and, believing him possessed, kills him in the tower. Within the month St Tropez declares Wizard's War on the unresisting Marc and kills him. Under Mariola, the covenant splits into the Blacks, who hold it, and the Whites, who plot in the city to retake it.

diary.title: Siege of Marmande
diary.details: Soon after Christmas, Prince Louis's crusaders under Centule d'Astarac besiege Marmande.

diary.title: Tibaut dies
diary.details:
Tibaut, the Presiding Quaesitor, dies in the care of the monks of Saint Hilaire, taken for a Cathar by crusaders who later raid the abbey. His body is buried there and his belongings sit locked in the abbot's chest. At Dama's suggestion his filia Beatrice of Guernicus fills the office until the 1221 Tribunal. (The Hermetic culture chapter also says once that he died in 1214; the 1221 Tribunal takes 1219.)

Secrets
Warned by Luc of Ara Maxima Nova of Tibaut's questions, Dama ambushed him with Maju near the road to Foix. Her Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus shattered his Parma, but Maju's venom worked slowly; he staggered into the road and divinely blessed crusader knights carried him to the abbey before she could reach him. Before he died he confided something to the knights.

diary.title: Marmande massacred; Toulouse besieged
diary.details: After nine months Marmande surrenders on terms. Amaury de Montfort, urged by the Bishop of Saintes, then kills all five thousand townsfolk and their beasts and burns the town. Prince Louis's royal crusade besieges Toulouse but withdraws when pestilence breaks out in his army, and Raimond begins to win back his county.

tribunals.secrets:
Fraxinetum Redux, the hidden successor of Fraxinetum on the Hyères islands, holds 3 votes it has never claimed, since the Tribunal does not know it exists.

The Praeco killed both of the last two Presiding Quaesitors. Senex, investigating her cult of Matres & Matrones, slipped into her sanctum at Mimizan in 1210 while she was away at an akelarre and was caught there; his death was lawful under the Code, but she hid it. Tibaut took up his trail, and in 1219 Dama and her familiar Maju ambushed him near the road to Foix, stripping his Parma with Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus; he died of the serpent's poison at the Abbey of Saint Hilaire, where crusaders had carried him, and his belongings are still locked in the abbot's chest. A letter he sent Beatrice by an Iberian Redcap lies in the satchel of the Redcap, who died of his wounds beside the Via Domitia. Dama bought the Chief Redcap's tacit support with a Longevity Ritual for Alazais's mundane lover. Beatrice is suspected of sympathy with the cult, and Alazais and Mariola of Tolosa Paratge are rumoured to be members.

The Tribunal next meets in summer 1221 at the ruins of Glanum, a neutral site agreed on by all; its first business is whether Beatrice of Guernicus succeeds Tibaut as Presiding Quaesitor. If the Tribunal resolves to act against the crusade and the Church, the Pyrenean covenants may boycott the meeting of 1227 and, with the four covenants a Tribunal needs, ask the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to let them secede. If the saga follows history, Guy de Montfort is killed near Castelnaudary in April 1220, James I of Aragon comes of age in 1223, the count of Foix defies Louis in 1226 and 1227, and the crusade ends in 1229.

Dama must renew her Longevity Ritual before 1232.

Fraxinetum Redux. Heirs of the raider covenant the Coenobium destroyed in 975, led by Ahmad ibn Nasr of Tytalus, keep a pirate base on the Hyères islands with two magi, a third aboard a ship, and still sponsor raids on the Provençal coast and on Catalan and Genoese shipping, steering clear of the Coenobium's fleet. They have never declared themselves for fear their ancestors' name would bring a Wizard's War; their three votes go unused. They oppose only a new maritime stronghold or an island covenant off the south coast.

The Drac of Beaucaire. The monster said to have returned beneath the Rhône is a Tytalus eremite, Aucassin, who never comes to Tribunal and lives as the merchant Rene of Dragonianum, ruling the town council by subtle Mentem magic. He has learned he is heir to the Drac's blood and seeks a Mystery that would make him a true elder Drac; he has kidnapped children and servants to serve him.

neighbours.name: Windgraven
neighbours.summary: Founded 1060, destroyed 1197. Squat stone towers inside the remains of a Visigothic fortress on a rocky plateau in the south of the County of Toulouse. Its necromancers were notorious for cruelty, widely thought diabolists, and had sunk deep into Winter when Mistridge declared a lawful Wizard's War on them and battered the towers almost flat with giant boulders. Few grieved; the attack may have prompted Tres's destruction of Mistridge soon after. The book gives no aura.

neighbours.name: Lariander
neighbours.summary: Founded 1192, destroyed 1211. A Spring covenant of House Tremere in a faerie wood near the village of Montgey. In the summer of 1211 peasants and southern knights slaughtered a column of German crusaders in the wood on their way to the siege of Lavaur, and de Montfort's reprisals burned the village and the trees and killed the bewildered Tremere, whose black robes were taken for those of Cathar perfecti. The massacre left an Infernal aura of 6 over the village site and the wood, where dark shapes move at night. Garsenda of Lariander, now of the Ostal des Exiles, believes herself the only survivor.
neighbours.secrets: Garsenda herself, with faerie white ladies, stirred the villagers to attack the column in the hope of saving Lavaur, and blames herself for her covenant's ruin.

neighbours.name: Berinor
neighbours.summary: Founded 1089, fallen 1210. A modest Jerbiton covenant of the County of Toulouse, patron of many troubadours and trobairitz. It lived in a castle held for it by a mundane lord, and fell when de Montfort's men dispossessed him. Its survivors went to Tolosa Paratge.

neighbours.name: Bentalone
neighbours.summary: Founded 1106, destroyed 1207. A Summer covenant in a castle that Simon de Montfort's army mistook for a Cathar stronghold and took by surprise assault. The book does not say where it stood.

neighbours.name: Filii Sinapis
neighbours.summary: Founded 1063, abandoned 1215. Founded by Flambeau of Sinapis, the Normandy liege covenant whose magi left Anjou when the feud of Flambeau and Tytalus ended, and abandoned after the crusade swept through. The book does not say where it stood.

neighbours.name: Château de Penne (the first Bellaquin)
neighbours.summary: Bellaquin's home from the last years of the Schism War until about 1200: a ruined castle restored by magic, high above the Aveyron in the Tarn, a day's march north-north-east of Toulouse. Flambeau built it as a stronghold, then left it to the Jerbiton, who made it one of the Order's most admired buildings and ruled the resettled land around it as lords. Caught between feudal obligations and its own intrigues, the covenant was ruined by mundane forces, perhaps steered by other magi. The survivors took what they could, destroyed the rest, left the site to their mundane proxies and moved to Andorra, where Bellaquin lives on.

neighbours.name: Bachlach's Hermitage
neighbours.summary: The remains of a Diedne covenant in the wilds of Gascony, turned into a hermitage. Its magus Bachlach renounced his magic and hid from the Order as the hermit Estebe some years before the Schism War; his followers, the Valerenes of Agen, still live there apart from the world, seeking the Divine in nature and chasing the unicorns seen near Bazas. Each summer solstice they walk to Limoges to honour St. Valerie's bones. The buildings hold a Divine aura of 2, which turns to Magic 2 for the solstice night alone. His notes and journals lie in an old ossuary beside his crypt: a rare window on early Diedne magic and ritual, and a likely way to reopen old Schism War wounds.
neighbours.secrets: Bachlach was a pagan warrior-magus who beheaded Valerie when she refused to marry him; when she rose and carried her head to the archbishop at Limoges, he was converted on the spot. His followers' initiations may reenact the beheading.

neighbours.name: Nemetannais
neighbours.summary: A once-prominent Diedne covenant a mile from the village of La Romieu, founded in the mid-900s as a southern offshoot of Branugurix and destroyed by Flambeau in the Schism War. Six small pyramids of garluche sandstone, twelve to fifteen feet high and older than memory, once marking 'safe haven', bound a Magic aura of 3 that takes in a complex of caves, made unstable by the attack. The area swarms with feral magical cats, matagots (Magic Might 15), said to descend from the magi's familiars and to share the traits of the Founder Diedne's own.

neighbours.name: Lapurdum
neighbours.summary: Founded 822, abandoned 858. A Flambeau covenant built around a mithraeum on a Roman camp's site where the Adour meets the sea, given up in the mid-ninth century under Viking raids and quarrels within. Its ruins lie lost somewhere beneath the city of Bayonne.

neighbours.name: Donjon Leyre
neighbours.summary: Founded 955, destroyed 1008. An early vassal of Montverte (of the Normandy Tribunal) at the fork of the Leyre in the Landes, set up as a base for raids into the Basque Pyrenees. Every one of its founders died fighting in the Schism War.

neighbours.name: The two lost Diedne sites of Gascony
neighbours.summary: Two Diedne covenants of Gascony whose names were lost in the Schism War. Most Gascon Diedne fled their sites, often burning them before their attackers arrived. They are among the nine or more Diedne sites the Quaesitores struck from the records after the war: magi are forbidden to seek them out, though by now few know where not to look.

neighbours.name: Mistridge
neighbours.summary: Founded 1050, destroyed 1209. A famous covenant of powerful magi in a magically raised tower on the brink of a precipice in the Val du Bosque, thought proof against any mundane assault. In 1197 it destroyed Windgraven. In the winter of 1209 Tres Ex Miscellanea, with two other Rusticani and a host of mercenaries carrying weapons he had made, declared Wizard's War on every member and brought the tower down with magical siege engines, killing the defenders; whether for Windgraven's sake or because Mistridge had scorned him as a hedge wizard is still unknown. His acquittal in 1214 made the law on grogs in a Wizard's War. Rixenda Mistridge and other survivors went to the Ostal des Exiles.

neighbours.name: Askelarre
neighbours.summary: Founded 945, destroyed 1011. A covenant formed by a coven of Hermetic sorginak, Basque witches, whose members were spread across the Basque country. It was destroyed in the Schism War; Leo Augustus of Flambeau and Vegetius of Tremere died in the assault.

neighbours.name: Val-Negra's chapterhouse near Girona
neighbours.summary: A second portal and entrance to the Mercurian temple complex, at the eastern end of the Pyrenees near Barcelona, north of Girona. It was abandoned at the start of the Schism War, along with the portal that led to Val-Negra itself.

neighbours.name: Aedes Mercurii's outpost at Saint Jean Pied-de-Port
neighbours.summary: Until 1177 Aedes Mercurii kept a large outpost in the city of Saint Jean Pied-de-Port on the pilgrim road. The townsfolk came to suspect its covenfolk of witchcraft, and the house was lost when Richard the Lionheart razed the city. Some Hermetic historians believe a Mercurian temple there held a lapis mercurius, now lost, which could give Insight into the old road magic.

neighbours.name: Himinis' Forge
neighbours.summary: A fallen covenant of the Narbonnais, named in the Tribunal's lists; the book gives nothing more about it.

neighbours.name: Uxellodunum
neighbours.summary: A fallen covenant of the Narbonnais bearing the name of the old Gaulish hill-fort; the book names it and gives nothing more.

neighbours.name: The two lost Diedne covenants of the Massif Central
neighbours.summary: Two Diedne covenants somewhere in the Massif Central, their names and sites lost: two of the nine or more that the Quaesitores struck from the records after the Schism War, which magi are forbidden to seek.

neighbours.name: The ruins of Glanum
neighbours.summary: The ruins of the Roman town just south of St-Rémy, where two short-lived Hermetic settlements called Glanum stood in the ninth century, one Mercurian and one Mithraic. Both collapsed quickly, too narrow in their magic and too zealous to admit anyone outside their cult, and neither lasted long enough to have a Quaesitor review its charter and be recognised by the Lotharingian Tribunal of the day. Empty since the Schism War, the ruins were agreed as the neutral ground for the Tribunal of summer 1221 and may not be resettled until that is settled. Beatrice of Guernicus lives here as the Coenobium's guest; her sanctum is in effect a small chapter of Castra Solis, given to the even-handed study of the Roman shrines of the many cults that once flourished here. The book gives no aura.

links.note: Beatrice's sanctum, in effect a chapter

neighbours.name: Barbegal
neighbours.summary: Founded 895, abandoned 930. A Roman watermill complex a few miles north of Arles, home to three mage-smiths of House Verditius; one, an engineer, was said to have found how to draw vis of different Forms out of a Magic aura with enchanted waterwheels. Saracen raiding, abetted by Fraxinetum, emptied the undefended site, and its last survivor helped found the Coenobium. It keeps a Magic aura of 5. The broken remains of 13 of its magical wheels lie hidden under the undergrowth and three are missing: repairing the mill might recover its secret of vis on demand, a project the Coenobium, short of strong auras, would gladly sponsor.

links.note: Its survivor helped found the Coenobium

neighbours.name: The Birds of Camargue
neighbours.summary: Founded 901, merged 970. A Bjornaer covenant in the marshes at the mouth of the Rhône, whose magi joined the Coenobium against the threat of Fraxinetum. Its site is no longer a covenant.

neighbours.name: Elisii Campi (the Alyscamps)
neighbours.summary: Founded 843, driven out 1009. A small covenant of Ex Miscellanea necromancers and spirit masters in the crypts of the Alyscamps, the old Roman necropolis of Arles. They lived through the Schism War underground, but the rising Coenobium quietly turned the townsfolk against them with rumours of diabolists under the tombs, and they fled. Many of the sarcophagi still carry their enchantments and traps, and the city council now gives sarcophagi away to honoured visitors.

neighbours.name: Portus Termini (the Verdon gorge)
neighbours.summary: The refuge the necromancers of Elisii Campi sought in a hidden cave network in the Verdon gorge, under a new name. All contact with them was lost soon after, before the next meeting, so it was never registered as a covenant. Many suspect hoplites in the Coenobium's pay hunted them down.

neighbours.name: Fraxinetum (La Garde-Freinet)
neighbours.summary: Founded 889, destroyed 975. The raiders' covenant in the dark granite Massif des Maures above St Tropez, named for the ash groves planted by its founder Sayyid Shajarat al-Darda (an Andalusian Herbam master House Flambeau disowns) with his Tytalan lieutenant Nasr ibn Amaf. For a century it secretly backed the Moorish raids on the cities of Provence and the fall of several small coastal covenants, until the ransom of Abbot Maieul of Cluny in 973 roused the eastern magi, whose army under William I of Provence broke the Moors at Tourtour and besieged the base; the magi vanished into the forest. The razed fort keeps a Magic aura of 4 inside a dense palisade of ash, and what remains of the defensive rituals wakes the larger trees against intruders, so peasants say the place is haunted and leave it alone.
neighbours.secrets: Fraxinetum's heirs survive in secret as Fraxinetum Redux on the Hyères islands.

neighbours.name: Yf
neighbours.summary: Founded 821, fallen 911. A Diedne covenant on the islet of Yf off Marseilles, a Magic aura of 3 around an ancient yew grove where its magi held their rites. It fell to Fraxinetum's Moors long before the Schism War; one of its magi joined the Coenobium's founders for revenge, but her line died out just before the war. Sleepers under the yews dream of green-robed magi whispering vengeance. Vis: each All Souls' Eve up to six of the youngest branches of the oldest yew can be cut, each a pawn of Extraordinary Intellego vis that, burnt, lets its bearer speak with the dead once as by Whispers Through the Black Gate. No covenant claims it.

links.note: One of its magi joined the founders

neighbours.secrets: The magi of Fraxinetum Redux quietly harvest vis on the deserted isle.

neighbours.name: Castra Peccaius
neighbours.summary: The ruins of a Hermetic settlement abandoned three centuries ago, on the east bank of the Petit Rhône across from where Aigues-Mortes will one day stand. The Coenobium's covenfolk still come to harvest salt vis from a brackish pond inside the ruins, on land its mundane dependents lease from the Abbey of Psalmody. If history runs its course the monks will sell the land to King Louis.

neighbours.name: Telo Martius
neighbours.summary: A former Flambeau covenant at Toulon, under Mount Faron. The Coenobium now keeps a small chapter house on its site, run by a retired Redcap, the unGifted alchemist Aloysius Porphyri, who oversees the murex and kermes dye harvests.

neighbours.name: Turris Mascis (the Tropaeum Alpium)
neighbours.summary: A short-lived, mostly Mercurian covenant, the 'Tower of the Masques', that studied the Trophy of Augustus at La Turbie, the Roman monument that by tradition marks the Tribunal's eastern limit; what it learned is lost. The statue of Augustus inside was mostly smashed by Christian mobs, the monument's stones are built into the village, and the church of St Michael's Divine aura of 3 smothers any magic in them. The town is under Genoa's sway.

neighbours.name: Portus Cottiae
neighbours.summary: Founded 821, overrun 906. The first Mercer House and a Mercurian covenant, founded by Julius Donnus of Flambeau, an outcast Mercurian from the Greater Alps, as a second home for the revived Cult of Mercury. Built in the Roman manner of the Alpine covenants, its motherhouse, Brigantium, stood in the cliffs above Briançon commanding the Montgenèvre pass and the upper Durance, with chapters kept by mansionarii at Gap (Vapincum), Chorges (Caturigomagus), Embrun (Ebrodunum) and Oulx (Ulcium). Berber raiders overran it in 906; the survivor Anaïs of Jerbiton fled to Avignon and pressed for the league that became the Coenobium.
neighbours.secrets:
Brigantium: its magi brought the mountain down on the raiders and sealed themselves in; ghosts of the magi and Infernal shades of the attackers haunt the rubble, and its Mercere Portal lies buried beneath.

Caturigomagus: a sanctum under a ruined Roman way station a day beyond Chorges, its slain Merinita's books of Faerie magic guarded by three seductive dememoilles.

Vapincum: in the crypts under Gap cathedral, an old temple to Apollo, its weak aura smothered by the church's.

Ebrodunum: a stabling post, its hidden shrine to Mercury built into the new cathedral and its aura gone; descendants of the covenfolk may hold books and records.

Ulcium: a temple of Mars Ultor reached through a regio in the ruins above Oulx, the easiest to resettle but on the Roman Tribunal's border.

The heirs of Anaïs in the Coenobium may resist anyone who tries to reopen these sites.

neighbours.name: The County of Toulouse
neighbours.summary:
The middle of the Tribunal: a broad, shallow basin between the Pyrenees to the south and the uplands of Provence to the east, dusty with orchards, vines and fields. Every ridge and rocky spur seems to carry a castle. Villages are of timber and wattle or of the local brick, pink to deep red, so that whole towns flush with colour at sunrise and sunset, a sight northerners never stop praising. Drovers' roads up to a mile wide cross the plain, and each late spring huge herds of cattle, sheep and goats go up to the Pyrenean pastures, coming down again in early autumn.

The counts began as Merovingian officials, made the office hereditary under the Carolingians, and took on the speech and customs of the south, owning the French king as liege in name only. Raimond III pushed the county over old Septimania in the tenth century; Raimond IV (1093 to 1105) took the march of Provence and the Narbonnais, which with his Aragonese marriage made him lord of nearly all the Tribunal save Gascony. Raimond V gave the city its council of capitouls. A daughter may inherit when there is no son, as Philippa, Duchess of Aquitaine, did.

Lordship sits lightly here. Many lords long ago shook off their oaths, as the counts shook off the king's, and Raimond VI's easy rule, tax exemptions and war have raised a class of merchants and landholders who owe fealty to nobody and are often richer than the barons. A covenant here can stand outside the feudal web more easily than almost anywhere in Mythic Europe. Many towns copy Toulouse and elect capitouls or consuls of their own.

The crusade has turned the county into a patchwork. Since Simon de Montfort died before Toulouse in 1218 there are no borders: castles of either side stand a few miles apart, both keep garrisons scattered across the land, and the faidits, knights stripped of their lands by the crusaders, are drifting home to take them back by papal favour or by the sword. Raimond VI holds his city and much of the county again; Amaury de Montfort holds Carcassonne and the crusader strongholds. The massacres have left Infernal auras across the land, at Lavaur, Montgey, Bram, Montlaur, Hautpoul, Puisserguier and Alairac.

Hermetically the county is Tolosa Paratge's, one of the Tribunal's oldest covenants, now torn in two; the exiles of the Ostal des Exiles hide under Castle d'Aguilar. Windgraven, Lariander and Berinor have fallen here within living memory, and the Tribunal of 1214, meant for Toulouse, was moved to Castra Solis because de Montfort's army stood outside the walls.

neighbours.name: The City of Toulouse
neighbours.summary:
Capital of the county and heart of the Languedoc, once a Roman and then a Visigothic seat, and among the largest, richest and most cultivated cities of Mythic Europe; its people think Paris a backward rival. The count rules it in name, but the elected Capitole holds most of the power he has handed over, and the bishop shares the right of justice, so the city lives in constant friction between them.

Its stout wall has turned back siege after siege: de Montfort failed before it in 1211, was let in in 1215, was thrown out by a rising in 1216, besieged it from autumn 1217 until a stone killed him under the walls in summer 1218, and in 1219 Prince Louis tried again and withdrew when disease struck his camp. De Montfort razed the towers built into the wall, but twenty or more fortified towers still stand within the city, kept by petty nobles, capitouls and rich burghers with small guards of their own; the White faction of Tolosa Paratge holds one of them, and buying or building one is a sensible way for magi or wealthy companions to keep a foothold here.

Justice is shared by old custom between the count's court (now the Capitole) and the bishop's, each poaching on the other's ground, and a man condemned by one can sometimes win on appeal to the other. The law is the magisterial Roman law of the south, the Ability Civil and Canon Law, not the common law of France.

Since the White and Black Brotherhoods fought in the streets, lending at interest has been forbidden and money is hard to raise; the moneylenders have gone to Cahors. Six districts make up the city, and each returns two capitouls, who wear red robes trimmed with black fur over clothes in their district's colours.

neighbours.name: The Château Narbonnais
neighbours.summary: The count's castle on the western edge of the city, inside the walls, commanding the great western gate; it serves as the citadel if the walls fall. Raimond once gave it to Bishop Foulques to win him over. Alice de Montfort held it against the townsfolk when Raimond came back in autumn 1217 and had to yield it. In 1213 a mob broke into its dungeon, seized three crusader knights taken at Pujol, and tore them apart in the streets.

neighbours.name: Saint-Sernin District
neighbours.summary: The district of the great basilica of Saint-Sernin, for centuries the region's chief pilgrim shrine, which Pope Urban consecrated while travelling to Clermont to call the First Crusade. Its huge church of white stone and red brick, with its octagonal tower and spire, looms over the houses; Augustinian canons keep it, with a college and a hospice for the city's poor, and pilgrims crowd it each summer to see the relics. An Augustinian poetry contest is held in its orchard. Its capitouls wear yellow and white.

neighbours.name: La Pierre (Saint-Pierre des Cuisines)
neighbours.summary:
A poor riverside parish of boatmen by the Garonne, known for vice and theft; its harlots are called Magdalenes. Its church, a property of the Benedictines of Moissac, stands on the oldest Christian site in the Tribunal, though the building is only two hundred years old. Humble as it is beside Saint-Sernin and the Daurade, it is where the counts hold court, make their great announcements and sign their charters before the crowd, and where the capitouls proclaim their laws. Its capitouls wear deep blue.

The church steps hold a tiny Magic lacuna of aura 1. Here the counts swear to the people and new capitouls take their oaths, and here alone the Spirit of Tolosa can bind an oath made before the crowd: whoever breaks it, even unknowingly and in secret, becomes the subject of mostly false rumours across the county and gains the Flaw Infamous, though nobody learns what he did.

neighbours.name: Santa Maria Dealbata District
neighbours.summary: St Mary the White, named for the lime wash on its church: a district of rich merchants among smaller shops and craftsmen. A few wealthy artisans resent the merchants' grip, and an ambitious would-be capitoul can buy his way in if he will wade into the quarrel between the two. Its capitouls wear carnation pink. A candidate must live in the city a month before an election, and the capitouls talk of making it seven years.

neighbours.name: Saint-Etienne District
neighbours.summary: The wealthiest quarter, home to nobles and rich citizens. In Toulouse birth matters less than wealth, taste, learning and influence, and a rich commoner can climb into the petty nobility, to the scorn of nobles from elsewhere. Its cathedral, on the site of a chapel Saint Sernin founded, is a Romanesque basilica forever being enlarged and now caged in scaffolding; it has less standing than the other churches, perhaps because of its bishop, the hated Foulques, who is away with the crusaders. Its capitouls wear violet and white.

neighbours.name: Pont-Vieux and the Boom
neighbours.summary:
The district round the oldest bridge over the Garonne, whose capitouls wear amaranth, a maroon, and white. A huge timber boom has lately been built across the river to narrow it and quicken the current for the many watermills. Adam Carpentiere of Tolosa Paratge enchanted it with small devices set through its frame: it tames the river so that even the snow-melt floods no longer spill over, and, in a way few magi follow, it props up the covenant's regio, which is bound to the river's flow and had been fading as silt choked the channel.

At night the Spirit of Tolosa sometimes sits on the boom in the shape of a fisherman, glad to talk to anyone.
neighbours.secrets: The boom helps the regio not through the water but through the prosperity it has brought the mills and their shareholders.

neighbours.name: Adam Carpentiere's Waterfront Lacuna
neighbours.summary: A small pocket of Magic aura 2 on the waterfront, amid the city's Dominion, where Adam Carpentiere of Tolosa Paratge has long kept his sanctum and laboratory.

neighbours.name: Daraude, the District of the Sea Bream
neighbours.summary: The quarter nearest the Garonne, whose capitouls wear green and white. Its church, Our Lady of the Sea Bream (the Daurade), is a domed basilica of twelve sides whose gold mosaics outshine even its dome, built on a Roman temple of Apollo and served by Benedictines; it keeps a Black Madonna, Notre-Dame Noire. Each early May the church is decked with flowers brought in procession and a public feast is held. The district is loyal both to Toulouse and to the Church, and Cathars are not welcome. Somewhere in its misty alleys lies the way into the drowned lake of Tolosa.

neighbours.name: The Drowned Lake of Tolosa
neighbours.summary:
Before Rome, the Tolosates appeased a spirit in a lake by the Garonne, here in what is now the Daurade quarter: when fever rose from the marshes they sank consecrated gold and silver in its waters and the sickness passed. In 106 BC the governor Quintus Caepio drained it and carried off the hoard, the aurum Tolosanum, and something stranger besides, it is whispered. The Tolosates rose against Rome for the first time; within a year Caepio was dead in battle and the treasure gone. Some say it is the hoard the Cathars are rumoured to guard at Montségur, and every legend agrees gold still lies hidden in the region under a deadly curse. A temple of Apollo replaced the lake, and the Daurade replaced the temple.

Yet the lake survives. Whoever knows the signs, or simply loses his way in the riverside lanes on a misty evening, may with difficulty cross into a regio where the houses and streets stand empty and the water rises toward the river until only roofs break the surface of a still, black lake under drifting mist. Those who know the way step from roof to roof to the last house, where a boat waits to row them to the island of Tolosa Paratge. Things move in the dark water that are only ever half seen.

The regio is the work of the city's genius loci, the Spirit of Tolosa (Magic Might 40, Aquam; it answers to no name but Tolosa). Seen with Second Sight it is a damp mist or a sexless figure of water and reeds; in human shape, from one sunrise or sunset to the next, it is an unremarkable common townsman who nonetheless unsettles everyone, and it likes to fish from Adam Carpentiere's boom at night and chat, making little sense to mortals. It is soft-hearted toward the citizens and bound to the land. Its powers mend a breach in the walls until the next sunset or sunrise, when the stone falls away again; steer a body such as the capitouls in session or the bishop toward what is best for the whole city; bless a person with sudden prosperity and the Virtue Ways of Toulouse for as long as it likes; and bind oaths sworn on the steps of Saint-Pierre des Cuisines. The magi leave it alone, but know it has grown much weaker of late.

levels.name: The drowned streets and the lake
levels.see: Signs known to the Tolosates, or a misty evening in the waterfront lanes
levels.enter: Hard to find; the empty streets slope down into black water
levels.notes: Empty houses sink into a misty lake; an island with a black octagonal tower and red brick houses holds Tolosa Paratge. An enchanted boat comes to the last roof when a short Occitan poem is called.

links.note: the genius loci whose work this regio is

neighbours.secrets: The regio echoes the old sacrificial lake and is bound both to the river and to the power and prosperity of Toulouse itself. De Montfort's conquest and the city's strife are what weakened the aura and made the regio hard to reach, and the magi's own feud mirrors the city's. Only healing the city will save the covenant: restoring learning and culture, perhaps by founding a university inside the walls or championing Occitan letters. Adam's boom is only a first step, and it worked through the mills' wealth, not the water.

neighbours.name: The Toulouse Hinterland
neighbours.summary: The towns round the city stand among golden wheat, with stony sheep pastures on the low hills. Many have followed Toulouse in shedding feudal dues and electing capitouls to rule for their artisans and burghers. Small castles dot the country, some held by crusaders or their friends, some by southern lords still hiding Cathars and faidits.

neighbours.name: Termes
neighbours.summary: Reckoned with Cabaret and Minerve among the three mightiest castles of the region, taken by de Montfort after a hard siege. Held in 1220 by a crusader garrison, but word has come that Oliver and Bernard of Termes, its defender's sons, are coming back with their men this spring, as dispossessed southern lords across the county retake their lands.

neighbours.name: Pujol
neighbours.summary: A small castle and hamlet three miles from the city, the home of Carolus St. Tropez, who passes for a minor southern noble owing no liege. De Montfort took it; St. Tropez won it back with a handful of men in summer 1213, captured the three crusader knights holding it (they had been burning crops round Toulouse, and with them vis sources) and put the rest of the garrison to the sword. A Toulousain mob later dragged the knights from the Château Narbonnais and hanged what was left of them outside the walls. Arnaud Amalric often stays here as St. Tropez's guest. Held in 1220 by St. Tropez.
neighbours.secrets: St. Tropez believes the Gorgiastic Cathar Marc controlled the knights' minds; it fed the hatred that ended in Marc's death.

neighbours.name: The Ashen Field and Haunted Wood of Montgey
neighbours.summary:
Montgey is gone: only a field of ash remains. In 1211 a column of crusaders, mostly Rhinelanders, marching to the siege of Lavaur was caught in the woods here by the Count of Foix's knights and the villagers, and some six hundred were butchered. Survivors spoke of white ladies, the faerie demesoilles, casting spells on the column and of the trees themselves attacking. When Lavaur fell, de Montfort came back and hanged the villagers.

Both the village site and the wood of the massacre now hold Infernal auras of 6, and dark shapes scurry between the trees at night. In the burned wood stood Lariander, the Tremere covenant the crusaders destroyed in the reprisals, mistaking its black-robed magi for Cathar perfecti.
neighbours.secrets: The tales are true. Garsenda of Lariander stirred the villagers to fall on the column, hoping it would save Lavaur, with the demesoilles' help, and so brought the crusaders down on her own covenant.

neighbours.name: Castle Puivert and its Lake
neighbours.summary:
A castle on a low hill in a green, thickly wooded valley, famous for a great gathering of Cathars in 1170 and for its open-handed welcome to troubadours. Bernard of Congost held it until de Montfort took it in 1210; the crusader Lambert de Thury rules it in 1220.

Below it lies a quiet lake with a throne-shaped rock on the shore, where troubadours serenaded the ladies of the castle. On Midsummer night, if a new song praising a lady's beauty is sung while she sits on the throne, the lock of hair she gives the singer holds 4 pawns of Rego vis (unclaimed). The faerie lady of the lake grows jealous of such homage and sometimes raises the waters to carry off the lady, her maids and the singer beneath the water to a regio where all of them must serve her.
neighbours.secrets: Lambert de Thury may come home from a late Midsummer hunt to find his castle empty and his wife and household gone beneath the lake.

neighbours.name: Bruniquel
neighbours.summary: A castle Count Raimond meant to destroy when he saw he could not hold it against de Montfort. His brother Baudouin talked him out of it and took command of the garrison, but Baudouin had already gone over to the crusade and handed the castle to it at once, a treachery that later cost him his life.

neighbours.name: Puilaurens
neighbours.summary: A powerful castle, a fief of the King of Aragon since 1162, where faidits and hunted Cathars find shelter; being Aragonese, it is off limits to the crusaders. Held in 1220 for the King of Aragon.

neighbours.name: Villedieu-du-Temple
neighbours.summary: A Templar commandery near Montauban, where a Templar knight cut Baudouin of Toulouse down from the walnut tree he was hanged on and buried him. The Templars stay mostly neutral in the war, though they lean to the crusaders.

neighbours.name: The Albigeois
neighbours.summary: The country south of Albi, so steeped in Cathar sympathy that its name came to stand for every heretic, and for the crusade sent to destroy them. It is well wooded, and its vineyards make a cheap, plain but drinkable wine poured all over the Tribunal and beyond.

neighbours.name: The Woods of the Demesoilles
neighbours.summary: The many woodlands of the Albigeois are haunted by the demesoilles, faerie White Ladies who take the part of the poor and oppressed. Several are close to Garsenda of the Ostal des Exiles, and some of them helped turn the woods of Montgey against the crusaders in 1211. The book gives no auras or Might for them.

neighbours.name: Lavaur and the Field of Ashes
neighbours.summary:
A small Trencavel town on the Agout, called the citadel of Satan for its heresy. The Bishop of Clairvaux failed to take it in 1181; in 1211 its horseshoe of earthen ramparts and walls, backed against a high cliff, looked unbreakable. Faidits had gathered there under Aimery of Montreal and his learned sister Na Geralda (Guirauda), who ran a house for Cathar women believers and patronised troubadours and scholars. It fell after six weeks: Aimery's gallows broke under his armour and his throat was cut with his knights'; Na Geralda was given to the soldiers, thrown into a well and stoned to death, which sickened even some crusaders; and three or four hundred Cathars walked willingly onto a pyre in a meadow outside the walls. Toulousain knights found in the garrison exposed Raimond's double game and turned the crusade against him for good. Gui de Lucy holds it for the crusade in 1220.

Where the Cathars burned is a field of ash on which nothing grows, with an Infernal aura of 6. Na Geralda's ghost haunts the town, appearing whole and finely dressed; she courts a likely lover in fin amor and only well into the affair reveals what she is and begs for her bones to be properly buried. Refused, she shows herself as the mangled corpse she became and terrifies the faithless suitor. The crusaders cannot see her and laugh at the stories, but they want her bones left alone, and anyone trying to lay her to rest will face Gui de Lucy and his men.
neighbours.secrets: Nobody knows why the crusaders cannot see the ghost.

neighbours.name: The Agenais
neighbours.summary: The county's far north round Agen: low wooded hills and sheep country, more like France than the south. Its fine wool keeps it prosperous, and the heretics are very strong here.

neighbours.name: Château Lolmie
neighbours.summary: The castle near Montcuq where, in 1214, Baudouin of Toulouse's own men betrayed him to two of his brother's knights; he was hauled naked from his bed and carried off over a saddle, then hanged at Montauban a few days later.
neighbours.secrets: Dying, Baudouin cursed his brother's bones never to be buried and the traitors of Lolmie to early graves. Most of the thirty have died in strange accidents, and the rest are desperate for help. The curse is a unique Invocation of level 60, of Divine or Infernal power as the storyguide chooses; its victims roll four extra botch dice until they confess the treachery and are forgiven.

neighbours.name: Morlhon le Haut
neighbours.summary: The castle of the Morlhon family, crusaders in the Holy Land; Odo de Morlhon built the Cluniac house of the Holy Sepulchre at nearby Villeneuve after a vision. Orthodoxy did not save them: the crusaders took castle and town in 1214, made the lord a faidit, and burned seven Waldensians in the market place a year before the Church even condemned them. The de Montfort family holds the Morlhon titles in 1220. Pons de Morlhon has joined the Ostal des Exiles as a companion, advised by the furious shades of the seven Waldensians burned there.

neighbours.name: The Vineyards of Cahors
neighbours.summary: The country round Cahors gives itself to the famous black wine, in truth a deep red, shipped all over Mythic Europe; vines climb almost every south-facing slope, many crowned by castles. A few flasks, rightly made, hold a strong source of spell-like vis (unclaimed).
neighbours.secrets: A Cahors moneylender ruined by a noble of Toulouse who calls his loan void under the city's ban on usury offers the magical wine to anyone who can make the debt good; the loan was made after the ban, so it may take the capitouls or the bishop to settle.

neighbours.name: The Carcassès
neighbours.summary: The old Trencavel lands round Carcassonne: hilly, with oak and beech forest and villages of grain or vines as the soil allows, littered with castles from the Trencavels' endless wars with the counts. Pilgrims on the way to Santiago de Compostela pass through. The crusade's worst cruelties were done here, and its marks are Infernal auras in castle after castle.

neighbours.name: The Dry Wells of Carcassonne
neighbours.summary: In 1209 the springs, cisterns and castle well of Carcassonne all failed in a hard drought, and with its viscount taken by treachery the city surrendered. The besiegers call it a miracle; the townsfolk suspect magic was turned on them.
neighbours.secrets: Nobody has found out what dried the wells.

neighbours.name: The Gold Mines of Auriac
neighbours.summary: Ancient gold mines, long abandoned, where nuggets can still be found and Terram vis gathered (unclaimed), if anyone can face what lives there. A Faerie aura of 4 fills the tunnels, home to follets: stone-throwing fae like northern goblins who love to bring the roof down on intruders. They live under two rival counts, one in each mine, and wage a bitter war on each other.

neighbours.name: The Marketplace of Bram
neighbours.summary: A small walled town that held de Montfort off for three days. The priest of Montreal, who had betrayed the crusaders, was defrocked here by Bishop Gui of Carcassonne, mutilated, dragged through the streets and hanged. The hundred defenders had their eyes put out and their ears, noses and lips cut off, and were sent to Cabaret led by one man left a single eye. Some of the maimed still live, and some serve as grogs at the Ostal des Exiles. The market place keeps an Infernal aura of 3, and violence and revenge are now common there.

neighbours.name: Lastours and the Castles of Cabaret
neighbours.summary:
Rich in nearby iron and staunchly Cathar, Lastours is famous for three small stone castles a few miles apart on a sheer ridge above the Grésillon: Quertinheux on a rock low in the valley, Fleur Epine crowning the slopes, and Cabaret on a spur ringed by cliffs and the Orbiel on three sides, one of the three strongest fortresses of the region. The crusaders fell back in winter 1210, and de Montfort's kinsman Bouchard de Marly spent sixteen months in chains here; in 1211 Pierre-Roger de Cabaret had to give up the castles and free him, but escaped capture. The castles are held for the crusade in 1220, and Pierre-Roger, a friend of Cathars and a lavish host to troubadours, may win them back now the crusade falters.

At Fleur Epine his brother Jourdain, lord of Pennautier, kept court with his wife Auda, a famous beauty called Na Loba, the She-Wolf, cruel to the lovers she enthralled; the troubadour Peire Vidal once crept up in a wolfskin to sing to her and was mauled by a mastiff that took him for a real wolf. Now old, she waits in exile with her three bewitching daughters.
neighbours.secrets: Na Loba is blamed for betraying her liege Raimond-Roger Trencavel in 1209: he spurned her for her eldest daughter, so she arranged his safe-conduct to de Montfort and then withdrew her guards. She may bear the Curse of Venus, Venus' Blessing or something darker. Peasants whisper that her daughters are werewolves, and those who repeat it disappear.

neighbours.name: Montlaur
neighbours.summary: The villagers besieged the garrison de Montfort left in the castle; he came back, hanged everyone he could catch and burned the village to the ground. Their ghosts are still seen in the woods, a dreadful sight, and the site has an Infernal aura of 4.

neighbours.name: Hautpoul
neighbours.summary: A Visigothic fortress on a crag which de Montfort took in 1212 after a four-day siege, many defenders slipping away in a thick fog that rose without warning during the assault. Castle and town were burned; now an eerie, bat-haunted ruin stands above a few shacks of survivors, under an Infernal aura of 3 and frequent uncanny fogs.

neighbours.name: Saissac
neighbours.summary: Once a Cathar stronghold known for its generosity to troubadours, taken after Carcassonne fell and given to de Montfort's friend Bouchard de Marly, who holds it in 1220 against its dispossessed heirs. The heirs will likely look for help to win it back, and are open-minded enough to welcome a new covenant inside the citadel.

neighbours.name: Puisserguier
neighbours.summary: When a northern knight killed a southern lord of the crusade in a quarrel, de Montfort had him buried alive as southern custom demanded. The dead lord's nephew was not appeased: he changed sides, set fire to Puisserguier, the castle entrusted to him, threw its fifty northern soldiers into the dry moat and buried them alive under stones, and took its two knights to Minerve to be blinded and mutilated. The moat has an Infernal aura of 4.
neighbours.secrets: The buried garrison still claws at the earth at night and will soon break out to take revenge on the living, unless someone buries them deeper or brings their spirits peace.

neighbours.name: Castelnaudry and St. Martin-Lalande
neighbours.summary: A weak castle, which is why de Montfort went there in 1211, to lure Raimond and the Count of Foix into open battle. At nearby St. Martin-Lalande the southerners routed Bouchard de Marly's relief column, but de Montfort rode out with fifty knights, rallied the fugitives and fell on the southerners as they looted the baggage, turning their victory into a costly defeat. Afterwards the mercenary captain Savary de Mauléon kidnapped Raimond's son for his unpaid wages. Raimond's false claim that de Montfort had fallen sparked a revolt, crushed with great brutality.

neighbours.name: The Ruins of Alairac
neighbours.summary: A Visigothic mountain fortress that de Montfort stormed in a howling gale, throwing every defender from the battlements onto the rocks thousands of feet below. Bandits now lair in its shattered, bat-haunted towers, an almost endless wind whistles through them, and the ghosts of the dead seek burial for their broken bones. Infernal aura 4.

neighbours.name: Fanjeaux and Prouille
neighbours.summary: Fanjeaux, a small castle town on a hilltop, is where Dominic lived from 1206 to 1215 and led the preaching against the Cathars. Below it, at Prouille, he founded the nunnery of St Marie for women won back from Catharism and girls seeking the veil. Even Cathars honour his holiness, the more so since he drove off a demon here shaped like a huge cat with burning eyes and a long grasping tongue, a corrupted beast that may still roam the country. Once a heretic stronghold, the town now meets Cathars with threats and denounces them.
neighbours.secrets: Perfecti keep slipping back into Fanjeaux at the risk of the stake; they are looking for something they left there.

neighbours.name: Castle d'Aguilar
neighbours.summary: A fortress with six great towers on a dome of rock, Roman in origin and strengthened by the Visigoths, long home to many Cathars. A Trencavel castle, it was taken by de Montfort in 1210 and the de Termes family withdrew to Termes, but it was retaken in 1213 and has been a centre of resistance ever since; the crusaders passed it by. Faidits and minor dispossessed nobles shelter within its walls and in the villages round about. Held in 1220 by the southern party, under the lords of Termes.

neighbours.name: The Grottoes of Aguilar
neighbours.summary: A wide, little-known maze of natural caves riddling the rock under Castle d'Aguilar, with a Magic aura of 3, known to the Order of old as a mithraeum and a vis source. Here the Ostal des Exiles has its sanctums.

neighbours.name: The Mithraeum of Aguilar
neighbours.summary: Deep in the grottoes, a mithraeum with a Magic aura of 5, long used by Flambeau magi pursuing the Mithraic mysteries. The exiles have left it alone, but it lies inside their Aegis of the Hearth, and the Flambeau may soon find the new covenant on their doorstep and have to decide what to do about it.

neighbours.name: Count of Toulouse
neighbours.summary:
Raimond VI has ruled since 1194, easy-going and tolerant, and has never tried to win back the power the capitouls took in 1188. The crusade stripped him of many titles; after losing Toulouse he spent four years in exile, much of it at the papal court with his son pleading for his lands, while Simon de Montfort named himself count in 1216. He came back in 1217 and has won back many vassals; de Montfort died besieging him in 1218 and Prince Louis's royal army was turned back in 1219. In 1220 he holds his city firmly and much of the county by force of arms, and works tirelessly to be recognised again as its rightful count, a title Amaury de Montfort also claims; whether he can make terms with the French crown and the pope and leave the county to his son is still in doubt.

His heir is his loyal son Raimond; Raimond's daughter Joan, born in 1220, will inherit only if he has no son. Bishop Foulques is his implacable enemy, but the legate Arnaud Amalric has lately made peace with him. He let his brother Baudouin, who had gone over to the crusade, be hanged at Montauban in 1214 and watched with approval.

The arms shown are Toulouse's red and gold; the real charge is the voided, pommelled cross of Toulouse, which the app draws as a plain cross. The number of manors is a guess; the book gives none.

neighbours.name: Amaury de Montfort
neighbours.summary:
Simon de Montfort's son, who claims his father's titles: Count of Toulouse and Viscount of Béziers and Carcassonne. Since Simon was killed in 1218 the great domain he carved out has been falling apart, and in 1220 Amaury hangs on to Carcassonne, where his father lies in St Nazaire, and to the crusader garrisons scattered through the county. His mother, Alice de Montfort, remains a leader and strategist of the campaign; she was forced to give up the Château Narbonnais when Raimond returned in 1217.

The Montfort lion has a forked tail, which the app draws as a plain lion.

neighbours.name: Raimond II Trencavel
neighbours.summary: The seventeen-year-old heir of the Trencavel viscounts of Béziers and Carcassonne, dispossessed by Simon de Montfort. His father Raimond-Roger was seized during talks under a supposed safe-conduct in the siege of 1209 and died in his own dungeon, of dysentery or poison. The young viscount is trying to reclaim his title, and many local clergy pushed out by northern priests back him; Castres looks to the Montforts instead.

neighbours.name: Lords of Termes
neighbours.summary: The sons of Termes's defender, dispossessed by de Montfort, who are said to be coming home with their men in spring 1220 to take Termes back. Their family held Castle d'Aguilar, lost it in 1210 and won it back in 1213; the Hermetic exiles in its caves owe them no formal fealty, but the family knows of them and lets them be.

neighbours.name: Lord of Pujol
neighbours.summary: A minor southern noble who holds the small castle of Pujol, three miles from Toulouse, owing allegiance to nobody, and won it back from the crusaders in 1213. He has befriended the legate Arnaud Amalric, who often stays with him and has been swayed by him against the French.
neighbours.secrets: The lord is Carolus St. Tropez of Tolosa Paratge, leader of its White faction.

neighbours.name: Gui de Lucy
