Shunning the worldliness of Benedictines and Cistercians, its monks live in solitude and silence within the Chartreuse massif, with no ministry but prayer, and seldom take retreatants. They avoid needless speech but may talk on their weekly four-hour walk in the woods, changing partners each half hour; only the prior speaks to would-be retreatants and outsiders. Lay brothers in a dormitory at the valley's foot do the labour, manage supplies and turn visitors away.
neighbours.ruler: The prior of the Grande Chartreuse

neighbours.name: Cathedral of St Apollinaris
neighbours.summary: A cathedral rebuilt in the Cluniac Romanesque style and reconsecrated by Pope Urban II in 1095. Set into a column of its ambulatory is a milestone of the Via Agrippa whose Latin inscription names its sponsor, Florentius Niger, a senator thought to have been a priest of Mercury; it reeks of non-Hermetic magic and may hold an Insight into the old Mercurian road magic, or a clue to a lost temple. Studying it in place is hard, and taking it out would bring the clergy hunting the thief.

neighbours.name: Church of St Michael, La Turbie
neighbours.summary: The church beside the Tropaeum Alpium whose Divine aura of 3 smothers whatever magic the monument's scattered stones hold.

neighbours.name: Avignon
neighbours.summary: The commune that has dominated southern Provence since 1129, half free of the Empire and owing nothing to the Catalan count. Its bridge, the Pont St Bénezet, and the Isle de Barthelasse are the heart of the Coenobium, and the city's Divine aura is 3. Magi visiting openly are expected to call on the covenant and pay its toll.

neighbours.name: Arles
neighbours.summary: A free commune on the pattern of the Italian city-states, ruled since 1132 by an elected podestà from outside, who names the other consuls. A busy seaport where northern crusaders and pilgrims take ship for the Holy Land, where the Rhone barges hand cargo to sea craft, and where most of the Rhone boatmen live. The Coenobium's Mercer House hides in the old arena, the Factory stands across the wooden bridge at Trinquetaille, and the drac's lair is said to open from a pool outside the north gate.

neighbours.name: Beaucaire
neighbours.summary: 'Beautiful rock', on the Languedoc bank facing Tarascon, nominally the Count of Toulouse's; he took it back from Simon de Montfort's men after a short siege in 1216. The utricularii of the boatmen's guild rule the wharves under the cliff, the guildsmen guard the ferry to Tarascon jealously and charge dearly, and the Coenobium, unusually, keeps no one here, though rumours of the Drac's return may draw it.

neighbours.name: Tarascon
neighbours.summary: The imperial town facing Beaucaire across the Rhone, with its own legend of an amphibious dragon, the Tarasque, whose lair lies in the hills outside.

neighbours.name: Marseille
neighbours.summary: Massalia of the Phocaean Greeks, above the mouth of the Lacydon; Caesar slighted it for Arles after it backed Pompey, and Saracen raids wasted it, but with the Catalan counts' support it is again an important port. Pilgrim and crusader ships sail now and then, though Genoa holds most of the Levant trade. Hugh III of Baux holds it as viscount for the Emperor.

neighbours.name: Orange
neighbours.summary: A town of the Baux princes with a strong commune that curbs them, its north gate Tiberius's arch, its great Roman theatre in ruins.

neighbours.name: Aix
neighbours.summary: The Count of Provence's new capital, grown from the Celtic hill fort of Entremont and the Roman camp of Aquae Sextiae by its hot spring. Marius beat the Teutones nearby at Montagne Sainte-Victoire, and the Garagai Gorge lies close.

neighbours.name: Toulon
neighbours.summary: A dyers' town under Mount Faron since Phoenician times, with murex on its beaches and kermes oaks on its hills; the Coenobium has a chapter house and a dye works here.

neighbours.name: St-Rémy
neighbours.summary: A medieval town under the Alpilles, with the ruins of Glanum just to the south, where the Tribunal meets in summer 1221.

neighbours.name: Vienne
neighbours.summary: Capital of the Allobroges and a great Roman colony, now the seat of the prince-archbishop of northern Arelat, with its Roman stone bridge over the Rhone.

neighbours.name: The Utricularii
neighbours.summary: The boatmen of the Rhone, a powerful guild that controls the river's trade. Nominally based at Beaucaire, where they hold the wharves and the ferry, they are most numerous at Arles, where cargoes pass to sea-going ships. Many venerate St Bénezet at his chapel on Avignon's bridge, and they respect Nicodemus warily.

details.wants: Control of every cargo and crossing on the Rhone

neighbours.secrets: Aucassin of Tytalus has agents among them at Beaucaire and Arles who spy and enforce for him and keep the ferry toll high; one lately humiliated a Redcap of the Coenobium.

neighbours.name: The Masques of the Coenobium
neighbours.summary: The witches, cunning folk, herbalists and faerie doctors of the southern coast and Alpine foothills, allied to the Coenobium for two centuries: it shelters them, and they watch over its mundane interests and let its magi keep within the letter of the Code. Some have been adopted as nominal Redcaps; Alazais's lover is one of them. The Coenobium suits a troupe wanting a non-Hermetic saga.
neighbours.ruler: Lavandarius the Pralician, for the Coenobium

details.rules: The Hermetic magi remain the senior partners
details.wants: Protection from the authorities and from other magi
details.offers: UnGifted agents and informants, vis harvesting and guarding, charms and amulets, sway over common folk

neighbours.name: The House of Baux
neighbours.summary: Lords of Baux, Orange and much of Provence's petty nobility, who claim descent from Balthazar and bear the Star of Bethlehem. The Gift appears strangely often among them, lending weight to their talk of magical blood. House Jerbiton has long recruited their less warlike sons, but these seldom have the Gentle Gift and tend to nepotism and self-advancement, and often to a coarse taste in beauty; several have gone over to Tytalus and a few warlike ones to Flambeau. Balthazarine magi have the Mythic Blood (Balthazarine) Virtue. Marcus d'Les Baux is the current Hermetic heir, with at least two younger Balthazarine magi of junior branches.

details.wants: Advancement, lands and the favour of Emperor and Church

neighbours.name: The Corsairs of the Hyères
neighbours.summary: Pirates and Saracen raiders who haunt the coves of Port-Cros and Porquerolles and moor at the Frioul islands off Marseille, raiding the towns of the coast and Catalan and Genoese ships.

details.wants: Plunder from the coast and its shipping

neighbours.secrets: They are the mundane arm of Fraxinetum Redux, led by Ahmad ibn Nasr, who keeps them off Hermetic shipping and away from the Coenobium's fleet with spies ashore.

neighbours.name: Val-Negra
neighbours.summary:
Founded 774, fallen 1012. Once domus magna of House Flambeau, home of the Founder himself and seat of the first Tribunal of the region; at its height, with 33 members, the largest covenant the Order has ever had, and as mighty as Durenmar. Its device is a cartwheel whose seven spokes are swords. Every magus knows the legend, yet almost no one knows where it lies or how to get in. Some say it still lives, shut away from the Order by choice; others that the regio of Mount Perditu is slowly turning it into a myth, or that the Magic Realm has swallowed it; a few think bold magi could find it and bring it back.

History. The stronghold first belonged to Delendar the Destroyer, an old Mercurian wizard who took it from a cabal of sahirs who had enslaved the Aerie Clan, the strange folk native to the vale. Flambeau came to recruit him after the Founding, but Delendar had died first, having foreseen Flambeau's coming in a last vision and left the place to him; his one apprentice, Delendos, joined House Flambeau. The covenant was settled straight after the First Tribunal, but Flambeau would not accept a charter unless he held suzerainty over every covenant Val-Negra helped to found, and Guernicus's objections led the Second Grand Tribunal to lay down how regional Tribunals are made and run. Val-Negra was recognised a year later, in 774, and a Tribunal grew up around it.

Flambeau was the only Founder to live here, and Trianoma and Mercere visited often; Gelon of Verditius spent decades here, and the Founder trained and housed his army of wizards here for his war on the Moors. Apromor, a Basque and Flambeau's first apprentice, became the first Primus in 820 and spread outposts across the Pyrenees; with his support Priamitus of Mercere raised a temple to Mercury nearby and revived the Cult of Mercury here, its heyday the early 900s. In 865 Val-Negra was placed in the Iberian Tribunal. Most of its golden age is unrecorded, and what tales survive disagree, so each troupe may write its own.

The fall. Just before the Schism War, many of its Flambeau left after one of them had a vision, and founded Aedes Mercurii from its outlying halls and temple. Those who stayed had long distrusted House Diedne and pressed hard for war. Primus Entisimon roused the House with a speech, the vaults were thrown open to pour out vis and silver, and magi rode out to strike first; it cost them dearly. Lucien the Fat of Flambeau was ambushed and killed; Leo Augustus of Flambeau and Vegetius of Tremere fell attacking Askelarre; Delendez of Flambeau, victorious against the Diedne of Galicia and Navarre, was lost to Twilight in battle; seven magi of several Houses died in the Final Victory over Llewellyn; and Iarna of Flambeau left at the war's end to hunt the last Diedne wherever they had fled and never returned (an Ex Miscellanea prophecy says she will, if the Diedne ever do). Of 25 magi when the war began, 4 lived to see it end, and much of the covenant's lore died with the rest.

Meanwhile five Diedne archmagi struck the home its magi had left lightly guarded, slipped past its traps and wards, and fought their way to the Iron Door. They killed three of the five magi defending it, and were themselves destroyed. The Quaesitors kept what happened quiet and ruled that Val-Negra must never rise again; the domus magna moved to Castra Solis, and the survivors went to Aedes Mercurii, which has claimed ever since that Val-Negra is gone and its legacy theirs. Castra Solis disputes the claim. Only a few old, powerful magi still alive have been there; they warn others off, though they like telling tales of its glory, and a careful player may coax facts out of them.

The Black Vale. A gorge of the Tessier on the south side of Mount Perditu, cut so deep that the sun reaches the bottom only around midday, and then through the mist off the river: hence the name. It is the mountain's magical heart; most of its wilds have a Magic aura of 1 to 4, by place and season.

Perdut (Magic aura 6). A hamlet of about thirty at the gorge's mouth, five houses and one shared field. The aura has left its people looking very old or very young; no outsider has come in generations, and they fear and revere unseen 'watchers' whom their tales say strangers once came to meet. The Gift seems not to touch them. They keep up an empty manor on a hill, once the covenant's guest house, and gladly lodge and feed visitors there. A ruined stone hut on the edge of the village held a Mercere Portal to an unknown destination, wrecked on purpose long ago by a Disenchant ritual. Aedes Mercurii's own portal here was abandoned at the start of the Schism War.

The way in. Past Perdut the gorge is a regio of three levels: the Labyrinthine Caverns (aura 6), the Valley of Mists (aura 7) and the fortress (aura 8), reached only through the Circle of Light (see the levels). Redcaps once carried enchanted lanterns whose coloured light showed a safe path all the way; Harco keeps one in its vault and Primus Garus has another, but asking to borrow either will draw questions.

The fortress. Across the chasm the crumbling but still splendid fortress climbs the mountain face under the great Black Tower. The outer walls hold and several towers stand; most buildings inside have fallen. Pits scattered about drop into caves and tunnels beneath, and the Black Guard of the Aerie Clan still keeps watch. Astella of Jerbiton's garden of magical plants, gone wild since she fled early in the Schism War, has overgrown most of the ruin: its creepers are rooted so deep in the walls that killing them would bring much of the place down. Some rooms hold vis-bearing plants, plants with powers like spells, and a few that kill. Her own garden is still kept in order by old enchantments; studying it and the wild growth counts as a Significato in Herbam, gaining a stress die + 8 experience.

The Guardian's Tower. The path to the main gate runs beneath a bridge joining this tower, over the chasm on the right, to the Black Tower on the left; neither opens onto the path. It is entered only over the bridge from the Black Tower (magic can lift a magus to the bridge, if it penetrates the Aegis). At least two Aerie guards are always posted, one at the top and one at the bottom; they admit anyone who proves to be a Hermetic magus and hand out tokens for the Aegis. A bell at its centre rings whenever someone crosses into the regio. Its middle floor is at the covenant's ground level, and its lowest is cut into the cliff, with wide windows over the drop.

The Black Tower. Built by Delendos as Apromor's seat as Primus, and the Primi's sanctum until the domus magna moved; half of it is sunk into the mountain. The second floor, jutting from the rock, holds the barracks and the only outside door, onto the bridge; a spiral stair leads up to the third, the great hall of banquets and meetings, now bare and deep in dust. The Grand Stair climbs from the third to the sixth floor. The fourth and fifth hold meeting rooms, a conference hall, a scriptorium and two wrecked guest laboratories, and on the fourth the Memorial, a cobwebbed hall to fallen heroes with an unfinished tapestry of the magi lost in the Schism War. The sixth was the Primus's reception floor: a small dining hall, a spare laboratory still in fair order, and rooms for six guests. The seventh has no door, window or stair and is reached only by magic: the Primus's quarters, a tiny library, the main laboratory reshaped by Primus after Primus, and Apromor's Perdo laboratory, the Dissolution Chamber.

Below the Black Tower. Behind a blocked door on the second floor a stair runs down to a ground floor and a basement, both stuffed with stores and forgotten long ago. Under the junk in the basement are two trap doors. The wooden one opens on a cellar of laboratory ingredients, mostly rotten, where odd magical effects linger. The stone one needs a combined Strength of +3 or magic to lift; under it a stone spiral stair passes the Catacombs into the Dungeon (whose passages lead back up to the Catacombs), then stops dead against rock flecked with jade spirals, a sigil, not stone, that seals the way. Any Aerie nearby raises the alarm and fights anyone trying to get past it, with grim warnings of what lies below. Beyond, a narrow shaft ends in a round, damp room ten paces across, its walls carved with old battles that may hold clues to House Flambeau's past. Set in the floor is an iron disc five paces wide engraved with the seven-sworded wheel; it sounds solid but hollow beneath. It baffles any divination of level 40 or less (a constant PeVi 40 effect over the room). This is the Iron Door. It has been here from the start, no one knows who made it, and tampering with it has been forbidden since Apromor's day.

The Grand Library. A great hall of charred oak tables. Many of its books burned in the Diedne assault, when one of the attackers set herself alight here; restoring the ashes might give back rare and potent texts, but most of what survived was carried off when the survivors left.

Inirelte's Tower. The third tallest, built by Prima Inirelte and left empty of laboratories after her death. It was enchanted as her talisman through the Mystery of Hermetic Geometry. On its top floor of three, her sanctum still holds a few old Hermetic texts, kept intact by strong magic and guarded by stronger traps.

The Catacombs. A wide warren of caves under the covenant: specialist laboratories, small libraries, rooms for arcane uses and stranger chambers, and the tombs of the covenant's magi and several Primi of Flambeau, their bodies mummified by the dry air. Some of their ghosts walk here, keys to the covenant's past, though death has blurred and twisted what they remember.

The Shrine of the Aerie. Deep in the Catacombs, the clan's holiest place: a cavern of crystal seams flashing with colour, a waterfall roaring at one end, and carvings made over many generations. Its calm tempts visitors to sit and forget their troubles (a Personality Trait roll, perhaps; it is not magic).

The Aerie Clan. Magic humans who lived here before any wizard; their tales tell of beating off Roman wizards and Carthaginian sorcerers before the sahirs enslaved them. Delendar freed them, and they have served him and his heirs, the Primi of Flambeau, ever since; they wait for a living magus to come and claim the inheritance. They know no life but that of covenfolk and go on as if Val-Negra still thrived. They look drab and almost alike, have classical Latin names and write in Latin. They hold that each generation is reborn from its elders, though nothing proves it. Each adult has Magic Might 10 (Mentem; companions 20), speaks mind to mind with any other Aerie (Silent Speech), and turns invisible when standing still and silent; a typical Black Guard fights with long sword and round shield (Attack +12, Defence +11, Damage +8, Soak +7). They are led by twins always named Romulus, Autocrat of the Interior, who wants Val-Negra kept closed, and Remus, Autocrat of the Exterior, who wants to reach out (Might 33 and 32, each with an Aura of Rightful Authority).

Abaddon of Tytalus. A Living Ghost (Magic Might 50, Mentem), the last magus of Val-Negra, whom the Aerie serve devotedly; one of the most feared necromancers in the Order. His haunt is the whole covenant, and he likes to conjure and possess a strong young body to pass for a living man. He is wary of strangers at first but can come to trust them, give them casting tokens for the Aegis, and ask for help with neglected work or a stronger Aegis; he could anchor a saga of restoring Val-Negra. A true Tytalus, he enjoys puzzling and provoking his guests. Personality: Obsessed +3, Ruthless +2, Eclectic +5; reputed a Necromancer 3 (Hermetic), with Hermetic Prestige 4.

Vis: each Aerie's brain holds 2 pawns of Mentem vis; some of the wild plants in the ruin bear vis, and Astella's garden once yielded vis and herbs of virtue. Unclaimed.

levels.name: The Labyrinthine Caverns
levels.enter: Follow the gorge on past Perdut: the regio begins where the trail starts to wander.
levels.notes: The gorge forks and turns back on itself, and its path never runs the same way twice. Cave mouths open all along it into shifting mazes of dark tunnels that join the regiones running under the Pyrenees. Beasts lost in the maze, or lairing near its mouths, prey on travellers: man-eating ogres, poisonous drakes, warped animals and serpents of fire.

levels.name: The Valley of Mists
levels.enter: Only while mist climbs out of the Tessier, at night and just after dawn.
levels.notes: A silent, choking fog, scalding in one place and icy a few steps on; little that lives moves here. Second Sight shows it crowded with spirits: the ghosts of lost travellers, spiteful imps, river sprites and wretched spirits that no longer recall what they were. Getting out is as easy as finding a gap in the fog (Auram magic makes it trivial); going on to Val-Negra means finding the Circle of Light.

levels.name: The Fortress of Val-Negra
levels.see: Only from inside the Circle of Light: an hour's search, Per + Awareness against 12, and another hour for each failure; then a regio perception roll shows the bridge.
levels.enter: Cross the great stone bridge over the chasm from the Circle of Light.
levels.notes: The Circle of Light is an enchantment on the boundary (MuVi with Perdo and Terram requisites, level 79, constant, Penetration 0, built with the Mystery of Hermetic Architecture and Closed Privacy of the Enchanted Regio) that narrows the way into this level to a lit circle ten paces across; no one outside it can see in. Beyond the bridge stands the fortress, under an Aegis of the Hearth of level 50 (Penetration 25). Its rooms are described in the place's summary.

links.note: Kept, lost or hidden in Val-Negra
Kept, lost or hidden in Val-Negra
Founded by magi who left it; claims its legacy
Took its place as domus magna of House Flambeau

neighbours.secrets:
The Iron Door holds the Adulteration of Flambeau: the magical residue of the Founder's Twilights, built from his mistakes, base desires and failings (an Adulteration as Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults describes them; House Criamon knows of such things). It is not Flambeau, who is long dead or gone into Final Twilight, but it believes it is, and does not understand why it cannot leave. Loose, it would lay the country waste in mad rage. It is a Malignancy of Magic Might 65 (Ignem), Wrathful +5, Proud +3, Hard-Hearted +2, with the Founder's fire spells as powers (Pilum of Fire, Ball of Abysmal Flame, Arc of Fiery Ribbons, a burning aura, any non-ritual Ignem effect up to level 50), flight, a body until sunrise or sunset as a bald, sun-darkened man of nearly sixty in a coarse brown robe, rituals that curse a victim with Deficient Form (Ignem) or Incompatible Arts, and awareness of everything in the fortress's level. It cannot act beyond the door while the ward holds. It hates Moors and sahirs and attacks them on sight. Its full stat block is the book's.

The Diedne archmagi of 1012 broke the door's ancient seal, made by a lost Rite of Fenicil that kept it forever, and released the Adulteration, which destroyed them. The two surviving defenders, both archmagi, overpowered it and closed the door again, but the seal was gone; the round Hermetic ward they cast in its place holds it in, yet breaks if anyone simply opens the door, which is physically easy. This is why the Quaesitors hid the truth and barred the covenant's return. The door probably dates from after Delendos built the Black Tower, by him or another magus; the legend that it is as old as the Aerie, and holds demons, is wrong.

Abaddon was one of the two who resealed the door. He gave up his life to guard it and the covenant forever, watches the ward, and stands ready to recast it. He keeps the Aegis up through the Mystery of Hermetic Empowerment, often by binding the ghosts of former members, who volunteer; hidden laboratories in the Catacombs let him make each Aegis item from lab texts in a season, and his spirits power it two or three times before release. Val-Negra's old wealth, and supplies from the Haruspex, keep him in vis for centuries. His talisman stores many useful spells, and he may know unique Mysteries of spirit magic.

The 'watchers' of Perdut are Aerie who still walk unseen among the villagers now and then. Romulus and Remus are renewed when twins are born: old and young pairs hold a secret rite at the Shrine, and the young emerge with the elders' minds and memories while the elders vanish; Remus holds secret knowledge. Priamitus may have hidden the original scroll of a lost Mercurian ritual somewhere in the covenant.

neighbours.name: The Albigensian Crusade
neighbours.summary:
The war on the southern heretics has run for eleven years. The legate's murder by the Rhône in 1208 brought the crusade; Béziers was sacked and its people slaughtered in 1209, Carcassonne yielded and its viscount died a prisoner, and Simon de Montfort, a minor knight of the Île de France, took the Trencavel lands. Minerve, Termes and Lavaur followed; the massacre at Montgey in 1211 brought down the Tremere covenant of Lariander, and Mistridge fell to Tres's Wizard's War. At Muret in 1213 King Pedro of Aragon died and the southern host broke; Simon entered Toulouse in 1215.

Then the tide turned. Count Raimond VI slipped back into Toulouse in 1217, Simon was killed by a stone from the walls in 1218 (some say from one of Tres's engines), and the royal expedition of 1219 butchered Marmande but failed before Toulouse. In 1220 the count is winning back his county. Amaury de Montfort claims his father's titles, with his mother Alice still a shrewd hand in the war, but his domain is crumbling. There are no borders: castles of either side stand within sight of one another and garrisons of both are scattered across the land.

A saga frame as well as a threat: the crusade played as a war, in which characters of every faith and loyalty meet, change sides and betray one another. Who holds each town in 1220 is in that place's notes.

details.antagonist: The crusaders: Amaury de Montfort, the papal legates, and in time the French crown

stages.title: The count's recovery
stages.clues: Southern lords take back castle after castle, and faidits, the knights the crusade dispossessed, ride home to claim their lands. Unpaid crusader garrisons hold on in isolated towers. Routiers and camp followers rob the roads; a Redcap died of their blows on the Via Domitia.
stages.ignored: The patchwork war grinds on around any covenant in the Toulousain, and both sides come asking for oaths, food and shelter.
stages.stopped: The covenant stays hidden and the fighting passes it by.
stages.turned: A returning faidit, or a crusader captain, owes the covenant his castle, and may pay in land or rights.

stages.title: The old count's death
stages.clues: If history holds, Raimond VI sickens and dies still under the Church's ban, and the clergy will not bury him in consecrated ground. His son Raimond VII, already the south's best captain, takes up the war.
stages.ignored: The son carries on the reconquest with fresh energy.
stages.stopped: The old count is reconciled before he dies, and one bitter grievance of the south is laid to rest.
stages.turned: The covenant wins the young count's goodwill, through healing or counsel, and must answer for it if the Quaesitores hear.

stages.title: The Montfort claim gives way
stages.clues: If history holds, Amaury runs out of silver and men, leaves Carcassonne, and hands his southern claims to the King of France; the Trencavel heir comes home. Deserters from his garrisons sell their swords on the roads.
stages.ignored: The crusaders' domain falls apart, but its claim now rests with a crowned king rather than a struggling heir.
stages.stopped: Amaury finds money and allies, and the war stays a southern affair a while longer.
stages.turned: The covenant gains from the vacuum: a castle, a market or a vis site on land that no lord now holds.

stages.title: The king takes the cross
stages.clues: If history holds, a council of the Church condemns the young count again, the crusade is preached anew across the north, and the French king leads it himself. Town after town submits before his army arrives; Avignon on the Rhône shuts its gates and is besieged all summer, and the king dies on the road home in the autumn.
stages.ignored: The royal host comes down the Rhône; Arelat, spared until now, sees war, and the Coenobium's holdings at Avignon lie under its siege lines.
stages.stopped: The crusade is delayed or turned aside, and the south gains years to make its peace.
stages.turned: The covenant shelters a town or a lord through the siege, or quietly helps the royal army, and is owed by whoever wins.

stages.title: The burning of the fields
stages.clues: If history holds, the king's lieutenant wages a war of attrition, burning crops and uprooting vineyards around Toulouse season after season. The same year the Grand Tribunal meets, and magi of the south carry their quarrels there.
stages.ignored: Hunger, not battle, wears the south down.
stages.stopped: The ravaging is checked and the harvest saved.
stages.turned: The covenant feeds the countryside, and wins its loyalty, at the risk of a charge of interference.

stages.title: The Treaty of Paris
stages.clues: If history holds, the count submits in Paris: his heiress is to marry the king's brother so the county passes to the crown in time, Toulouse loses its walls, a university is founded there to teach sound doctrine, and a council of the Church sets about hunting heresy town by town.
stages.ignored: The south is bound to France. The Perfecti flee to mountain refuges, the Hermetic faidits lose their cause, and the Church's inquisitors begin asking questions.
stages.stopped: The war goes on, or ends on terms that leave the south its own lords.
stages.turned: The covenant has placed itself well with the new order, and gains from the peace.

links.note: His engines may have killed Simon

neighbours.secrets: The book tells the war only to 1219. The stages after 1221 follow history in broad strokes; a troupe that wants the south to win, or the war to end sooner, changes them.

neighbours.name: The Serpent's Venom
neighbours.summary:
A saga frame, the book's central one, and a threat. Dama of Merinita, the Praeco, is the Tribunal's oldest maga: respected, even by the Mercurians, and known to favour women. She founded the Matres and Matrones, a cult that advances women, draws on the Basque folk witches, the region's love of the female saints and its Black Madonnas, and the memory of Eleanor of Aquitaine. She lives apart from Castra Solis in a tower near Mimizan, an eerie and unwelcoming place that she says keeps crusaders away.

Two Presiding Quaesitors have gone in ten years. Senex vanished in 1210 on some errand to a village, and Tibaut, who took his office, died in 1219. Tibaut's filia Beatrice holds the office until the Tribunal of 1221 confirms her, on Dama's suggestion.

details.antagonist: Maju, the Praeco Dama's familiar: a faerie turning into a demon

stages.title: Sins of the Past
stages.clues: At Beatrice's confirmation in 1221 there is talk that Senex met foul play. A Redcap's remains lie by the Via Domitia with a sealed letter. Tibaut's chest waits at Saint Hilaire, and his lab notes in his sanctum. A Quaesitor trained by Senex or Tibaut comes to find the truth; Protendus of Tremere, hunting Tytalan intrigue, stumbles on the Praeco instead and wants Tremere help, for a price in sigils.
stages.ignored: Beatrice is confirmed without knowing, and Dama invites her into the cult before the letter reaches her, making her complicit.
stages.stopped: The truth comes out at Tribunal: Senex's death was lawful, Tibaut's was murder, and the Praeco stands accused.
stages.turned: The characters keep what they know, and hold the most powerful maga of the Tribunal in their debt or their grip.

stages.title: Schemes of the Present
stages.clues: Maju whispers that time is short: Dama's Longevity Ritual is failing, Marie is estranged, Mimizan small beside Oriande's court in the Médoc, and the cult too small to outlive her. She recruits harder among the sorginak and the coastal villages, tests would-be initiates with odd questions, and seeks vis from enchanted items, perhaps through a newly arrived Verditius, which may betray her part in Senex's end.
stages.ignored: Either the cult becomes a quiet Black Madonna devotion that forgets its founder while Dama ages and grows desperate, or she defeats those who pry, Maju becomes a demon and carries her soul to Hell, the sorginak break away from the Order, and the Tribunal suffers another blow.
stages.stopped: Shown the rot in her familiar and convinced that her life has left a legacy after all, Dama is redeemed and helps destroy Maju.
stages.turned: If the investigation is bungled, Maju kills Dama and takes the cult, or turns it on the characters in a hidden war of witches; the characters who survive it hold the cult's secrets.

links.note: Dama's familiar, the demon behind her cult

neighbours.secrets:
Dama killed them both. Senex had turned his eye on her cult and slipped into Mimizan while she was away at an akelarre with the sorginak; she came back early and found him in her sanctum. Her Aegis, her spell Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus and Maju's venom killed him, and Maju, as a drake, ate the body. He had forfeited his immunity by entering her sanctum, so the killing was lawful, but she hid it to keep the Quaesitores away from the cult.

Tibaut found the start of Senex's inquiry in his notes, came to believe him dead, told Beatrice so, and from 1217 looked into the Tribunal's cults. His sealed letter to Beatrice still lies in the satchel of a Redcap who died of a camp followers' ambush on the Via Domitia. Luc of Ara Maxima Nova, after losing a certamen to Tibaut over his questions, told Dama which Arts he had used. She lured Tibaut into an abandoned house near the road to Foix where Maju waited as a viper; he staggered out into the road, crusader knights carried him to the Abbey of Saint Hilaire thinking him a monk, and he died there of the poison. His belongings sit in a locked chest in the abbot's office; the crusaders, deciding he had been a Cathar, came back and raided the abbey. Dama does not know what he told the knights or the monks.

Maju is the real enemy. The Gauls worshipped it as Teutates and drowned captives for it in the lake at Mimizan; among the Basques it wore the face of Sugaar, and Dama still calls it so before them. It bound her spirit as she bound it, and has turned each of her works a little: the cult's upper circle is a coven of tainted witches close to diabolism, and Dama drove her filia Marie away over it. Maju sets women against men and the Black Madonna against the God of the Dominion, and its sins are slowly making it a demon (in its final form a Duke of False Gods, Infernal Might 45, who cloaks the Infernal aura at Mimizan as Magic or Faerie). Dama bought the tacit backing of Alazais and the Coenobium with a secret Longevity Ritual for the Chief Redcap's mundane companion. Her own ritual is failing; she must renew it before 1232.

neighbours.name: The Six Deadly Spirits
neighbours.summary: When the pope laid England and its lands under interdict in 1208, Gascony's churches stood closed for six years, and in the wild country off the pilgrim roads a band of demons took root. Infernal auras are common there still, and in many villages the Dominion holds by day and the Infernal by night; no Divine aura below 7 is older than the interdict.

details.antagonist: Six demons of the deadly sins, loose since the interdict

stages.title: A village gone wrong
stages.clues: A Gascon village near the covenant turns sour: its reeve grows proud, its smith envious, its young men idle, and at night the church feels cold. A handsome stranger advises the best craftsman; a troubadour sings that the war is no one's business.
stages.ignored: The village falls under an Infernal aura, and its dead do not rest.
stages.stopped: The possessed are freed and the demon driven off.
stages.turned: The covenant learns the demon's name and nature, a hold over it, or a clue to the others.

stages.title: The old man of the bridge
stages.clues: Travellers drown at the bridge of St. Thibery, each last seen talking with an old peasant carrying a load of firewood, who offered to mind their goods while they dived for coins glinting in the river.
stages.ignored: The Via Domitia gains a deadly crossing.
stages.stopped: The Old Man is caught counting coins thrown at his feet, his weakness, and banished.
stages.turned: The demon's purse holds three pawns of Vim vis.

stages.title: Gluttony and Wrath in the camps
stages.clues: Atrocities and drunken excess spread in both armies; a garrison near the covenant runs riot, and the cruelty spills onto the countryside.
stages.ignored: The war grows crueller, and the Infernal takes root in the places it scars.
stages.stopped: The two demons are found among the soldiers and cast out.
stages.turned: The covenant uses what it learns to sway a captain, at the price of dealing with the Infernal.

stages.title: The spirits notice the covenant
stages.clues: A companion is advised by a charming stranger; a grog turns idle, another lustful; a magus's craft is praised beyond reason by someone who knows too much of his work.
stages.ignored: One of the covenant is corrupted, or dies unrepentant.
stages.stopped: The tempter is unmasked before it takes hold.
stages.turned: The covenant traps the demon, and learns the others' plans from it.

stages.title: All six descend
stages.clues: If one demon escapes the covenant, it brings the rest: grogs and covenfolk possessed one after another, from within the Aegis. Cenodoxus's Might is high enough to pass many an Aegis.
stages.ignored: The covenant rots from within.
stages.stopped: The six are driven out or destroyed, and Gascony begins to heal.
stages.turned: The covenant earns the Church's gratitude, and its notice.

links.note: Pride and Envy, still in Gascony
Greed, gone to the bridge of St. Thibery

neighbours.secrets: Each demon descends on a community, possesses its leading folk and leads the rest into its own sin until the place lies under an Infernal aura; a host who dies unrepentant comes back as a lesser demon or a ghost. Three are still in Gascony: Cenodoxus Superbia, Lord of Pride and Envy (a Vessel of Iniquity, Infernal Might 40), who plays the muse to craftsmen and spreads envy through whole guilds; Adrian, the Voice of Safety (a Spirit of Deceit, 30), a troubadour preaching the sloth of standing aside from the war; and Julian or Julia, the Tempter of the Way of St. James (15). Greed has gone to the bridge of St. Thibery on the Via Domitia as the Old Man of the Bridge (15), who lures travellers into the river after a phantom treasure. Gluttony and Wrath march with the crusaders in the Narbonnais and the Toulousain, feeding both armies' vices.

neighbours.name: The Procrustean League
neighbours.summary: A short-lived alliance led by Tolomae of Bellaquin, a Cathar sympathiser, that called for open war on the Church to save the Order's holdings in the south. At the Tribunal of 1214 he urged a joint Hermetic answer to the crusade, which would have meant open meddling in mundane and Church affairs; he was thrown out of the debate and swore revenge on the Mercurian conservatives and on the Coenobium, his old covenant. Aedes Mercurii and the Coenobium both renounced the League, Jerbiton declared him orbus in 1216, and he was Marched for repeated interference and slain early in 1218.

details.antagonist: Tolomae's surviving followers, hidden among the faidits

stages.title: Whispers among the faidits
stages.clues: Dispossessed knights speak of a wizard who promises them their lands back; spells strike a crusader garrison with no sigil the Redcaps know.
stages.ignored: The followers gather strength and allies unseen.
stages.stopped: A follower is found out and brought to the Quaesitores.
stages.turned: The covenant finds them first, and decides what to do with what it knows.

stages.title: Tolomae's revenge
stages.clues: Attacks fall on the Mercurians of Aedes Mercurii and on the Coenobium, the two Tolomae swore to punish; each side suspects the other.
stages.ignored: The Tribunal's old rivals turn on each other.
stages.stopped: The true culprits are exposed before blood is spilled.
stages.turned: The covenant brokers a reckoning, and both sides owe it.

stages.title: War on the Church
stages.clues: The League's heirs strike openly at churchmen and crusaders, as Tolomae wanted.
stages.ignored: The Church sees wizards behind the heresy, and the whole Order in the south pays.
stages.stopped: The followers are Marched, and the cause dies with them.
stages.turned: The covenant channels their anger into something the Code allows, and gains desperate allies.

links.note: His old covenant, which renounced him

neighbours.secrets: Tolomae was suspected of the papal legate's murder and fled rather than answer the Quaesitor. Several of his supporters went to other covenants or vanished in the war, and hide among the faidits; some magi fear the cause will return, sharpened by grief. No one knows who they are, which makes it an open case.

neighbours.name: Tolosa Paratge's Civil War
neighbours.summary: The old covenant in the regio beside Toulouse is tearing itself apart over its Cathars. In 1218, sure the city would fall, its leader Augustus, a senior Quaesitor, asked the Gorgiastic Cathar magi to leave for their own safety. Marc, one of them, declared Wizard's War on him and, convinced he was under a demon's sway, killed him in a confused quarrel in the tower; a month later Carolus St. Tropez declared war on Marc, who did not resist, and killed him. Mariola, made leader, did nothing, and the covenant split: the Blacks, who shield the Cathars, hold the regio under Cyprian of Flambeau; the Whites, who would expel them, follow St. Tropez in the city and try to blockade it.

details.antagonist: The White and Black factions of Tolosa Paratge

stages.title: The blockade
stages.clues: Covenfolk of both factions brawl in the streets of Toulouse. Half a dozen grogs and a dozen covenfolk are trapped in the regio, and their friends in the city ask outside magi, or send Redcaps, for help. A book lent to the covenant before the quarrel must be fetched back.
stages.ignored: The siege tightens and the covenant sinks towards Winter.
stages.stopped: A truce lets the trapped covenfolk out.
stages.turned: The covenant becomes a trusted go-between, welcome on both sides of the lake.

stages.title: Allies called in
stages.clues: The Blacks look to Castra Solis, which they think would answer Cyprian, and to Renaud of Stella Durus, Cyprian's filius; the Whites court Stella Durus through Mariola's friendship with Jean Marie. Both seek the Coenobium's weight. A covenant that backs the wrong side may face a Wizard's War.
stages.ignored: The quarrel draws in covenants across the Tribunal.
stages.stopped: The outsiders refuse to take sides.
stages.turned: The covenant chooses a side and is rewarded if it wins.

stages.title: Tribunal or Wizard's War
stages.clues: The Whites must choose between a case at Glanum in 1221 and a fresh Wizard's War to retake the regio.
stages.ignored: New Wizard's Wars are declared, and more magi die.
stages.stopped: A case is brought and the Quaesitores rule on both factions' breaches.
stages.turned: The covenant brings the case itself and shapes the settlement.

stages.title: The lake closes
stages.clues: Open battle reaches the island; the boom on the Garonne is threatened, and with it the regio.
stages.ignored: Tolosa Paratge is destroyed or its regio lost, and Toulouse loses the magi who guarded its spirit.
stages.stopped: The covenant is reconciled and rebuilt under a new leader.
stages.turned: One faction wins with the covenant's help, and the ancient site and its lore are open to its friends.

neighbours.secrets: Both sides are plainly depriving each other of magical resources, which the Code forbids, but no one has brought a case and the Quaesitores have kept out of it, partly from respect. The rest of the Tribunal waits to see what survives. Adam Carpentiere's enchanted boom across the Garonne keeps the weakening regio alive, and the Gorgiastics opposed it. Raimond, a Gorgiastic Good Man, believes he will die by drowning in the Garonne and fears no other death. St. Tropez would rather die striking at the Gorgiastics than wait for a Tribunal to convict him.

neighbours.name: The Coenobium's Hegemony
neighbours.summary: The Coenobium, a league of chapter houses along the Rhône and the coast run mostly by Jerbiton magi and the Tribunal's Redcaps, has long been praised as a model of cooperation. Since it destroyed Fraxinetum in 975 it has gathered most of the magical and mundane resources of the County of Provence, and it smothers any new covenant in its shadow that will not join it as a chapter: none has thrived in southern Provence for over a century. With several covenants lost to the crusade it has grown unopposed, and even old allies are uneasy. It offers help to any petitioner, and everyone knows the help implies annexation.

details.antagonist: The Coenobium Rhodanien and its First Consul, Alazais

stages.title: A generous offer
stages.clues: A new covenant finds its suppliers slow, its Redcap late and its neighbours unfriendly, until a consul of the Coenobium calls with an offer of help.
stages.ignored: The covenant's efforts keep failing, and it grows dependent.
stages.stopped: The covenant finds friends elsewhere and stands alone.
stages.turned: It becomes a chapter house on good terms, with a consul as patron and a path to full membership, or to independence later.

stages.title: Chapters beyond Arelat
stages.clues: The Coenobium courts Stella Durus as a chapter, offers to take the Exiles under its direction, and sponsors magi to reclaim Barbegal or the Alpine sites of Portus Cottiae.
stages.ignored: Chapter houses spring up in the Narbonnais and the Toulousain, and their votes are the Coenobium's.
stages.stopped: The western covenants refuse, and its reach stays in Arelat.
stages.turned: The covenant founds a chapter on the Coenobium's silver.

stages.title: The bloc
stages.clues: At Tribunal the Coenobium and Castra Solis vote together, and a motion against the Praeco is buried without debate.
stages.ignored: Little can stand against the pair; the smaller covenants stop coming, and the Tribunal struggles for a quorum.
stages.stopped: A coalition of the small covenants, perhaps with Aedes Mercurii, checks the bloc.
stages.turned: The covenant learns what the Praeco paid, and uses it against her or the Coenobium.

neighbours.secrets: It allies with Castra Solis and knows the pair can carry most votes, but it also knows that isolating the small covenants risks a Tribunal too thin to be quorate. Its First Consul, Alazais, the Chief Redcap, is rumoured to belong to the Matres and Matrones, and Dama's secret Longevity Ritual for her companion has bought the Coenobium's quiet support for burying a motion when the Praeco needs it.

neighbours.name: The Tribunal at Glanum
neighbours.summary: A saga frame. The Tribunal meets in summer 1221 in the ruins of Glanum, a neutral ground agreed on after the bitter meeting of 1214, which was driven from Toulouse to Castra Solis by de Montfort's army. Midius of Flambeau, the flamen, opens each day masked and robed in the old Mercurian rite, to the scorn of the pious at Castra Solis. The crusade and interference with mundanes will fill the agenda.

stages.title: The Presiding Quaesitor
stages.clues: The first business is Tibaut's successor. Beatrice of Guernicus, his filia, is expected to be confirmed, but she is young, lives in Arelat after quarrelling with Primus Garus, and has no following of her own.
stages.ignored: Beatrice is confirmed, or a rival is chosen, without the covenant.
stages.stopped: The appointment is contested and another Quaesitor named.
stages.turned: The covenant's votes make Beatrice, and she remembers.

stages.title: The faidits' petition
stages.clues: The Hermetic faidits and refugees of the fallen covenants demand licence to defend themselves and win back their power, and want Garus and the milites behind them. The Mercurians, with Ara Maxima Nova, Stella Durus and Miniata Sophia, argue for waiting the war out. The Exiles also want their covenant recognised.
stages.ignored: The vote goes as the great covenants decide.
stages.stopped: Non-interference is upheld and the Exiles are restrained.
stages.turned: The covenant shapes a ruling that lets magi defend their own without making war on the Church.

stages.title: The weight of the Coenobium
stages.clues: Senior magi mutter about the Coenobium's growing power, and watch how its votes and Castra Solis's fall together.
stages.ignored: The hegemony grows.
stages.stopped: A motion curbs its expansion.
stages.turned: The covenant trades its votes to the Coenobium for favours.

stages.title: Tolosa Paratge's case
stages.clues: Someone may at last bring Tolosa Paratge's war before the Tribunal, and both factions lobby every covenant.
stages.ignored: No case is brought, and the war goes on.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal rules and the factions must obey.
stages.turned: The covenant brings the case and frames the ruling.

neighbours.secrets: Rumours at Beatrice's confirmation will hint that Senex was murdered (The Serpent's Venom). If the Tribunal votes to intervene against the crusade, the Pyrenean covenants may walk out for good (Pyrenean Secession).

neighbours.name: The Adulteration of Flambeau
neighbours.summary:
Val-Negra, Flambeau's own covenant and once the largest in the Order, fell as the Schism War was ending and never rose again. The Quaesitores ruled it must not, the domus magna moved to Castra Solis, and even its site in the far south is forgotten: a regio on Mount Perditu, where travellers go astray and return with no memory, if they return at all.

A saga frame as well as a threat: an expedition into the lost covenant, its catacombs, ghosts and Aerie Clan, and perhaps a saga of restoring it against the ban.

details.antagonist: The Adulteration of Flambeau, the Founder's Twilight-born shadow

stages.title: The lost covenant
stages.clues: Someone seeks Val-Negra: Mercurians after Priamitus's scroll of the great road ritual, Flambeau eager to settle which covenant is the true heir, or treasure hunters with an old Tribunal record. Merinita bring back tales of faeries on Mount Perditu.
stages.ignored: Another party finds the way in first.
stages.stopped: The seekers are turned back, and the Quaesitores' ban holds.
stages.turned: The troupe reaches Val-Negra and wins its guardian's trust, and Casting Tokens for its Aegis.

stages.title: The Iron Door
stages.clues: Intruders reach the round chamber beneath the shrine. The Aerie raise the alarm and fight anyone who goes on; carvings on the walls tell of old wars.
stages.ignored: The door is opened, and the ward with it.
stages.stopped: The intruders are stopped, and the ward renewed or strengthened.
stages.turned: The troupe restores a lasting seal, perhaps by finding the lost Rite of Fenicil.

stages.title: The Founder's shadow
stages.clues: Smoke and ash drift from Mount Perditu. A bald, sun-darkened man in a brown robe walks the foothills, smouldering when crossed, and calls himself Flambeau.
stages.ignored: The Adulteration burns its way across the countryside, and the Quaesitores' secret is out.
stages.stopped: It is subdued and shut away again, or destroyed at great cost.
stages.turned: Its twisted memories of the Founder yield secrets of House Flambeau before it is put down.

links.note: its guardian at the Iron Door
the thing behind the Iron Door

neighbours.secrets:
Deep in the mountain a round chamber holds the Iron Door, an iron disc carved as a wheel whose spokes are seven swords, warded against all but the strongest divinations. Since Apromor's time it has been forbidden to touch it. Behind it is the Adulteration of Flambeau: a malignant spirit born of the Founder's Twilights, made of his failings, wants and errors, which believes it is Flambeau. It is Magic Might 65 (Ignem), wrathful and proud, casts the Founder's Pilum of Fire at will, flies on smoke, curses magi with Deficient Ignem or Incompatible Arts, and when furious bursts into flame. Released, it would lay the country waste in rage.

When five Diedne archmagi stormed Val-Negra in 1012 something got out and destroyed them. The two surviving defenders put it back, but the old seal, made by a lost Rite of Fenicil, was gone; their Hermetic ward holds only while the door stays shut, and anyone can open it. The Quaesitores hid the whole affair. Abaddon of Tytalus, one of the two, keeps watch over the door as a Living Ghost.

neighbours.name: Pyrenean Secession
neighbours.summary: The conservative covenants, led by the Mercurians of Aedes Mercurii with Ara Maxima Nova, Stella Durus and Miniata Sophia, want the Order to keep out of the crusade and trust to their isolation. If the Tribunal decides to act against the crusaders and the Church, they may refuse to take part any longer and ask the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to make them a Tribunal of their own: four covenants, the number a new Tribunal needs. Aedes Mercurii already threatened to walk out in 1214, which could have made the meeting invalid, until Tibaut and the Chief Redcap's threat to suspend the Redcaps stopped it.

details.antagonist: The Pyrenean conservatives, led by Aedes Mercurii

stages.title: Intervention at Glanum
stages.clues: The Tribunal votes to act against the crusaders; the Mercurians leave the meeting in anger.
stages.ignored: The conservatives begin to talk of leaving.
stages.stopped: The vote fails, or a compromise keeps them in.
stages.turned: The covenant brokers terms each side can live with, and both remember it.

stages.title: The boycott
stages.clues: The Pyrenean covenants refuse any further discussion with the rest of the Tribunal, and their Redcaps carry letters to the other Tribunals.
stages.ignored: The Tribunal is split in two in all but name.
stages.stopped: Concessions bring them back to the table.
stages.turned: The covenant sides with the bloc, and has its trust.

stages.title: Petition at the Grand Tribunal
stages.clues: With four covenants behind them they ask the Grand Tribunal for their own Tribunal; Bellaquin presses its idea of a Catalan one.
stages.ignored: The Grand Tribunal decides without the covenant.
stages.stopped: The petition fails and the Pyrenees stay Provençal.
stages.turned: A new Tribunal is made in the mountains, with a Code the covenant helped to write.

neighbours.secrets: Bellaquin, for its own reasons, dreams of a Catalan Tribunal, and several of the Tribunal's places lie south of the mountains where the Iberian Tribunal also looks.

characters.name: Mariola

params.group: the count's and the bishop's factions

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Jerbiton, leader of Tolosa Paratge, apprenticed there and fiercely proud of its heritage. After Augustus and Marc died she seemed the one magus both factions could accept, and was pushed into a leadership she never wanted. Her agents have long carried messages between Count Raimond's party and the bishop's, and she knows people in every corner of the city, though she has little sway with the capitouls. A strong Imaginem maga, she failed to act against St. Tropez after he killed Marc, and the covenant fell apart; too proud and inward-looking to ask for help, she has shut herself in her sanctum, sunk in doubt. She corresponds with Jean Marie of Stella Durus, who has fallen for her. Looks about eighty.
characters.secrets: She is rumoured to belong to the Matres & Matrones.

characters.name: Carolus St. Tropez

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Jerbiton, Mariola's former apprentice and still fond of her, leader of the White faction. He passes as a minor southern noble and keeps a small castle and household at Pujol outside the city, owing no liege. A Perdo specialist, he declared Wizard's War on Marc after Marc killed Augustus, letting years of resentment loose; Marc did not defend himself. Fearing the other Gorgiastics, he fled into the city, rallied many grogs and covenfolk to his white banner and swore to drive the heretics from the covenant and then from Toulouse; his Whites now try to blockade the regio, though no new Wizard's War has been declared. His great coup was winning the legate Arnaud Amalric to the southern cause and turning him against the French crown. He believes the Cathars brought God's judgement on the land and that only their destruction will spare it. No Tribunal has convicted him, and he may seek martyrdom attacking the Gorgiastics first. Looks about forty-two.
characters.secrets: Arnaud Amalric does not know St. Tropez is a magus; he thinks the Order a loose fellowship of scholars and natural philosophers. St. Tropez also blames Marc for the crusader knights of Pujol, whom he thinks Marc controlled.

characters.name: Cyprian

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: A Flambeau magus who heads the Black faction, a Perdo Terram specialist and the pater of Renaud of Stella Durus. He has been a troubadour knight and an ardent Seeker after the Tribunal's lost magical secrets, and years posing as a knight errant and unmatched skill at arms made him the Blacks' natural leader. He is devoted to the covenant and to Mariola above all, and belongs to the Cult of Mercury. He is no Cathar, and finds their pacifism and mysticism rather tiresome, but he thinks Bishop Foulques betrayed the Church and his own honour, and St. Tropez's killing of the defenceless Marc and the anarchy after it have made him ready to fight his sodales, if only to defend his home. Looks about seventy-one.

characters.name: Adam Carpentiere

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: A follower of Verditius in the White faction, steeped in Hermetic Architecture, with his sanctum and laboratory in a waterfront lacuna of Magic aura 2 in the city. He cares far more for the city's politics than his covenant's. He owes a great sum to the Jewish moneylenders of Cahors, so Bishop Foulques's railing against Jews and Cathars pleases him, and that alone made him a White. The Gorgiastics opposed his enchanted boom across the Garonne, fearing for the aura, and he has never forgiven them; since the Wizard's Wars he has backed St. Tropez as the covenant's best hope. Looks about sixty-five.

characters.name: Raimond

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Ex Miscellanea, a Gorgiastic Cathar of the Black faction and a sworn Cathar Good Man, though his theurgical faith is far from the Divine belief of ordinary Cathars. He is convinced his soul has passed through many lives, even through these very lives over and over in endless cycles of the world, and means to escape rebirth through Final Twilight and help hold open the way to the refuge outside time. So he acts unpredictably to break the pattern of his past lives, and seeks out Twilight as a way to step outside time. He does not fear dying against the Whites, sure that if he fails now he will win in a later cycle; besides, he knows he is fated to drown in the Garonne, so offensive magic holds no terror for him. Gorgiastic Cathars are prone to Twilight, keep a guardian spirit they call their Genius, and cast quietly. Looks about thirty-nine.

characters.name: Gilbert

abilities.name: Organization Lore: Knights of the Green Stone

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Flambeau, the exiles' leader, born near Marseilles of noble blood, Gently Gifted, and an ardent follower of Apromor's Perdo tradition. Apprenticed late, at the Coenobium, he passed his Gauntlet as a Jerbiton and wandered the Tribunal for years, careless of its politics; his move to House Flambeau earned the Coenobium's undying hatred. Cultured and polished, he is known across the region as a knight and romantic troubadour, and few of the noble ladies who favour him know he is a magus. Long an outsider among magi, he found a purpose when Lariander fell and the Tribunal began to buckle; after Mistridge he saw it coming apart. Love of battle has replaced courtly love, solitude has given him the strength to lead, and he has vowed to defend the Order against all its foes and to cut down anyone who hinders him. Charismatic and unstable, he leads the Knights of the Green Stone here. Looks about forty.
characters.secrets: Few care to test whether his boast of a second Schism War is only talk.

characters.name: Rixenda Mistridge

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Jerbiton, the first exile to settle at Aguilar after Tres destroyed Mistridge, who welcomed Gilbert and the others as they came. Where Gilbert stands for the anger of the wronged, she stands for rebirth: a Mentem maga drawn to dreams and nightmares, she wants the Tribunal's acceptance, not revenge, and thinks the Order's future may lie in hiding from the world. Her calm good sense makes her a real rival to Gilbert. No Cathar, she sympathises with them and writes to some learned Perfectae, though she cannot see why they hold so woman-hating and world-denying a faith, and quietly uses her influence to protect the best women scholars. She was appalled by Marc's war on Augustus and is one of the few magi to have watched Tolosa Paratge's collapse closely. Like the other exiles she has not forgiven Tres, and knows her alliance with Gilbert is a dangerous one. Looks about thirty-eight.

characters.name: Garsenda of Lariander

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Tremere, only a few years past her Gauntlet when Lariander was destroyed; she fled into the forest and somehow lived, the only survivor she knows of. A Seeker after the magical secrets of antiquity, above all those of faerie powers once worshipped as gods, she is now chasing tales of the Drac, dragonish creatures said to haunt the region's rivers, and is troubled by strange dreams. An Imaginem specialist, she dresses as an outlaw rather than a knight, is close to several local demesoilles, and shares their zeal for the poor and oppressed. She sympathises with the Cathars only because she questions every authority by nature, and has no religion. Guilt makes her jumpy and short-tempered with magi she does not know.
characters.secrets: Her part in the Montgey massacre brought the crusaders down on Lariander, and she fears the Order will learn of it. She may be a Knight of the Green Stone, and met Gilbert through an esoteric mystery cult.

characters.name: Popilia

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Ex Miscellanea, a Pharmacopoeian who came to the Order late, after her village cast her out. A midwife and herbalist, she clashed with Sicart of Lavaur, a Perfectus who damned childbirth as the worst of sins and reviled sex and the raising of children; when he attacked her she went at him with a knife and was banished for it. She still broods on it and hates the Cathars, the Gorgiastics included, as fiercely as she resists the northerners, and the crusade has only convinced her the heretics brought this horror on the south. She has three children, two grown and the youngest, Jacquemart, fifteen. Looks about fifty-one.

characters.name: Garus

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Primus of House Flambeau, very old and frail, looking about eighty. English by birth and training, he crossed to Gascony in 1155 straight after Henry married Eleanor of Aquitaine. When Primus Vancasitum vanished late in the twelfth century, Garus won the primacy chiefly through the milites, the Flambeau Hoplites who stayed on at Castra Solis after each war; under him they came to see themselves as knights serving a liege, and his long rule has turned the House toward politics. He has always cared about the politics of the region, more than about the Legion of Mithras, whose inner circle he never joined. He keeps one of the old Redcap lanterns that light the way to Val-Negra. Everyone expects him to die soon, himself included, and Flammarcus of Aedes Mercurii waits for the day.

characters.name: Marcus Minor

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

reputations.name: Mystagogue of the Legion of Mithras (Hermetic)

characters.summary: The covenant's second most senior magus, looking about sixty, named Minor because an elder Marcus, Marcus Major, once lived here too. Pious and magnetic, he is the chief mystagogue of the Legion of Mithras at Castra Solis, and insiders know that he and his followers are the covenant's real leaders. He keeps the Legion's Christian bent, and through him the warrior magi have come to feel like brothers of a holy order of knights.

characters.name: Troya

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: An established maga, looking about forty, who has given her life to magical mounts, horses above all. Her stable is bred and trained to bear Gifted riders, by methods she shares by letter with like-minded magi in Hibernia, and her horses learn charges, leaps and other moves useful to a magus in battle: dashing in to cast a Touch spell or snatch a hair for an Arcane Connection, then away. Many of her spells change horse and rider together. Her horses are said to descend from the stock of Bayard, the magic horse Maugris gave his cousin Renaud de Montauban four centuries ago.

characters.name: Marie of Merinita

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Filia of Dama, who trained her as her only apprentice about a century ago; she looks about forty-five, and sometimes calls herself Marie of France. A famous figure in her House, headstrong and independent, she lives in a manor near Poitiers counted part of Castra Solis though it stands in Normandy's lands, attends the Provençal Tribunal, and works to bring all Aquitaine into it by spreading the language and culture of the south.

She escaped her mater's grip mostly through her devotion to Eleanor of Aquitaine, whom she sees as her twin or her mundane counterpart. She says she rode with Eleanor on the Second Crusade in her bare-breasted Amazon procession, guarding her with her Parma; came home with her after the annulment; followed her to Henry's English court; and wrote romances and fables for its nobles. Since Eleanor died she has come back to Poitou to grieve and turned to Hermetic politics. She has Faerie Blood and the second degree of the Matres and Matrones, which lets her initiate others and lead rites, though she seldom does; she has trained several apprentices, all gone abroad. She says Eleanor was a folk witch who brought secrets home from her uncle's court in the Holy Land. Dama wants her to become a Matron, but Marie thinks of her as a harsh taskmistress; they are cold to each other, and Marie honours Eleanor far more.
characters.secrets: Perhaps none of it happened: Marie may instead have trailed after an Arcadian faerie queen who looks like Eleanor and feeds on the stories told of her. Dama drove her away by putting the cult first and refusing the rites Marie said Eleanor taught her.

characters.name: Beatrice of Guernicus

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 45 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filia of the late Presiding Quaesitor Tibaut, acting in his office and presumed to succeed him at the Tribunal of 1221, though that may be contested and is the first business of the meeting. A troubled woman, she truly means to do right, but amid the crusade and the Tribunal's feuds she is no longer sure what right is. She is young for the office, has won little respect from the factions yet, and would likely hand it to another of her House if a better one came forward. Registered at Castra Solis, she spends all her time in the Arelat, living as the Coenobium's guest at the ruins of Glanum, where she studies the Roman shrines of the cults that flourished there; some say she has fallen out with Garus, others with one of the societies based in the Arelat. She is thought to sympathise with the Matres and Matrones.
characters.secrets: Tibaut told her he believed Senex dead, and sent her sealed letters by an Iberian Redcap who was ambushed by crusader camp followers and died in the wilds by the Via Domitia; the letter is still in his satchel. When Tibaut missed their meeting she took her fears to Dama, who calmly suggested she hold the office until the Tribunal; honoured, she agreed. Dama believes she will not pursue her pater's inquiry and has all but drawn her into the cult.

characters.name: Dama of Merinita

invented_spells.name: Circular Ward Against Faeries
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal.

description.biography:
Stat block printed in Faith & Flame (as 'The Guide'). Its age line reads 193 (apparent 60), which leaves out her 34 years in Twilight; she was born in 993. Longevity Ritual modifier 23 (ritual 15, baetylus 5, living conditions 3); her ritual is failing and must be renewed before 1232. Strength has 1 aging point; Stamina and Quickness have each lost a point to Decrepitude. Soak +5.

Virtues and Flaws the catalog lacks, left off the sheet: the Mystery Virtue Sympathetic Magic and the Flaw Oath (protect women). The Feminine Gift, Venus' Blessing and Dark Magic are Twilight Virtues. Her Driven is to leave a legacy, her Favors are owed to Oriande la Fée, her Fear is of spiders and her Weakness is for women in need. Story Magic, Charm Magic, Sympathetic Magic, her Major Magical Focus (in controlling people), Driven, Favors, Fear and Oath came by Mystery Initiation and Ordeal; Faerie Magic is her House Virtue. The book calls Chthonic Magic 'Cthonic Magic'.

Twilight Scars: three comprehended Twilights before 1061 gave her the Feminine Gift, Venus' Blessing and Dark Magic; her nineteen-year Twilight erased most of her memories before 1001; two later ones, of six and nine years, left her like the popular image of the Virgin, faintly glowing, with auburn hair and ruddy skin.

Spells: she also knows Demon's Eternal Oblivion at level 10. Enigma's Caress is Enigma's Gift but inflicts two Warping Points. Faerie Scourged from Memory is Demon's Eternal Oblivion against Faerie beings. Veil of Haunting Terror is laid along Mimizan's game trail. Faerie Chains of the Familiar Slave (the book calls it Familiar Chains of the Faerie Slave) is her House's spell, by which she bound Maju.

Familiar: Maju, a faerie of the lake at Mimizan (see the Secrets in her summary). Vis: 15 pawns of Faerie Vim in three gold rings, and 25 more within a week through her cult. Equipment: courtier's finery, dagger, four gold rings, the baetylus on a pendant chain, good boots, a walking stick used as a club. Casting sigil: a faint scent of lilies. Voting sigil: an ivory dragon's head gilded in red gold.

Her xp, as the book designed her: 5615, of which 1960 in Arts and 795 in spells; seasons went to a talisman she later sacrificed, three Longevity Rituals, one for Alazais's companion, Mimizan, her apprentice and her Initiation scripts.

characters.summary:
The Praeco of the Tribunal, by custom its eldest magus, born in 993. Twilight has shattered her early memories: she may have been the child of a Basque folk witch and a Viking raider. Her mater was a Greek Merinita and former Thessalian witch who had learned the Hoplite's trade at Val-Negra and Castra Solis and was versed in her House's symbolic and sympathetic mysteries. Dama became her apprentice in 1001, just before the Schism War, and the two hid as guests at the court of Oriande la Fée. Gauntleted in 1016, Dama took the whole path of Story Magic and unwisely swore herself to Oriande's court.

In 1061 her risks threw her into Twilight. Nineteen years later something came back that a Quaesitor confirmed as Dama, though it was more a husk woven of patchwork memory, ambition and desire, glowing faintly like the Virgin in the painted images, with auburn hair and ruddy skin. Her fey oath ran for her natural life, and a faerie prophecy said she would die at seventy, so she came back free of it. A very old man who called himself a childhood friend made her take a farewell gift, a green-black stone the size of a hen's egg he called a baetylus, and charged her to carry it far from the castle and keep it from the one who craved it: it would give Dama vigour, but Oriande would use it as an Orphic Egg for a great apotheosis. Oriande was displeased but could do nothing.

Resolved to leave a legacy of her own rather than her House's, she trained one apprentice, Marie; founded Mimizan; bound Maju, a faerie of the lake, as her familiar with her House's spell; and founded a mystery cult, the Matres and Matrones, devoted to raising up women, which she leads as mystagogue. The cult is obscure but not secret, and a little digging shows she is at its heart. She favours female magi and is a true friend to women. She is openly pagan, which leaves the pious of Castra Solis uneasy about her and gives Aedes Mercurii hope she is fair; even the Mercurians heed her when she speaks. She dislikes visitors, and has grown more secretive, paranoid and ambitious.

She looks an older, handsome Basque woman in rich court dress, silver hair with a trace of auburn pulled into a bun under a Basque shawl, with a fine dagger, gold rings on her fingers and the stone hung from a gold chain, leaning on a walking stick; her faint amber glow shows most at evening, when she seems almost a ghost. A scent of lilies attends her magic. Her voting sigil is an ivory dragon's head gilded in red gold, her father's gift and the only thing she has from before her apprenticeship.
characters.secrets:
Maju is not what it seems. Worshipped by the Gauls as Teutates, who drowned captives for it at the lake's black rock, it later wore the mask of Sugaar among the Basques, then returned to play in Oriande's court, where Dama first saw it. It has bound her spirit as she bound it, and its counsel led her into sin and blasphemy and to the edge of infernalism: it had her build the chthonic sorginak into her cult under the guise of the Black Madonna, so that at its upper levels the Matres and Matrones are a coven of tainted witches close to demonic corruption. Through them it sets women against men and against Christ, and the sins it spreads will soon make it a demon outright (Infernal Might 45, a Duke of False Gods); it already hides the Infernal aura at Mimizan. It appears as a winged sprite, a hare, a dove or, in private, a snake that coils round her throat. See the Serpent's Venom.

In 1210 Senex, Presiding Quaesitor, came to suspect her cult. While she was away at an akelarre he slipped into Mimizan; she came back early and found him in her sanctum. The Aegis, Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus and Maju's viper venom killed him; she stripped his goods and Maju, as a drake, ate the body. Having entered her sanctum uninvited he had forfeited his immunity, so the killing was lawful, but she told no one to keep the cult unseen. His successor Tibaut found the thread in Senex's notes, began probing the Tribunal's cults in 1217, and pressed Luc of Ara Maxima Nova about clergy and pilgrims on the Via Domitia; Luc lost a Certamen to him and told Dama which Arts to avoid. In 1219 she lured Tibaut into an abandoned house near the road to Foix, broke his Parma, and set Maju on him; he staggered into the road and collapsed, and crusader knights, Divinely blessed and proof against her magic, carried him to the Abbey of Saint Hilaire, where he died of the poison. They later took him for a Cathar and raided the abbey. He lies in its cemetery; his belongings sit locked in a chest in the abbot's office. Dama does not know whether he told the knights or the monks anything.

She has never killed a woman. She worries a little that Beatrice is a woman, but thinks she will not follow her pater's trail and has nearly won her for the cult. She bought the tacit support of Alazais and the Coenobium by secretly making a Longevity Ritual for Alazais's mundane companion. Her own ritual is failing: she must renew it before 1232, may sacrifice Maju for its vis, and feels her legacy slipping away. Maju urges her to draw more sorginak in and bend their faith in Mari and Sugaar, and needles her about Marie and about Mimizan's smallness beside Rosefleur. She has taken no more apprentices, as Maju thinks it too risky. If she is shown what her familiar truly is, she may yet be saved; if she falls, Maju means to carry her soul to Hell.

The baetylus holds a shard of the beginning of Creation, perhaps of Sol Invictus or of Cronus. Touching it she adds 5 to her aging rolls and suffers no aging crises; it purifies her and all she touches or eats as the Greater Purifying Touch, so poison cannot harm her; and it gives her visions of danger to herself or the stone, which feed her paranoia. The tale she believes says it fell into the lake of Toulouse and was raised by pagan wizards who later became Diedne, and that Maugris kept it, long-lived by its power, hid with it at Oriande's court in the Schism War, and gave it to her so that he could at last die and so that Oriande, whom he foresaw it would corrupt, would never have it.

characters.name: Rebecca

description.biography:
Stat block printed in Faith & Flame, built with the folk witch rules of Hedge Magic as an Ex Miscellanea sorgina. Age 32 (apparent 32). Soak +2.
