Virtues and Flaws the catalog lacks, left off the sheet: Well-Trained Folk Witch and the Flaw Flawed Folk Witch Gift Opening (Animal Ken). The Feminine Gift, Good Teacher and Venus' Blessing came by Mystery Initiation through her Cabal Legacy; her Proud Flaw by the cult's Initiations. Her Flawed Parma Magica is against Animal. Her folk witch Abilities (Cursing, Dowsing, Flight, Healing, Shapeshifting, Folk Witch Magic Theory) are entered by the book's names; the book calls Shapeshifter 'Shapeshifting'. Sorginak powers are not modelled.

Witch Moon Scar: 5 xp in Cursing. Vis: 15 pawns of Corpus in a string of animal skulls, and her personal source of 5 Corpus a year from afterbirth rendered each spring equinox at a hillside shrine. Equipment: bear, hare, raven, stag and wolf fetishes, clothing, a dagger, pots and gear for brewing potions. Voting sigil: the wolf fetish, won in a fight from a rival sorgina. She dresses as a Basque wise woman, in dark wool with a bright, wide sash, her hair under a shawl.

characters.summary:
A Basque sorgina of House Ex Miscellanea, a folk witch who has sworn the Oath, and the only other resident of Mimizan. Her father found a hoard of Roman gold in their village and spent it quietly on her comfort and schooling, grooming her to marry one of the region's lesser knights; but Dama's coven found her, talked several of her suitors into going on crusade, and took her in. After her apprenticeship she became Dama's chief helper, and she serves her as envoy, messenger and spy, flying and changing shape to travel fast and unseen. She often goes home to fly over the whalers as an albatross, and they follow her gladly as a good omen. She nurses young mothers through childbirth with potions and takes the afterbirth as her fee, rendering it each spring equinox at an old hillside shrine for 5 pawns of Corpus vis, her own source.

She still hopes to find a husband, ideally a young magus of good breeding and character, and would welcome a quick romance and a quicker marriage, for she wants a child soon; a mundane knight or ship's captain might do, but her upbringing, growing power and pride set the bar high. Close to pagan, she sees nothing wrong in the Matres and Matrones: does not all mortal life come from women? She is teaching an apprentice, young Alexa, who helps Dama while Rebecca is away and means to be initiated into Intuition when she joins the cult. Rebecca's voting sigil is a wolf fetish she took in a fight from a rival sorgina.
characters.secrets: She is one of the sorginak Maju is working to corrupt through Dama's cult.

characters.summary: An infamous rusticanus of House Ex Miscellanea, a craft magus born in the Tribunal who came home for revenge, leading two filii and a rabble of outcasts and routiers. He destroyed Mistridge in a Wizard's War in 1209 with magic-armed mercenaries and siege engines of his own making, was narrowly acquitted at the Tribunal of 1214 because grogs may lawfully fight in a Wizard's War, and went into hiding near Bazas. Some suspect the stone that killed Simon de Montfort at Toulouse came from one of his engines.

characters.summary: Priest of Mars at the Dorsum, who looks about seventy-five, styles himself Pontifex Maximus and thinks himself the covenant's leader. Like many at the Dorsum he is a Christian and treats the priesthood as ceremony. He worships the memory of Flambeau the Founder and holds that Castra Solis has corrupted the Founder's story: his research says Flambeau was no Mithraian but a Mercurian who held some of the Order of Mercury's lost rites. Most magi think him overzealous and cannot see why it matters so to him. He burns to become Primus of Flambeau as soon as Garus dies.
characters.secrets: He may be willing to do anything at all to get there.

characters.summary: The senior Tremere of the Tribunal (he looks eighty-three), priest of Pluto on the covenant's council, and said to be a necromancer without equal. He answers, with some reluctance, to the exarch of Iberia, who he thinks resents the House's weakness in Provence. He has trained several apprentices and urges young Tremere to make their names, but the House's last venture, Lariander, vanished twenty years ago, and he suspects the crusaders and the Merinita around Castra Solis. He belongs to the Vexillation of the Golden Thread, a secret Tremere society sworn to foil the schemes of House Tytalus. Though he holds six sigils he mostly stays out of Tribunal politics, abstaining unless his House is touched or a Tremere warns him. He is the likeliest magus to look into the deaths of Senex and Tibaut.
characters.secrets: He acts as an unofficial Quaesitor, tacitly allowed, whose rank and secrecy let him investigate discreetly and by methods Quaesitors would not use; he guards the secret with oaths backed by certamen. He has kept the northern Tytali from gaining a foothold so far, but suspects they now work through the Mithraian Flambeau of Castra Solis.

The other magi respect him and step carefully round him; he seldom comes to council and would rather spend his time among the covenfolk, but authority he chose to claim would be accepted, if grudgingly.

Most of the Dorsum dislike his company and his interests, above all the many tractatus he writes on them, but he is sociable and has a hand in nearly everything the council does, so at Tribunal he is often supported, uncomfortably. He is said to be skilled in Creo and Mentem.

characters.summary:
One of the few priestesses at Aedes and head of the priesthood of Janus, living at the Templum with the other haruspices. She is a Hermetic Haruspex, one of a small band of oracular magi said to have been offered a place in House Flambeau who refused it for Ex Miscellanea. She thinks nothing of the difference between the sexes and blames her lower standing on her House, not on being a woman. She is a pagan and the chief mystagogue of the covenant's Neo-Mercurian branch. She looks fifty-nine.

Her familiar Elias is a magical cat with two mouths, two noses and three eyes, which she believes an aspect of Janus inhabits; she makes a point of including him in all her magic.

He looks forty-one. One of the few at Aedes with no grudge against Castra Solis, he admires and respects Garus, the Flambeau Primus, but the forge obliges him to stay on good terms with his covenant-mates.
characters.secrets: He hides his friendship with Garus, and he admires and secretly loves Dama, the Praeco, and would do nearly anything to protect her.

characters.summary:
Archmage, the oldest magus of the covenant and an immigrant from the Rhine Tribunal, who looks seventy-seven. He drew up the contingency plan that saved Bellaquin and led it through the move. He still keeps distant contact with a few noble friends, far more carefully than before, giving only advice and Longevity Rituals to the two or three closest. He devotes himself to running the covenant smoothly, leaves members wide freedom in their offices, but keeps talking to them about their tasks, which some find tiresome; he is a brother to the older members and a father to the younger.

An old friend of Constantine who has known Antoinette since her birth, he hardly knows the others and sometimes feels a stranger at home; he remembers Bellaquin as a covenant of poets and musicians and misses the troubadours. His magic centres on music (a Minor Magical Focus): spells to make or enrich music, and a necklace that records the wearer's performance and plays it back. His archmage's challenge is a performance that moves him to tears. His sigil: horns faintly sounding a fanfare.

characters.name: Constantine

characters.summary: A merchant and master banker, looking forty-nine, who runs Bellaquin's transfers through a network of trusted contacts built on his travels and his Imaginem magic. An old friend of Valgravian, he sold off and moved old Bellaquin's assets and made the covenant a rich Andorran landowner; he imagined its present shape but leaves management to Valgravian and minds the money. Strict and serious, and daunting to young magi, he grows merry among friends and family, helps his sodales gladly but expects favour for favour, and collects coins, especially from far or ancient lands. Antoinette is his daughter. His sigil is a light dusting of gold on the target or in the air about him.

characters.summary: The covenant's champion, looking forty-two, invited by Valgravian for his name as a skilled fighter and an honourable magus; his Gentle Gift suited Valgravian's vision. He insisted Bellaquin also take in Artemis to help him, recruited the almogavars of the Andorra Company and is their overall commander, and means to give every soldier at least one lesser enchanted device, a task barely begun. A widower whose wife died in childbirth, he brought two children: Michael, unGifted, now captain of the guard, and Carmen, who finished her apprenticeship here, was Gauntleted five years since and has gone from the Tribunal. His sigil leaves a faint taste of ash on the air.

characters.summary: Bellaquin's Guardian, in charge of its security, a Blatantly Gifted Tremere invited at Robert's insistence for her name for dedication and discipline. She looks thirty-three, is strong in Corpus, and is second in command of the Andorra Company, working closely with Captain Michael; the two are drawn to each other and will not admit it, out of duty and propriety. Two guards trained at Coeris, the Danior, never leave her side. Her sigil is a dull ache in the teeth of those she targets or stands near as she casts.
characters.secrets: The Danior may be homunculi of her making.

characters.name: Antoinette

characters.summary: Constantine's daughter (chapter three gives her surname as LeBarre), eight when the first covenant fell, who has known only Andorra and was apprenticed here; she has the Gentle Gift and is a budding Imaginem specialist whose sigil is barely audible whispers. She has long loved Captain Michael in secret, watching him grow into a bold, able man, and has thought of telling him, since she could give him children and her father grandchildren, but fears what Artemis would do. She would seek out a Verditius to arm Michael's soldiers, or a certamen master to teach her to beat Artemis or find the Tremere's weak Arts.
characters.secrets: She also fears Michael will learn of her fling with Carolus of the Rhine Tribunal during a Jerbiton fosterage at Oculus Septentrionalis.

characters.summary: Founder of Miniata Sophia, from Aragon across the mountains, who looks fifty-seven. Soon after her Gauntlet a fellow Criamon at the Cave of Twisting Shadows told her of the painted caves; wanting a new road along her Path and believing the first homes of mankind held old wisdom, she wandered until she found Niaux. She befriended the villagers, who were glad of her help many times, and her skill in Creo, Rego, Corpus and Vim built the ties that keep the covenant so well informed: for two visits a year she gave the Redcap Embeth a Longevity Ritual and boots that work the Leap of Homecoming.

characters.summary: A Mentem specialist from Northumbria who works with ghosts and spirits, and treats them callously, since they will have another chance in the next Cycle. Nominally Christian, he hunts for epiphanies in ancient philosophy, apocrypha, Judaism and Islamic learning, and has begun writing to kabbalists in Arles to work the Tree of Life into his labyrinthine meditations. Bad arthritis plagues him, worst in the winters he spends in Niaux.

characters.summary: Second son of an Aachen merchant, put in a seminary as a boy until a visiting Criamon who could sense the Gift offered him another life. He looks forty, is endlessly curious and a student of languages, and loves his seasons in Niaux, where the children call him Grandfather Hans; his Gentle Gift makes him the village's favourite ambassador. He means to enjoy this life to the full and live as aptly as he can while seeking the Enigma, and is in no hurry along the Path. His Arts are Rego, Imaginem and Terram.

characters.name: Marcella of Bonisagus

characters.summary:
The elder Bonisagus of Stella Durus, far from her native Lancaster; she looks about sixty-three. She believes a genius loci or daimon and a nearby town can live in symbiosis, the people strengthening the spirit, so that vis it makes regularly, too little to be worth hunting, could be gathered; she is working on the spirit of the Aude. Obsessive in research, she keeps strange hours, chases tangents and travels wherever a lead or an expert takes her. She loves talking Hermetic theory with anyone, and at Tribunal is known for trapping listeners with odd trivia until something more urgent rescues them.

She leaves the covenant's necessary chores to Jean Marie and cares only that there is money for supplies. She talked her filia Giacoma into coming back to help her for seven years in return for getting her out of trouble; Giacoma's indiscretions disappoint her. She is a suitable parens for a new magus of the Tribunal.
characters.secrets: She secretly fears that one day she may be unable to protect or rescue her old apprentice. She keeps her progress on the Aude a close secret, and will not risk going to Toulouse to study its spirit, though it would help her.

characters.name: Giacoma of Bonisagus

characters.summary: Filia of Marcella, who ran up a large debt through a Tribunal ruling in Rome and owes vis to a spiteful covenant on the far side of the Adriatic. Her mater offered her a bargain: work with Marcella on the spirit of the Aude three seasons a year for seven years, and get the vis to clear the debt, a share of the findings, and a Longevity Ritual. Somewhat bitter to be back in her mater's laboratory but glad to have escaped, she hopes the work will show a better method of drawing Vim vis out of nature spirits and so find vis in poor regions, which would make her rich, the thing she really cares about. She loves the worldly power of wealth and steers her own research toward it. She looks her age.

characters.name: Renaud of Flambeau

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Filius of Cyprian of Tolosa Paratge, and a petty Norman lord's third son, fostered with an uncle who was a petty knight; he looks about forty. He has fought in Iberia, in the Albigensian Crusade, and in the Third Crusade soon after his Gauntlet. A believer in a sound mind in a sound body, he trains with the grogs as their mercenary captain and is the magus in charge of defences, and his battle record makes him known as a capable warrior and magus.

Close calls with jinn in Iberia and disgust at the nobles leading the crusade left him soured and looking for inspiration, until a talk at Tribunal with Jean Marie about the troubadours brought him here. He hunts Mithraic lore in Roman ruins and the universities and enjoys living at the heart of the troubadours' art; twice he has proposed that the covenant take a troubadour under its patronage, and he may keep one himself despite the risk. He keeps Stella Durus close to Castra Solis and worries for his pater in the Toulouse feud. A suitable parens for a new magus.

characters.name: Jean Marie of Jerbiton

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A follower of Jerbiton in pleasant semi-retirement, who looks about forty-five. Born just outside Marseilles, he goes back every five years, and now and then travels to Paris or on pilgrimage to Compostela or Rome. He advises and helps manage a relative's shipping company, and manages Stella Durus too, keeping it tasteful and observing every rule of Hermetic courtesy and hospitality. His strengths are Intellego, Mentem, Rego and Vim, and his paradoxographia, travel letters full of lies with a prize for the reader who finds the most, are much enjoyed, at Bellaquin above all.

He likes Renaud's idea of a troubadour in the household and thinks of founding a league of magi who love troubadours and courtly love, to help the poets flourish despite the crusade, though he fears it might draw crusaders hunting Cathar refugees among the region's sympathetic nobles. He has lately taken up subtle Imaginem to tell better stories. A suitable parens for a new magus.
characters.secrets: Through letters with Mariola of Tolosa Paratge he has fallen in love with her. He suspects Ducaru's game, since the Tytalus sometimes pumps him for news of the local nobles gathered through his troubadour friends.

characters.name: Ducaru of Tytalus

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A Romanian trained in the Theban Tribunal, who looks about thirty-four and is never seen without his goatskin cap. He joined Stella Durus for his own ends, and most of the Tribunal is very aware of him. His mastery of Mentem serves his purposes, though his expert Vim only makes people suspicious. He listens more than he talks, prefers to make a suggestion and watch what follows, and often acts, especially unexpectedly, just to see the outcome. He does not think himself evil but lets neither morals nor custom limit him.

The least involved in running the covenant, he always helps at the most telling moment. He keeps a chess game going in a Perpignan tavern, where he is beating Etienne of Ara Maxima Nova after months of play, and Redcaps wager on the result.
characters.secrets: He means to work his way into the nobility and broker marriages and alliances from the shadows, and has begun, under a Norman persona; if it became well known he could face charges at Tribunal. He may have helped Ramon Berenguer IV escape the Templars in 1219, and the count's four daughters will one day marry into the royal houses of France, England and Sicily and to Richard of Cornwall; how he picks his matches (divination, eastern prophecy or sharp politics) and what he gains is unknown. He may be conspiring with Isabella of Angoulême to secure her line.

characters.name: Luc of Merinita

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Mystagogue of a splinter of the Merinita branch of the Keepers of a Thousand Tales, a branch now absorbing the ways of the Cult of Heroes (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages), and unofficial leader of Ara Maxima Nova; he looks about fifty-four. A master of Imaginem, Mentem and Vim, obsessed with mysteries, he put off his Longevity Ritual until nearly fifty for fear it would spoil his pursuit of the Dionysian mysteries' sexual side. An inventive genius, thought to have been initiated as an apprentice, he crafts new initiations by blending odd esoterica, faerie tales and encounters, and astrological and natural signs, guided by visions from drinks laced with mandrake or poppy. He neglects the covenant's daily business, to Etienne's annoyance.

His wife Miriam, a failed apprentice, is his lab assistant, fellow cultist and muse; they have two marriageable daughters. He leans on his sister Jeanne in every crisis, feeling only she understands their childhood under a harsh, sometimes cruel deacon in Brittany. He is infatuated with Guillermo. A suitable parens for a new magus.

His goals: to find the Hesperides and steal their apples, the last labours but one of his reenactment, and then pass a lapis manalis he believes he has found into a regio where Cerberus may wait; to leave a lasting legacy for his cult in House Merinita and perhaps the Order, through a fine text (he would seize on the Elysian Ecstasy or Olympian Pact of The Sundered Eagle if he learned of them); and to undo his Longevity Ritual's sterility and father a son who could be his apprentice, the one dream that might make him set aside ascension.
characters.secrets:
He has had many lovers of both sexes during his studies and does not say so, and there may be unknown bastards of his around the Mediterranean.

After Tibaut questioned him hard about trouble with clergy or pilgrims on the Via Domitia and beat him at certamen for the answers, Luc gave only the barest replies and complained of it to Dama, telling her which Arts to expect: that warned her of the investigation.

characters.name: Etienne of Merinita

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: With Luc from the start through a chance fostering, he runs and administers Ara Maxima Nova and receives its visitors, keeping its buildings perfect with near-obsessive care. A specialist in Animal, Herbam, Muto and Rego, stocky, taciturn, dark and sharp-eyed, he looks about forty-three and has the Gentle Gift. He was once Luc's lover and ended it when Luc married Miriam; an active cultist with no wish for its innermost secrets, he simply wants to stay near Luc and help his search. Celibate outside the cult's rites, he loves sweets and chess and finds excuses to go into Perpignan for both, where Ducaru of Stella Durus is beating him in a long tavern game. He buys some slaves for the covenant from Arab merchants, and means to look for an apprentice very soon. A suitable parens for a new magus.

characters.name: Jeanne of Merinita

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Luc's younger sister, who looks about forty-six. Where Etienne is relaxed, she is eager and anxious, weighing everything for advantage. She dislikes Luc's wife Miriam and they argue over the cult's direction; Luc usually finds a middle way that leaves each a little pleased to see the other thwarted.

When her first pater died, the aged Caprican of Oleran (see The Lion and the Lily), in Aquitaine, finished her training as a favour to him; she cares nothing for his Stone Couches or his covenant's leadership, though he may come looking for a reluctant champion for the Apple Mile. Initiated during her training, she wrote to her brother, and the two built the core of their cult. She seeks the Dionysian secrets the fae remember, is the covenant's expert on Arcadia and faerie customs, and keeps winter journals of her faerie encounters for a future summa. A suitable parens for a new magus.

characters.name: Guillermo of Mercere

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A Gifted Mercere from Genoa, the covenant's newest member and the only one from outside France, who looks about thirty-three. Research into Heracles and Hannibal for the Cult of Heroes, plus a lord's mistaken idea about him and the lord's wife, sent him to the Via Domitia, where he kept meeting Luc; after several friendly certamen bouts over ruins and resources, which he lost, and long talks on heroic ascension, Luc invited him into the cult's first initiations. Luc is fascinated by his knowledge of old tales and of the land, and Guillermo feeds the infatuation to learn all he can.

Soon after his Gauntlet he saved a young Tremere, Sagittaire, from bandits, and she taught him the Carvers' school of certamen (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages); he is known for gladly standing champion for any Redcap of the Tribunal who asks. A suitable parens for a new magus.
characters.secrets: His loyalty is to himself alone: made to choose between a great sacrifice for the covenant and his own good, he will choose himself.

characters.name: Alazais of Mercere

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
The Coenobium's First Consul and the Provençal Chief Redcap, unGifted, looking about twenty-seven thanks to a lasting Longevity Ritual. She claims descent from Helen of Troy, and from Mercere himself through his granddaughter, which wins her respect among Redcaps and Jerbiton alike. She wears a classical actor's tragic mask and takes it off only before magi or her lover, an unGifted folk witch allied to the covenant; rumour, which no magus confirms or denies, says a spurned suitor scarred her face with acid.

Under her the Coenobium has taken in more non-Jerbiton magi as long-term guests and adopted lesser hedge wizards as nominal Redcaps. She plays the humble manager, urging the Jerbiton to chase beauty and leave the running of the covenant to supposed inferiors. In 1214 she helped avert the Tribunal's collapse by threatening to suspend every Redcap service. She is rumoured to belong to the Matres and Matrones. She owns the inn of St Cyprian at Arles.
characters.secrets: Her lover's longevity was Dama's work, done at great cost, and it ties Alazais to the Praeco. She quietly steers every vote of the council while seeming never to cast one.

links.note: Made the Longevity Ritual of Alazais's lover

characters.name: Nicodemus Ex Miscellanea

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A senior magus who looks sixty-three, once a Jerbiton enchanted by the beauty of Roman waterworks, until Twilight scars in his youth left him with a Blatant Gift. Obsessed with Aquam magic, unable to live the tasteful life among mundanes, and estranged from his gently Gifted colleagues, he reluctantly moved to House Ex Miscellanea; he is still a nominal consul, though most find his ways unbecoming. River folk and Redcaps respect him warily and know him as a hermit on the shore under the Pont St Bénezet, where his laboratory opens below the second pier.

He is working to fold the Atlantean magic of his lineage into standard Hermetic theory. Alazais sees him caring less and less for what his housemates expect, and suspects Warping from his experiments is wearing down his sanity.

characters.name: Marcus d'Les Baux, the Balthazar

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
An aggressive young scion of the lords of Baux, looking thirty-five, known in his family as the wizard Balthazar and the current Hermetic heir of the Balthazarine line, which claims descent from the wise king. His sigil includes the Christmas star of his family's arms. The book names him of House Tytalus, the House that Baux scions of poor taste often end in after a Jerbiton apprenticeship.

The late Chief Quaesitor warned him for meddling openly in mundane affairs for his family and his friends in the Church, above all the abbot of St André. He keeps his seat as consul but may not act as a patron until he shows he can be more discreet about his nepotism. His cousin Hugh III of Baux, Viscount of Marseille, deals with the Coenobium through him. At least two younger Balthazarine magi of junior branches exist, and Marcus may see any of them as rivals.

characters.name: Pola the Sophist

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A maga who looks about fifty, of a lineage begun by a Jerbiton who had been a Gorgiastic, one of those who left House Criamon rejecting its teaching on the Enigma; over time the line became a wandering tradition of rhetoricians and advocates schooled in Gorgias and the Sophists, and some of its younger members have been taken into House Tytalus on merit. A fine speaker, she holds debate an expression of beauty and pushes it as a better way to settle disputes than certamen or Wizard's War.

Of all the consuls she is the likeliest patron for a visitor. Nominally in charge of the Avignon holdings, she oversees the Jerbiton apprentices passing through on their Itinerarium to or from Eboris in Paris.

characters.name: Xiphos filia Damocles

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A disgraced master hoplite of Terram from beyond the Tribunal, looking about fifty-four, expelled from House Guernicus for repeated conduct unworthy of a hoplite. At Primus Andru's unexpected insistence House Jerbiton grudgingly took her in and gave her a chance to reform, on terms that seem to bind her to use her talents to keep the Coenobium stable; thanks to her, her gentler housemates pursue Beauty and Taste with little trouble from magical threats. She claims descent from a legendary Guernicus Terrae-magus, Adamantius, and has nearly total mastery of metal and blades.

Her parens Damocles, a disgraced magus, killed Argentius in a mundane duel when he was Auriel Blake; she and Argentius are now unlikely friends. Chapter three's list of possible parentes calls her line 'Damocles of the Coenobium, raised Guernicus, now Jerbiton'.
characters.secrets: The exact terms of her pardon are unknown.

characters.name: Lavandarius the Pralician

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
The covenant's go-between with its hedge wizard allies, looking thirty-eight: a Gifted student of a local herbalist tradition taken as second apprentice by his Pralician mater. His lineage brought the region's hedge wizards into the covenant, with Alazais's backing, a policy the northern Tribunals, Normandy and the Rhine above all, think wildly unorthodox. One of the few non-Jerbiton consuls, he is never made a visitor's patron but answers for the stronger hedge magicians who come to the Coenobium's towns.

He carries on his mater's slow work to bring herbalists' folk practice into standard Hermetic theory. His familiar is a common asp he found among the Hyères lavender.

characters.name: Argentius of Mercere

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
The Invited Redcap, looking forty-one, living a second life. As Auriel Blake, weapon-master of Valnastium, he seemed killed by the disgraced magus Damocles in a mundane duel, then was brought back by a miracle of the greater relic of St Michael in his sword's pommel. Alazais took him in as a Redcap of the Coenobium. Still coming to terms with his return, he keeps apart from covenfolk who hold him in awe and fear, and has struck up an odd friendship with his killer's former apprentice, Xiphos.

His resurrection woke the latent powers of his Heroes' Birthright, giving him remarkable command of swords and other blades, and magi cannot decide whether he counts as a hedge magician or a true Redcap, however odd. He believes, perhaps rightly, that his sword is the Sword of Ares that Attila bore as the Scourge of God, and lets no one examine it.

characters.name: Bubulcus

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. The book gives no age, nor anything to judge one by: 50 is the default for a magus of unknown age.

characters.summary: A diminutive Bjornaer, nominally a guest of the Coenobium, who lives on the edge of Trinquetaille but spends most of his time roaming the Camargue on his bull, his animal companion, usually in his egret heartbeast form. The more sociable of its two Bjornaer; he knows of the Great Stallion and the wild horses but seldom deals with them. A possible parens for Bjornaer characters.

characters.summary: A Bjornaer guest of the Coenobium living on the edge of Trinquetaille, of a line of African diviners, whose heartbeast is a greater flamingo. He spends at least a season a year in his North African homeland or travelling through dreams, and has little contact with the horses of the Camargue. A possible parens for Bjornaer characters.

characters.name: Calais filius Septentrio

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age, nor anything to judge one by: 50 is the default for a magus of unknown age.

characters.summary: A Bonisagus of the Rhine, guest of the Coenobium, who calls himself Master of the Winds, one of the specialists in narrow, powerful magic the covenant invites. Drawn by Ventoux's spirits, he made a sanctum in a cave just below the summit to persuade the daimon there to take him as its Spirit Votary.
characters.secrets: The Faerie lord Mistrau has sealed the spirits' regio with Calais inside, still fighting Ventoux's furious servants; his hosts expected him back last season and are growing worried.

characters.name: Aloysius Porphyri

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age, nor anything to judge one by: 50 is the default for a magus of unknown age.

characters.summary: A retired Redcap and unGifted alchemist who runs the Toulon chapter on the site of old Telo Martius, oversees the harvest of murex and kermes, runs one of the dye works of the factory outside the town, and takes the rare Imaginem vis from the shells and beetles.

characters.name: Jorin

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. The book gives no age, nor anything to judge one by: 50 is the default for a magus of unknown age.

characters.summary: A retired Redcap and former Rhone boatman who keeps the door of the chapel of St Nicholas on the Pont St Bénezet, where St Bénezet lies, and reports to the Coenobium.

characters.name: Ahmad ibn Nasr

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: A Tytalus magus the Tribunal does not know of.
characters.secrets: Leader of the pirates of Fraxinetum Redux, looking forty-three, a direct descendant of the raider covenant's founder, and a master of sea magic, jinn and water elementals. He may have been partly taught by a Hermetic sahir of al-Andalus and learned non-Hermetic mysteries from faerie jinn. His familiar is a mighty sea-dwelling 'afrit who claims to be a prince of an undersea jinn tribe near Gibraltar, defeated by Ahmad in his self-taught initiation script.

characters.name: Aucassin of Tytalus

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age, nor anything to judge one by: 50 is the default for a magus of unknown age.

characters.summary: A Tytalus magus, an orphan raised by a peregrinator of the Rhine and born at Beaucaire, who does not come to Tribunal and is thought by many to have vanished, perhaps after training an apprentice.
characters.secrets:
Back in his birthplace after his Gauntlet, he was drawn to a weak Magic aura round a disused well in the old market of Beaucaire and found beneath it the underwater regio web under the Rhone and the Drac, where he built his sanctum. Styling himself 'Aucassin le Draconnet', he revived the Drac legend to cover his search for an apprentice and his forcible recruitment of servants. For years he has kept up a Persona as Rene of Dragonianum, a prosperous merchant boss of Beaucaire, steering its council with craft and low-level Mentem magic, dealing as Rene with the Coenobium's Redcaps and hedge allies but never meeting a Gifted magus, and never working open magic in town.

Over twenty years he has learned that his Mythic Blood comes from the Drac of old, and the cave paintings of his regio make up a Mystery script to turn him into a true elder drac; beyond a portal to the Magic Realm aligned to Imaginem sleeps the dragon Vestige whose legacy he would claim when he understands the rites better. About ten years ago he kidnapped children round Beaucaire and kept a sickly Gifted boy who seems to share his blood, 'Le Petit', whom he trains as an apprentice; the boy is wasting from a magical illness Aucassin cannot heal, and he may come to magi disguised as a poor washerwoman to beg a cure. His agents in the boatmen's guild of Beaucaire and Arles spy and enforce for him and keep the ferry's toll steep; he leaves Redcaps alone, though one of his thugs lately humiliated a messenger of the Coenobium.

characters.name: Romualdus

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age, nor anything to judge one by: 50 is the default for a magus of unknown age.

characters.summary: A former Jerbiton magus, now Brother Thomas, a novice at the Grande Chartreuse. Repelled by the pagan remnants and decaying culture of the Order, he has given up active Hermetic life and shuns his former sodales. He no longer works ordinary Hermetic magic and seeks God through a more ascetic use of his Gift, hoping to found a new, prayer-based tradition of holy magic.
characters.secrets: He has found that Brother Jude, a young novice, holds True Faith and the Gift, and fears the Order will claim him.

characters.name: Fraxinus of Portus Termini

description.biography: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age, nor anything to judge one by: 50 is the default for a magus of unknown age.

characters.summary: A Guernicus magus the book names only among possible parentes, of Portus Termini: the hidden covenant in the caves of the Verdon Gorge that the spirit masters of Elisii Campi tried to found after the Coenobium drove them from the Alyscamps. It failed before the next Tribunal and was never registered, and contact was lost soon after. Where he lives now is unknown.

books.name: The library of Tolosa Paratge
books.description: The library of one of the Tribunal's oldest covenants, gathered since the Order's first generation and rich, one may suppose, in spirit lore from its Diedne past and in Occitan poetry from its patronage of troubadours; the book names none of its books. With the Blacks holding the island and the Whites working in the city, neither faction can freely use what the other holds. A valuable text lent before the split is somewhere inside, and its owners may send someone to fetch it.

books.name: The library of the Ostal des Exiles
books.description: Hardly a library at all: the exiles' books burned with Mistridge, Lariander and the other fallen covenants, and only what each magus carried out survives. The book names no books; a covenant that could offer texts would win the exiles' gratitude.

books.name: The library of Castra Solis
books.description: The domus magna's library, strong in military subjects: the warfare of magi, Hoplite tactics, and the lore of the House's many wars. Faith & Flame names none of its books (Houses of Hermes: Societates describes it). Hidden stairs lead from it to the chambers behind the mithraeum.

books.name: The library of Tres' Band
books.description: Whatever books the band keeps travel with it or lie in its scattered sancta; the book names none. The rusticani are a craft tradition, and their lore of magical weapons and siege engines is their treasure.

books.name: Set the Stones of the Via (casting notes)
books.description: Notes and details for casting the great Mercurian ritual that lays down a via mercuria of enchanted Roman milestones (a non-Hermetic ritual, Effect level 36, a season's work needing 36 pawns of vis and 36 pounds of silver in materials). Kept in the Templum. As a source of Insight for integrating True Mercurian Road Magic it adds 6 to the roll (Ancient Magic). Another copy may be in Fenicil's library at Magvillus, and Priamitus's original scroll may be hidden in Val-Negra.

books.name: Link the Rent Path
books.description: A copy of the lesser Mercurian ritual (ReTe(Cr), Ease Factor 18) that joins separate viae mercuriae, ties a new lapis mercurius into a network, or replaces one lost milestone; kept in the Templum and unread for centuries, the old roads being broken. Adds 3 as a source of Insight into True Mercurian Road Magic.

books.name: The library of Aedes Mercurii
books.description: The covenant's library, inherited in part from Val-Negra's halls; the book names no titles beyond the Mercurian rituals. Malfortis has written many of its books, and Ricardus fills it with tractatus most of the Dorsum find distasteful. Berezi the Redcap brings books for the western magi from the Roman Tribunal.

books.name: The library of Bellaquin
books.description: What the survivors carried from the Chateau de Penne in 1202, and what two decades of wealth have added; the book names no books. Valgravian's own spells to make and enhance music would be found here as Lab Texts, and Stella Durus sends Jean Marie's paradoxographia and letters on gossip and courtly love.

books.name: The library of Stella Durus
books.description: The book names no books here. The collection reflects its magi: two Bonisagi's work on genii loci, daimons and spirit vis; Renaud's Mithraic lore gathered from ruins and universities; and Jean Marie's strengths in Intellego, Mentem, Rego and Vim, on which he writes tractatus as prizes for his paradoxographia.

books.name: Jean Marie's Paradoxographia
books.author: Jean Marie of Jerbiton
books.description: Letters of travel marvels Jean Marie writes about his journeys, especially his visit every five years to his birthplace near Marseilles, salted with lies. He sends them to a list of magi, Bellaquin's among them, and gives vis or a tractatus on Intellego, Mentem, Rego or Vim to whoever spots the most falsehoods.

books.name: The library of Ara Maxima Nova
books.description: The book names no books here. Its magi gather every text, carving and work of art on Heracles and his labours, notes from their pilgrimages to St. Stephen of the Carriages in Rome and from searches of Durenmar, Alexandria, Constantinople, Paris and Montpellier for the Hesperides, and Luc's experiments in cult rites. Luc wants to write an excellent text of his cult's teachings to pass, carefully, to sympathetic magi.

books.name: Jeanne's Winter Journals of the Fae
books.author: Jeanne of Merinita
books.description: Every winter Jeanne writes down her dealings with faeries that year, meaning one day to work them up into an authoritative summa on Faerie Lore.

books.name: The libraries of the Coenobium
books.description: The book names no books. With no shared roster or common household, each consul keeps his own collection in his townhouse or sanctum, and the Mercer House at Arles holds the Redcaps' records; a lost Merinita trove of Faerie books lies at Caturigomagus among the ruins of Portus Cottiae, and the covenant would sponsor its recovery.

creatures.name: The Spirit of Tolosa

powers.name: Sturdy Walls of Toulouse
powers.description: Mends a breach in the city walls with stone that holds only until the next sunrise or sunset, then crumbles away and leaves the gap.

powers.name: The Silent Counsel
powers.description: Quietly steers a body of people, such as the bishop or the capitouls in session, toward what is best for the city as a whole.

powers.name: Human Shape
powers.description: Takes bodily form until the next sunrise or sunset as an unremarkable townsman of the lower orders, still unsettling to be near because of its Gift.

powers.name: Grant Blessing of the City
powers.description: Makes its chosen one prosper, granting Ways of Toulouse until the spirit takes it back; the Might spent stays spent until then.

powers.name: Oath Swearing
powers.description: Works only on the steps of Saint-Pierre des Cuisines, where counts and capitouls swear to the people (a tiny Magic aura of 1). If it penetrates, the oath binds: breaking it, even in secret, sets mostly false rumours running through the county and gives the oathbreaker the Minor Flaw Infamous.

creatures.appearance: To Second Sight, a damp mist or a figure of no clear sex made of water and pond reeds. At night it may sit in human form as a fisherman on Adam Carpentiere's river barrage, glad to talk, though little it says makes sense to mortals.
creatures.notes: The genius loci of Toulouse, answering only to the name Tolosa. The book gives its Size as not applicable. Its Virtues include Ways of the Land and Servant of the Land (Toulouse), Anchored to the Land (Toulouse) and Inoffensive to the Magic Realm. It has grown much weaker since the conquest by de Montfort; the covenant's regio lives or dies with the city's prosperity and culture.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 37

creatures.name: Cenodoxus Superbia, Lord of Pride and Envy
creatures.order: Lord of the Vessels of Iniquity

powers.name: Form of Wickedness
powers.description: Its order's version of Coagulation: a material body with no shape or size, sin made visible, which drives envious onlookers to indulge their envy until they drop.

powers.name: Form of Man
powers.description: Once embodied, takes any human shape, and drops it at will.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Imposes the Obsession of Pride or Envy, for 1 to 3 points.

powers.name: Contagious Obsession
powers.description: One point per victim. Whoever falls to its Envy carries it on: anyone hurt by the victim's new vice must resist it in turn or become a carrier too, up to the points spent.

powers.name: Grant the Master's Potential
powers.description: A Ritual: raises the Characteristic behind the target's craft to +3, or by 1 if that is better (as Great Characteristic). Usually lent and taken back when a condition set at the gift is broken; given for good, it costs the demon Might and leaves the target Tainted with Evil.

powers.name: Grant the Master's Insight
powers.description: A Ritual: +2 to the target's craft Ability, as Puissant Ability and on top of it, lent or given on the same terms as the Master's Potential.

powers.name: Shroud the Stench of the Pit
powers.description: Variable cost. Makes another power or aura seem Magic, Faerie or wholly mundane, hiding it even from Sense Holiness and Unholiness, for the cost (or magnitude) of what it hides and as long as that lasts.

creatures.appearance: A handsome, fittingly dressed man or woman, whichever suits the victim, always with a dagger at the belt and fine tools of the victim's own trade.
creatures.notes: It plays muse to a craftsman, feeding his pride while sowing envy among those around him, until whole guilds are corrupted; a dagger left lying about invites murder. Its Might lets it slip through many Aegises, and it would happily join a Verditius's forge companions.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 52

creatures.name: Adrian, the Voice of Safety

reputations.name: The Convincing Silver Tongue of Doubt (Infernal)

powers.name: Change Form
powers.description: Takes any human shape from Size -2 to +2, most often a troubadour with a guitar.

powers.name: Trust of the Innocent
powers.description: The target sets judgment aside and believes one plausible lie until shown otherwise; an Intelligence roll against 6 resists.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Imposes the Obsession of Acedia or Sloth, for 1 to 3 points.

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Builds a body over 30 rounds of manifesting; dissolves it with a round's concentration.

powers.name: Forked Tongue of the Serpent
powers.description: The target believes any lie, however absurd, until he repeats it to someone and hears how foolish it sounds; an hourly Intelligence roll against 9, from an hour after, also breaks it.

powers.name: The Serpent's Oracle
powers.description: Duplicates any non-Ritual Intellego spell, or glimpses the immediate consequences of one future act.

powers.name: Strangle the Noble Endeavor
powers.description: Gives a flawless moral and scriptural argument for its point, usually that going on crusade ruins one's loved ones. Intelligence + Theology against 9, first a day later and then monthly, sees through it; someone else may explain the flaw and roll for the victim.

creatures.appearance: A handsome troubadour or lovely trobairitz wandering the country, carrying news and playing for peasant and lord alike.
creatures.notes: It tells of atrocities done in the Narbonnais and overseas in faith's name and talks people out of joining either the Crusade or the Cathars' defence: the sloth of standing aside. It wanders Gascony.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 54

creatures.name: Julian/Julia, the Tempter of the Way of St. James
creatures.weakness: cannot harm those who have already lost a love

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Takes a material body, and drops it at will.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Imposes the Obsession of Betraying Lust, for 1 to 3 points.

powers.name: Harness the Wind
powers.description: Flies from one place to another, until journey's end or dawn; it keeps what it carries, unlike a demon that simply dissolves and re-forms elsewhere.

powers.name: Hag Ride
powers.description: Rides a victim for a night: awake but helpless, he loses a long-term Fatigue level and recovers none that night, and can move again at dawn.

powers.name: Mutable Gender
powers.description: Shifts at will to any man's or woman's form; Julian is most often a black-haired, roguish young man in pilgrim's clothes.

creatures.appearance: A lively young man or woman of about twenty, richly but suggestively dressed in deep blues and browns, hanging on the victim's every word.
creatures.notes: An incubus or succubus. It preys on pilgrims along the Way of St. James, haunting the Blaye ferry and the crowds of Bordeaux.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 55

creatures.name: Oriande la Fée

powers.name: Call of the Kept
powers.description: Non-Hermetic: cues one of her faerie allies to appear and act as she bids.

powers.name: Caress of the Lethe
powers.description: Whoever she touches forgets his mortal life until he sees some object, or kind of object, tied to his home.

powers.name: Dream's Undeniable Invitation
powers.description: Puts a person within earshot to sleep.

powers.name: Enthralling Sound
powers.description: Her storytelling stirs, or heightens, one emotion in everyone listening; a stress roll on a fitting Personality Trait against 9 shakes it off.

powers.name: Extended Glamour
powers.description: Constant: takes over a mundane place and makes it part of her faerie kingdom.

powers.name: Focus Power (Plants within her realm)
powers.description: Up to 10 points: any Herbam effect up to tenth magnitude, with 10 Intricacy points spent on Initiative.

powers.name: On the Breath of the Wind
powers.description: Becomes a whirling breeze of the season's leaves until she chooses to take her own shape again.

powers.name: The Price of Impertinence
powers.description: Turns a person within earshot into a small woodland beast (squirrel, hare, fawn, hedgehog, polecat) until a condition she sets is met.

creatures.equipment: A glass-bladed dagger, which she sometimes gives a knight to use within her lands, where it becomes whatever weapon he wants; faeries know it as her token.
creatures.appearance: A beautiful, olive-skinned woman with moss-grown wooden antlers in wild, flower-threaded hair and amber eyes cold with arrogance, dressed in leaves and cobweb lace, trailing fireflies or snowflakes. The land grows lovelier in the season's way where she walks.
creatures.notes: Faerie queen of the lands from the Gironde to the Pyrenees and the Camargue. Faerie Might 60 within her demesne. Her Place of Power is the Médoc; her Personal Powers and Restricted Might (Storm) are as printed. Once honoured as a form of Sirona, she now plays the capricious challenger of knights and pilgrims, taking hostages and treasures and making them win them back, and loses interest in those who become faeries. Maugris and Dama have both stayed at her court.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 57

creatures.name: Unicorn

powers.name: Righteous Fury
powers.description: Wreathed in soft white light, its hooves and horn turn razor-keen with holy power: +5 to all Attack and Damage.

powers.name: Sense Virginity
powers.description: Looking into someone's eyes, it knows whether they are a virgin.

vis.where: Divinely aligned, in its horn (the alicorn)

creatures.appearance: A charger fit for a king, but with a goat's cloven hooves and beard, a lion's tail and a slender spiral horn.
creatures.notes: Built with the Magic rules but turned to the Divine: its Divine Animal and Divine Master Virtues (not in the catalog) work as Magic Animal and Magical Master. It spends Confidence instead of Fatigue on its Purifying Touch, though the book also prints Fatigue levels for it. Its Baneful Circumstances and Weakness are virgin women. Natural weapon: alicorn (Init +2, Atk +3, Def +2, Dam +3). Seen at the edge of the woods on the moors of Bazas, where shepherds take it as a sign of three safe days.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 59

creatures.name: Matagot
creatures.how_many: many, around the ruins of Nemetannais

powers.name: Quid Pro Quo
powers.description: A Ritual Power: makes a hidden hoard of coins worth about 20 Mythic Pounds, under a house or in a foundation, and doles it out when its family behaves as it likes. The coins copy a local coin it knows, or bear a strange design. Using it lowers its Might Score until it spends a season in a Magic aura of 3 or eats 15 pawns of Animal vis.

powers.name: Wages of Greed
powers.description: Racks a person with pain that keeps him from his daily work without wounding him; kept for those who will not let it go.

creatures.appearance: A big, dark calico cat flecked with gold, with tufted ears and cruel dark eyes. A kind of magical creature in its own right, not a line of magic cats.
creatures.notes: Its Vow: it serves whoever first feeds it until that person dies or frees it. Said to descend from the familiars of Nemetannais's Diedne magi; the country round La Romieu teems with them.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 62

creatures.name: Lou Carcolh

reputations.name: The Terrible Monster which Eats Travelers (Local Area)

powers.name: Viscous Travel
powers.description: Slides over any ground, unhindered by brambles, wreckage or rubble smaller than itself.

powers.name: Grasping Tentacles
powers.description: Shoots out a tentacle to strike up to 100 paces away with no penalty for the distance; each tentacle is a fresh use.

powers.name: Sense the Quivering Prey
powers.description: Feels the shapes of creatures through the air with its tentacles: crude, and blind to whether a body lives.

creatures.appearance: A vast snail with a dragon's head, a beard of a score of tentacles that reach impossibly far, and a mouth of teeth as long as a forearm; its lumpy shell and pebbled hide turn most blades, and it leaves a trail of thick slime.
creatures.notes: Its Ferocity is for trying to eat people, its Homing Instinct for its cavern and its Compulsion is to eat people. Natural weapons: fangs (Init 0, Atk +4, Def +2, Dam +5), tentacle (Init 0, Atk +5, Def +3, Dam +4). It keeps near its cave in the hills by Bayonne, eating pilgrims mostly; the Sorginak watch it and sometimes lead troublemakers to it.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 63

creatures.name: Sarda Whale
creatures.appearance: A huge, odd fish with a sweet smell from its great mouth, thick pebbled skin instead of scales, and a tail that lies flat.
creatures.notes: A mundane beast. Natural weapon: tail (Init 0, Atk +4, Def +2, Dam +5). Ill-tempered, it smashes or overturns the boats of fishermen who harass it. The whalers of Bayonne hunt it; the bones of a Whale of Virtue hold Animal vis and its baleen Aquam vis.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 66

creatures.name: The Serpent (Maju)
creatures.weakness: cannot harm those who have given alms that day

powers.name: Change Form
powers.description: Takes any humanoid shape from Size -2 to +2, often a troubadour with a guitar or a little winged sprite.

powers.name: Shapeshifter
powers.description: Takes any beast's shape from Size -2 to +2, fabulous ones included; most often a dove, a hare or a snake.

powers.name: A Pretty Cloak to Wrap it Within
powers.description: Up to 9 points: any Imaginem effect up to ninth magnitude.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Imposes Cruelty, Greed or Pride, for 1 to 3 points.

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Builds a body over 45 rounds of manifesting; dissolves it with a round's concentration.

powers.name: Lend Senses
powers.description: Lends its hearing or sight to someone it touches, indefinitely, until the eavesdropper witnesses an act of religious devotion.

powers.name: Shroud the Stench of the Pit
powers.description: Variable cost. Makes another power or aura seem Magic, Faerie or mundane, even to Sense Holiness and Unholiness, for the cost (or magnitude) of what it hides. It keeps Mimizan's Infernal aura cloaked, so it normally has only 42 Might Points to spend.

powers.name: Wealth of Nations
powers.description: Fetches riches worth up to 45 pounds of gold, of any kind valued for itself, not made but taken from wherever corrupts most: a distant treasury or a bystander's purse.

powers.name: His Master's Voice
powers.description: Variable cost. Summons other demons or corrupt beasts to it, a Might Point for each point of their Infernal Might, without any control over them.

powers.name: The Serpent's Oracle
powers.description: Duplicates any non-Ritual Intellego spell, or glimpses the immediate consequences of one future act.

creatures.appearance: As Dama's familiar, usually a small winged faerie sprite, or a hare, snake or dove as suits; in private a snake coiled about her, teasing her with the threat of strangling.
creatures.notes: Dama of Merinita's familiar, called Sugaar among the Basques. Once a Gaulish god, it is sliding wholly into the Infernal as it plays a long game to corrupt both Church and Order through Dama's cult. It waited as a viper when Dama ambushed the Quaesitor Tibaut, and its venom killed him.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 72

creatures.name: Pyrene the Spectre

powers.name: Invisibility
powers.description: Turns invisible at will, though Second Sight still sees her.

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Takes on a solid body.

creatures.appearance: A pale, ghostly, achingly beautiful black-haired woman with mangled lower legs, bloody feet and a tear-stained face, in nothing but a torn linen shift.
creatures.notes: The ghost of the nymph Heracles seduced, torn apart by beasts and buried under the cairn the mountains grew from. Her Homing Instinct is for the boulder at the vis site; she also has Master of Magic Creatures (not in the catalog). The printed Invisibility notes 25 levels against its PeIm 15 effect. On the night of her death she weeps at the cairn until dawn.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 80

creatures.name: Old Man of the Bridge: The Tempter of St. Thibery
creatures.weakness: it can do nothing until it has counted coins thrown on the ground into its purse

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Takes a material body, and drops it at will.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Imposes the Obsession of Greed, for 1 to 3 points.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: 1 point to enter a sleeper's dream, 5 for a waking vision, of life in desperate poverty: a Brave roll against 9 or the victim is terrified and loses a long-term Fatigue level.

powers.name: Change Form
powers.description: Takes any human or animal shape at will; it may become a raven, or make its bundle of firewood vanish.

powers.name: Trove Just Beyond Reach
powers.description: A phantom strongbox spilling gold and silver into the riverbed in plain view of the bridge, in water that looks calm, clear and deep enough to dive into.

powers.name: Rushing Wages of Greed
powers.description: Churns the water into a fierce current with an undertow: Swim rolls at -6 to escape, or the swimmer begins to drown.

creatures.appearance: A wizened old peasant with a great bundle of firewood on his back, a cane and a lantern.
creatures.notes: The demon of Greed among the Six Deadly Spirits. It offers to mind travellers' goods while they dive for the phantom treasure, for half the haul, then drowns them.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 100

creatures.name: The Jinn Corsair, Howling Knife of the Dunes

params.ward: the person it has agreed to serve
Name: Howling Knife of the Dunes

powers.name: Sirocco's Form
powers.description: Becomes a whirling cyclone of gritty desert wind, able to carry one person inside it.

powers.name: Sense the Living Treasure
powers.description: Senses where the person is whose arcane connection he holds, the distance and direction growing clearer the longer he concentrates.

powers.name: Scimitar of Blazing Fury
powers.description: Sheathes his blade in white fire: +10 damage.

powers.name: Conceal the Precious Charge
powers.description: Makes someone he touches invisible to ordinary sight whatever they do, though they still cast a shadow.

creatures.equipment: His scimitar (his External Vis: weightless, and its bearer gains Puissant Single Weapon), fine clothes and whatever his work needs.
creatures.appearance: A handsome, grinning Maghrebi pirate with a brand on his left cheek, dressed in rich cloth, with a fine scimitar that looks like glass in the morning light.
creatures.notes: His abilities are Pretenses. His Infiltrator Virtue mimics Branded Criminal; failing a mission drives him to Fury; he is Pious in Islam. Hired by mortals as a bodyguard, he takes the duty proudly and has lost a charge only twice, once to a dragon and once to a magus. He has a bargain with a corsair who raids the Gulf of Lion; the book prints him with Stella Durus.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 107

creatures.name: Drac, Lesser
creatures.how_many: a kind haunting the Rhone and its tributaries

powers.name: Crafter of Illusion
powers.description: 0 to 5 points: any Creo or Rego Imaginem effect of fourth magnitude or less, for its magnitude in Might, mostly to lure prey (a Focus Power).

powers.name: Transform into Human
powers.description: Shrinks from its great natural size to a human's.

powers.name: Gift of the Drac
powers.description: Someone it has grappled breathes freely underwater until they come up in its air-filled lair or escape to the bank.

creatures.appearance: In its true shape a greenish-black worm, long and sinuous, with webbed legs like a flamingo's and stubby fin-like wings of blue lace.
creatures.notes: Faerie Might +10 more at its Place of Power, the Rhone near Beaucaire. Its Major Flaw is Cruel (not in the catalog); its Focus Power is Crafter of Illusion, its Greater Power Gift of the Drac and its Personal Power Transform into Human. The Bite includes +3 for its crushing jaws, which open weakly: a Grapple can hold them shut. A young adult; it lures washerwomen, children and vagrants into its lair and feeds on the fear its stories spread. Civilised dracs living among men as boatmen, washerwomen or merchants lack Monstrous Appearance and take Infiltrator and Dark Secret instead.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 116

creatures.name: A Small Tarasque

powers.name: Unnatural Flight
powers.description: Flies, tirelessly, on wings that ought not to lift it.

powers.name: Breath of Flame
powers.description: A gout of fire 3 paces by 3 by 9 long: stress die +25 damage to all within.

creatures.appearance: A scaly winged ox some fifteen paces long, with a roughly reptilian lion's head, six legs ending in hooked talons, a tortoise's shell, a leathery tail and sword-like teeth; grey smoke drifts from its nostrils and mouth.
creatures.notes: Kin of the great Tarasque. Its Baneful Circumstances and Weakness are sincere displays of holiness; hymns are said to mesmerise it. The book's design notes give Unnatural Flight as a 25-level Personal Power and Breath of Flame as a 50-level Greater Power against the 15 and 40 levels of their effects.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 120

creatures.name: The Ogre Under the Bridge

params.ward: Payment: those who pay the toll

reputations.name: Ravenous Guardian of the Pont Flavian (Narbonnais)

powers.name: Stone from the Loam
powers.description: Pulls a throwing stone out of natural earth.

powers.name: Seeming of the Menhir
powers.description: Looks like a great boulder or standing stone that fits the land.

powers.name: Stealth through the Grass
powers.description: Moves without a sound, though its voice, thrown rocks and blows are heard as usual.

vis.where: in the skull netted at its belt

creatures.equipment: A tree-stump club with knotted roots for spikes; a sack of badly cooked mutton, half-empty casks of poor beer or wine and throwing stones; a skull in a net (its External Vis, weightless, granting its bearer Tough).
creatures.appearance: A huge, brutish man with clawed hands and a tusked boar's head, forearms stained rust-brown to the elbow, in a ragged hide loincloth with a saddle girth for a belt, and heads in various states of rot hanging from his waist.
creatures.notes: Faerie Might 30 at its Place of Power, the Pont Flavian. No Fatigue levels are printed. Its abilities are Pretenses. Its Traditional Ward is payment: it cannot harm those who pay its toll.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 121

creatures.name: Abaddon of Tytalus, the Living Ghost
creatures.notes: Archmagus of House Tytalus, a Living Ghost and great necromancer; the book prints only his Might, traits and reputations (see The Mysteries: Revised Edition for Hermetic spirit magic). One of the two who subdued the Adulteration and resealed the Iron Door, he guards it forever and keeps the Aegis over Val-Negra, empowering items with the willing ghosts of its magi. He haunts the whole covenant, usually in a strong young body he conjures and possesses, and is a teasing, befuddling host who may trust visitors with Aegis tokens. The Aerie Clan serve him.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 139

creatures.name: The Adulteration of Flambeau

powers.name: Arc of Fiery Ribbons
powers.description: As the spell: a dozen ribbons of fire fanning out over sixty degrees, +10 damage. Mastered (Fast Cast, Multiple Casting, Penetration).

powers.name: Aura of the Avenger
powers.description: Cloaks it in flame that burns whatever it touches for +10 damage.

powers.name: Aura of Enlightenment
powers.description: Shines as bright as the noon sun.

powers.name: Authority of Ignem
powers.description: 1 to 10 points, Init less the points spent: any non-Ritual Ignem effect up to 50th level, a point per magnitude (a Focus Power).

powers.name: Ball of Abysmal Flame
powers.description: A ball of fire at one target for +30 damage; mastered (Fast Cast, Multiple Casting, Penetration).

powers.name: Eidolon
powers.description: A single illusory figure, seen and heard, that moves and speaks at its bidding for as long as it wants.

powers.name: Curse of Ash
powers.description: A non-Hermetic Ritual Power: inflicts Deficient Form (Ignem). Made permanent, the cost comes off its Might Score; otherwise the points return when it lifts the Flaw.

powers.name: Curse of Cinders
powers.description: A non-Hermetic Ritual Power: inflicts Incompatible Arts (CrIg, ReIg), on the same terms as the Curse of Ash.

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Takes bodily form until the next sunrise or sunset as a sun-darkened old man in a rough brown robe, still unsettling because of its Gift.

powers.name: Ghost Touch
powers.description: Variable cost, Init less the points spent: moves loose objects, 5 pounds for a point and double for each more; hurled, they do +5 damage a point and must penetrate. It cannot reach past the Iron Door while the door holds (a Focus Power).

powers.name: Pilum of Fire
powers.description: The Founder's signature jet of flame, +15 damage; mastered (Fast Cast, Multiple Casting, Penetration).

powers.name: Presence
powers.description: Knows everything that happens in Val-Negra's innermost regio, but can touch nothing beyond the Iron Door while the ward holds.

powers.name: Smoke on the Wind
powers.description: Flies any way it wills by concentrating; if distracted it loses control but stays aloft.

creatures.appearance: A deeply tanned, bald man of nearly sixty, who smoulders, smokes and sheds ash as he grows angry and bursts into flame when ready to kill.
creatures.notes: A Malignancy: magical wreckage from the Founder Flambeau's Twilights, built from his mistakes, base desires and failings, which truly believes it is Flambeau. Its Improved Recovery is listed as (65). It mostly takes human form, or deals through its Eidolon. It hates Moors and sahirs and attacks them on sight; bewildered by its prison, it keeps trying to get out. Loosed, it would lay the land waste in pure wrath.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 140

creatures.name: Aerie Guard
creatures.how_many: the Aerie Clan; this is a soldier of the Black Guard

params.power: Silent Speech of the Aerie Clan

powers.name: Silent Speech of the Aerie Clan
powers.description: Speaks mind to mind with any other Aerie within the reach of its 'voice', as loud or soft as it chooses. Restricted to the clan; between kin its Penetration is multiplied by 6, so a typical Aerie reaches 40, enough to speak with Romulus and Remus.

powers.name: Invisibility of Silent Standing
powers.description: Standing quietly for a few moments, it fades into its surroundings until it moves or speaks, aloud or in silent speech; takes a round to start, then Init +0. Elders can stay hidden longer, even moving.

creatures.equipment: Long sword, round shield, partial chain mail.
creatures.appearance: Drab, dull and easy to overlook; the Aerie look nearly identical, differing only by sex and age.
creatures.notes: The template for every member of the clan: Covenant Upbringing always, an Affinity for the role's main Ability, and adjusted Characteristics and Abilities; grogs have Might 10 and companions 20 with more Qualities; children and youths have 240 fewer experience points, elders 360 more. A weaver woman, for instance, is Covenfolk with Affinity with Craft: Weaving, Gossip and Fear of the Outside World. Their leaders, the twins Romulus (Might 33) and Remus (32), add Aura of Rightful Authority (0 points, Init -2, Mentem, ReMe 20, Voice/Conc/Ind). The clan has served Val-Negra's masters for generations and now serves Abaddon.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 142

source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal, by Atlas Games, content under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 licence; summarised, not quoted.

mariola.name: Mariola
mariola.summary: Of House Jerbiton, leader of Tolosa Paratge, apprenticed there and fiercely proud of its heritage. After Augustus and Marc died she seemed the one magus both factions could accept, and was pushed into a leadership she never wanted. Her agents have long carried messages between Count Raimond's party and the bishop's, and she knows people in every corner of the city, though she has little sway with the capitouls. A strong Imaginem maga, she failed to act against St. Tropez after he killed Marc, and the covenant fell apart; too proud and inward-looking to ask for help, she has shut herself in her sanctum, sunk in doubt. She corresponds with Jean Marie of Stella Durus, who has fallen for her. Looks about eighty.
mariola.secrets: She is rumoured to belong to the Matres & Matrones.

carolus_st_tropez.name: Carolus St. Tropez
carolus_st_tropez.summary: Of House Jerbiton, Mariola's former apprentice and still fond of her, leader of the White faction. He passes as a minor southern noble and keeps a small castle and household at Pujol outside the city, owing no liege. A Perdo specialist, he declared Wizard's War on Marc after Marc killed Augustus, letting years of resentment loose; Marc did not defend himself. Fearing the other Gorgiastics, he fled into the city, rallied many grogs and covenfolk to his white banner and swore to drive the heretics from the covenant and then from Toulouse; his Whites now try to blockade the regio, though no new Wizard's War has been declared. His great coup was winning the legate Arnaud Amalric to the southern cause and turning him against the French crown. He believes the Cathars brought God's judgement on the land and that only their destruction will spare it. No Tribunal has convicted him, and he may seek martyrdom attacking the Gorgiastics first. Looks about forty-two.
carolus_st_tropez.secrets: Arnaud Amalric does not know St. Tropez is a magus; he thinks the Order a loose fellowship of scholars and natural philosophers. St. Tropez also blames Marc for the crusader knights of Pujol, whom he thinks Marc controlled.

cyprian.name: Cyprian
cyprian.summary: A Flambeau magus who heads the Black faction, a Perdo Terram specialist and the pater of Renaud of Stella Durus. He has been a troubadour knight and an ardent Seeker after the Tribunal's lost magical secrets, and years posing as a knight errant and unmatched skill at arms made him the Blacks' natural leader. He is devoted to the covenant and to Mariola above all, and belongs to the Cult of Mercury. He is no Cathar, and finds their pacifism and mysticism rather tiresome, but he thinks Bishop Foulques betrayed the Church and his own honour, and St. Tropez's killing of the defenceless Marc and the anarchy after it have made him ready to fight his sodales, if only to defend his home. Looks about seventy-one.

adam_carpentiere.name: Adam Carpentiere
adam_carpentiere.summary: A follower of Verditius in the White faction, steeped in Hermetic Architecture, with his sanctum and laboratory in a waterfront lacuna of Magic aura 2 in the city. He cares far more for the city's politics than his covenant's. He owes a great sum to the Jewish moneylenders of Cahors, so Bishop Foulques's railing against Jews and Cathars pleases him, and that alone made him a White. The Gorgiastics opposed his enchanted boom across the Garonne, fearing for the aura, and he has never forgiven them; since the Wizard's Wars he has backed St. Tropez as the covenant's best hope. Looks about sixty-five.

raimond.name: Raimond
raimond.summary: Of House Ex Miscellanea, a Gorgiastic Cathar of the Black faction and a sworn Cathar Good Man, though his theurgical faith is far from the Divine belief of ordinary Cathars. He is convinced his soul has passed through many lives, even through these very lives over and over in endless cycles of the world, and means to escape rebirth through Final Twilight and help hold open the way to the refuge outside time. So he acts unpredictably to break the pattern of his past lives, and seeks out Twilight as a way to step outside time. He does not fear dying against the Whites, sure that if he fails now he will win in a later cycle; besides, he knows he is fated to drown in the Garonne, so offensive magic holds no terror for him. Gorgiastic Cathars are prone to Twilight, keep a guardian spirit they call their Genius, and cast quietly. Looks about thirty-nine.

gilbert.name: Gilbert
gilbert.summary: Of House Flambeau, the exiles' leader, born near Marseilles of noble blood, Gently Gifted, and an ardent follower of Apromor's Perdo tradition. Apprenticed late, at the Coenobium, he passed his Gauntlet as a Jerbiton and wandered the Tribunal for years, careless of its politics; his move to House Flambeau earned the Coenobium's undying hatred. Cultured and polished, he is known across the region as a knight and romantic troubadour, and few of the noble ladies who favour him know he is a magus. Long an outsider among magi, he found a purpose when Lariander fell and the Tribunal began to buckle; after Mistridge he saw it coming apart. Love of battle has replaced courtly love, solitude has given him the strength to lead, and he has vowed to defend the Order against all its foes and to cut down anyone who hinders him. Charismatic and unstable, he leads the Knights of the Green Stone here. Looks about forty.
gilbert.secrets: Few care to test whether his boast of a second Schism War is only talk.

rixenda_mistridge.name: Rixenda Mistridge
rixenda_mistridge.summary: Of House Jerbiton, the first exile to settle at Aguilar after Tres destroyed Mistridge, who welcomed Gilbert and the others as they came. Where Gilbert stands for the anger of the wronged, she stands for rebirth: a Mentem maga drawn to dreams and nightmares, she wants the Tribunal's acceptance, not revenge, and thinks the Order's future may lie in hiding from the world. Her calm good sense makes her a real rival to Gilbert. No Cathar, she sympathises with them and writes to some learned Perfectae, though she cannot see why they hold so woman-hating and world-denying a faith, and quietly uses her influence to protect the best women scholars.
