She was appalled by Marc's war on Augustus and is one of the few magi to have watched Tolosa Paratge's collapse closely. Like the other exiles she has not forgiven Tres, and knows her alliance with Gilbert is a dangerous one. Looks about thirty-eight.

garsenda_of_lariander.name: Garsenda of Lariander
garsenda_of_lariander.summary: Of House Tremere, only a few years past her Gauntlet when Lariander was destroyed; she fled into the forest and somehow lived, the only survivor she knows of. A Seeker after the magical secrets of antiquity, above all those of faerie powers once worshipped as gods, she is now chasing tales of the Drac, dragonish creatures said to haunt the region's rivers, and is troubled by strange dreams. An Imaginem specialist, she dresses as an outlaw rather than a knight, is close to several local demesoilles, and shares their zeal for the poor and oppressed. She sympathises with the Cathars only because she questions every authority by nature, and has no religion. Guilt makes her jumpy and short-tempered with magi she does not know.
garsenda_of_lariander.secrets: Her part in the Montgey massacre brought the crusaders down on Lariander, and she fears the Order will learn of it. She may be a Knight of the Green Stone, and met Gilbert through an esoteric mystery cult.

popilia.name: Popilia
popilia.summary: Of House Ex Miscellanea, a Pharmacopoeian who came to the Order late, after her village cast her out. A midwife and herbalist, she clashed with Sicart of Lavaur, a Perfectus who damned childbirth as the worst of sins and reviled sex and the raising of children; when he attacked her she went at him with a knife and was banished for it. She still broods on it and hates the Cathars, the Gorgiastics included, as fiercely as she resists the northerners, and the crusade has only convinced her the heretics brought this horror on the south. She has three children, two grown and the youngest, Jacquemart, fifteen. Looks about fifty-one.

garus.name: Garus
garus.summary: Primus of House Flambeau, very old and frail, looking about eighty. English by birth and training, he crossed to Gascony in 1155 straight after Henry married Eleanor of Aquitaine. When Primus Vancasitum vanished late in the twelfth century, Garus won the primacy chiefly through the milites, the Flambeau Hoplites who stayed on at Castra Solis after each war; under him they came to see themselves as knights serving a liege, and his long rule has turned the House toward politics. He has always cared about the politics of the region, more than about the Legion of Mithras, whose inner circle he never joined. He keeps one of the old Redcap lanterns that light the way to Val-Negra. Everyone expects him to die soon, himself included, and Flammarcus of Aedes Mercurii waits for the day.

marcus_minor.name: Marcus Minor
marcus_minor.summary: The covenant's second most senior magus, looking about sixty, named Minor because an elder Marcus, Marcus Major, once lived here too. Pious and magnetic, he is the chief mystagogue of the Legion of Mithras at Castra Solis, and insiders know that he and his followers are the covenant's real leaders. He keeps the Legion's Christian bent, and through him the warrior magi have come to feel like brothers of a holy order of knights.

troya.name: Troya
troya.summary: An established maga, looking about forty, who has given her life to magical mounts, horses above all. Her stable is bred and trained to bear Gifted riders, by methods she shares by letter with like-minded magi in Hibernia, and her horses learn charges, leaps and other moves useful to a magus in battle: dashing in to cast a Touch spell or snatch a hair for an Arcane Connection, then away. Many of her spells change horse and rider together. Her horses are said to descend from the stock of Bayard, the magic horse Maugris gave his cousin Renaud de Montauban four centuries ago.

marie_of_merinita.name: Marie of Merinita
marie_of_merinita.summary:
Filia of Dama, who trained her as her only apprentice about a century ago; she looks about forty-five, and sometimes calls herself Marie of France. A famous figure in her House, headstrong and independent, she lives in a manor near Poitiers counted part of Castra Solis though it stands in Normandy's lands, attends the Provençal Tribunal, and works to bring all Aquitaine into it by spreading the language and culture of the south.

She escaped her mater's grip mostly through her devotion to Eleanor of Aquitaine, whom she sees as her twin or her mundane counterpart. She says she rode with Eleanor on the Second Crusade in her bare-breasted Amazon procession, guarding her with her Parma; came home with her after the annulment; followed her to Henry's English court; and wrote romances and fables for its nobles. Since Eleanor died she has come back to Poitou to grieve and turned to Hermetic politics. She has Faerie Blood and the second degree of the Matres and Matrones, which lets her initiate others and lead rites, though she seldom does; she has trained several apprentices, all gone abroad. She says Eleanor was a folk witch who brought secrets home from her uncle's court in the Holy Land. Dama wants her to become a Matron, but Marie thinks of her as a harsh taskmistress; they are cold to each other, and Marie honours Eleanor far more.
marie_of_merinita.secrets: Perhaps none of it happened: Marie may instead have trailed after an Arcadian faerie queen who looks like Eleanor and feeds on the stories told of her. Dama drove her away by putting the cult first and refusing the rites Marie said Eleanor taught her.

beatrice_of_guernicus.name: Beatrice of Guernicus
beatrice_of_guernicus.summary: Filia of the late Presiding Quaesitor Tibaut, acting in his office and presumed to succeed him at the Tribunal of 1221, though that may be contested and is the first business of the meeting. A troubled woman, she truly means to do right, but amid the crusade and the Tribunal's feuds she is no longer sure what right is. She is young for the office, has won little respect from the factions yet, and would likely hand it to another of her House if a better one came forward. Registered at Castra Solis, she spends all her time in the Arelat, living as the Coenobium's guest at the ruins of Glanum, where she studies the Roman shrines of the cults that flourished there; some say she has fallen out with Garus, others with one of the societies based in the Arelat. She is thought to sympathise with the Matres and Matrones.
beatrice_of_guernicus.secrets: Tibaut told her he believed Senex dead, and sent her sealed letters by an Iberian Redcap who was ambushed by crusader camp followers and died in the wilds by the Via Domitia; the letter is still in his satchel. When Tibaut missed their meeting she took her fears to Dama, who calmly suggested she hold the office until the Tribunal; honoured, she agreed. Dama believes she will not pursue her pater's inquiry and has all but drawn her into the cult.

tres.name: Tres
tres.summary: An infamous rusticanus of House Ex Miscellanea, a craft magus born in the Tribunal who came home for revenge, leading two filii and a rabble of outcasts and routiers. He destroyed Mistridge in a Wizard's War in 1209 with magic-armed mercenaries and siege engines of his own making, was narrowly acquitted at the Tribunal of 1214 because grogs may lawfully fight in a Wizard's War, and went into hiding near Bazas. Some suspect the stone that killed Simon de Montfort at Toulouse came from one of his engines.

flammarcus.name: Flammarcus
flammarcus.summary: Priest of Mars at the Dorsum, who looks about seventy-five, styles himself Pontifex Maximus and thinks himself the covenant's leader. Like many at the Dorsum he is a Christian and treats the priesthood as ceremony. He worships the memory of Flambeau the Founder and holds that Castra Solis has corrupted the Founder's story: his research says Flambeau was no Mithraian but a Mercurian who held some of the Order of Mercury's lost rites. Most magi think him overzealous and cannot see why it matters so to him. He burns to become Primus of Flambeau as soon as Garus dies.
flammarcus.secrets: He may be willing to do anything at all to get there.

protendus.name: Protendus
protendus.summary: The senior Tremere of the Tribunal (he looks eighty-three), priest of Pluto on the covenant's council, and said to be a necromancer without equal. He answers, with some reluctance, to the exarch of Iberia, who he thinks resents the House's weakness in Provence. He has trained several apprentices and urges young Tremere to make their names, but the House's last venture, Lariander, vanished twenty years ago, and he suspects the crusaders and the Merinita around Castra Solis. He belongs to the Vexillation of the Golden Thread, a secret Tremere society sworn to foil the schemes of House Tytalus. Though he holds six sigils he mostly stays out of Tribunal politics, abstaining unless his House is touched or a Tremere warns him. He is the likeliest magus to look into the deaths of Senex and Tibaut.
protendus.secrets: He acts as an unofficial Quaesitor, tacitly allowed, whose rank and secrecy let him investigate discreetly and by methods Quaesitors would not use; he guards the secret with oaths backed by certamen. He has kept the northern Tytali from gaining a foothold so far, but suspects they now work through the Mithraian Flambeau of Castra Solis.

ophilio.name: Ophilio
ophilio.summary: A Gifted Mercere of the Templum, looking eighty-five, long the High Priest of Mercury and now retired, and one of his House's longevity specialists. The other magi respect him and step carefully round him; he seldom comes to council and would rather spend his time among the covenfolk, but authority he chose to claim would be accepted, if grudgingly.

midius.name: Midius
midius.summary: High Priest of Mercury, keeper of the Templum and flamen of the Provençal Tribunal, who opens each day of its meetings with the Cult's rite; he looks about fifty. After many years under Ophilio in the temple he still feels himself the old magus's subordinate and longs to impress him, and he attends Tribunal in Ophilio's place.

pila.name: Pila
pila.summary: Priest of Mars at the Dorsum, in charge of the covenant's defences, which she takes very seriously, fanatically some would say. She stands firmly behind Flammarcus and his version of the Founder's story, counts herself a true Hoplite in the old sense of the word, and goes into battle armed like a Greek foot soldier; otherwise she seems mild and unremarkable, looking about seventy-nine.

malfortis.name: Malfortis
malfortis.summary: Another priest of Mars, though no warmonger: an excellent teacher and a strong writer who has filled the library with books, and who answers every letter at length, if seldom warmly. He backs Flammarcus's view of the Founder. Unusually for a Flambeau he fights with his bare hands, and he specialises in Corpus. He looks forty-four.

ricardus.name: Ricardus
ricardus.summary: Priest of Bacchus at the Dorsum, looking forty-two, openly homosexual and rumoured to have lusty tastes. Most of the Dorsum dislike his company and his interests, above all the many tractatus he writes on them, but he is sociable and has a hand in nearly everything the council does, so at Tribunal he is often supported, uncomfortably. He is said to be skilled in Creo and Mentem.

aintza.name: Aintza
aintza.summary:
One of the few priestesses at Aedes and head of the priesthood of Janus, living at the Templum with the other haruspices. She is a Hermetic Haruspex, one of a small band of oracular magi said to have been offered a place in House Flambeau who refused it for Ex Miscellanea. She thinks nothing of the difference between the sexes and blames her lower standing on her House, not on being a woman. She is a pagan and the chief mystagogue of the covenant's Neo-Mercurian branch. She looks fifty-nine.

Her familiar Elias is a magical cat with two mouths, two noses and three eyes, which she believes an aspect of Janus inhabits; she makes a point of including him in all her magic.

ruberus.name: Ruberus
ruberus.summary: Priest of Vulcan and keeper of the forge of Hephaestus deep in the Dorsum, and head of the Confraternity of Roland, Verditius magi who make magic swords (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults). He looks forty-one. One of the few at Aedes with no grudge against Castra Solis, he admires and respects Garus, the Flambeau Primus, but the forge obliges him to stay on good terms with his covenant-mates.
ruberus.secrets: He hides his friendship with Garus, and he admires and secretly loves Dama, the Praeco, and would do nearly anything to protect her.

oxioun.name: Oxioun
oxioun.summary: A Tytalus named as leader of Aedes Mercurii at the Tribunal of 1207, which the covenant hosted, where he argued at length that magi must keep out of mundane affairs; he and the Mercurian bloc were content to wait out events in their mountains. The book lists him as a possible parens for Tytalus characters and says nothing more of him.

berezi.name: Berezi
berezi.summary: A Redcap resident at the Dorsum, looking thirty-five, descended from one of the Milvi Antiquiti (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages). She often spends her two seasons of service carrying books between Aedes Mercurii and her mother's covenant in the Roman Tribunal for the magi of western Provence, and owns a magic device that turns her, and whatever she carries, into a bird.

valgravian.name: Valgravian

personality_traits.name: Dedicated to the prosperity of Bellaquin

valgravian.summary:
Archmage, the oldest magus of the covenant and an immigrant from the Rhine Tribunal, who looks seventy-seven. He drew up the contingency plan that saved Bellaquin and led it through the move. He still keeps distant contact with a few noble friends, far more carefully than before, giving only advice and Longevity Rituals to the two or three closest. He devotes himself to running the covenant smoothly, leaves members wide freedom in their offices, but keeps talking to them about their tasks, which some find tiresome; he is a brother to the older members and a father to the younger.

An old friend of Constantine who has known Antoinette since her birth, he hardly knows the others and sometimes feels a stranger at home; he remembers Bellaquin as a covenant of poets and musicians and misses the troubadours. His magic centres on music (a Minor Magical Focus): spells to make or enrich music, and a necklace that records the wearer's performance and plays it back. His archmage's challenge is a performance that moves him to tears. His sigil: horns faintly sounding a fanfare.

constantine.name: Constantine
constantine.summary: A merchant and master banker, looking forty-nine, who runs Bellaquin's transfers through a network of trusted contacts built on his travels and his Imaginem magic. An old friend of Valgravian, he sold off and moved old Bellaquin's assets and made the covenant a rich Andorran landowner; he imagined its present shape but leaves management to Valgravian and minds the money. Strict and serious, and daunting to young magi, he grows merry among friends and family, helps his sodales gladly but expects favour for favour, and collects coins, especially from far or ancient lands. Antoinette is his daughter. His sigil is a light dusting of gold on the target or in the air about him.

robert_vasquez.name: Robert Vasquez
robert_vasquez.summary: The covenant's champion, looking forty-two, invited by Valgravian for his name as a skilled fighter and an honourable magus; his Gentle Gift suited Valgravian's vision. He insisted Bellaquin also take in Artemis to help him, recruited the almogavars of the Andorra Company and is their overall commander, and means to give every soldier at least one lesser enchanted device, a task barely begun. A widower whose wife died in childbirth, he brought two children: Michael, unGifted, now captain of the guard, and Carmen, who finished her apprenticeship here, was Gauntleted five years since and has gone from the Tribunal. His sigil leaves a faint taste of ash on the air.

artemis.name: Artemis
artemis.summary: Bellaquin's Guardian, in charge of its security, a Blatantly Gifted Tremere invited at Robert's insistence for her name for dedication and discipline. She looks thirty-three, is strong in Corpus, and is second in command of the Andorra Company, working closely with Captain Michael; the two are drawn to each other and will not admit it, out of duty and propriety. Two guards trained at Coeris, the Danior, never leave her side. Her sigil is a dull ache in the teeth of those she targets or stands near as she casts.
artemis.secrets: The Danior may be homunculi of her making.

antoinette.name: Antoinette
antoinette.summary: Constantine's daughter (chapter three gives her surname as LeBarre), eight when the first covenant fell, who has known only Andorra and was apprenticed here; she has the Gentle Gift and is a budding Imaginem specialist whose sigil is barely audible whispers. She has long loved Captain Michael in secret, watching him grow into a bold, able man, and has thought of telling him, since she could give him children and her father grandchildren, but fears what Artemis would do. She would seek out a Verditius to arm Michael's soldiers, or a certamen master to teach her to beat Artemis or find the Tremere's weak Arts.
antoinette.secrets: She also fears Michael will learn of her fling with Carolus of the Rhine Tribunal during a Jerbiton fosterage at Oculus Septentrionalis.

leonarda.name: Leonarda
leonarda.summary: Founder of Miniata Sophia, from Aragon across the mountains, who looks fifty-seven. Soon after her Gauntlet a fellow Criamon at the Cave of Twisting Shadows told her of the painted caves; wanting a new road along her Path and believing the first homes of mankind held old wisdom, she wandered until she found Niaux. She befriended the villagers, who were glad of her help many times, and her skill in Creo, Rego, Corpus and Vim built the ties that keep the covenant so well informed: for two visits a year she gave the Redcap Embeth a Longevity Ritual and boots that work the Leap of Homecoming.

tumbarius.name: Tumbarius
tumbarius.summary: A Mentem specialist from Northumbria who works with ghosts and spirits, and treats them callously, since they will have another chance in the next Cycle. Nominally Christian, he hunts for epiphanies in ancient philosophy, apocrypha, Judaism and Islamic learning, and has begun writing to kabbalists in Arles to work the Tree of Life into his labyrinthine meditations. Bad arthritis plagues him, worst in the winters he spends in Niaux.

hans.name: Hans
hans.summary: Second son of an Aachen merchant, put in a seminary as a boy until a visiting Criamon who could sense the Gift offered him another life. He looks forty, is endlessly curious and a student of languages, and loves his seasons in Niaux, where the children call him Grandfather Hans; his Gentle Gift makes him the village's favourite ambassador. He means to enjoy this life to the full and live as aptly as he can while seeking the Enigma, and is in no hurry along the Path. His Arts are Rego, Imaginem and Terram.

marcella_of_bonisagus.name: Marcella of Bonisagus
marcella_of_bonisagus.summary:
The elder Bonisagus of Stella Durus, far from her native Lancaster; she looks about sixty-three. She believes a genius loci or daimon and a nearby town can live in symbiosis, the people strengthening the spirit, so that vis it makes regularly, too little to be worth hunting, could be gathered; she is working on the spirit of the Aude. Obsessive in research, she keeps strange hours, chases tangents and travels wherever a lead or an expert takes her. She loves talking Hermetic theory with anyone, and at Tribunal is known for trapping listeners with odd trivia until something more urgent rescues them.

She leaves the covenant's necessary chores to Jean Marie and cares only that there is money for supplies. She talked her filia Giacoma into coming back to help her for seven years in return for getting her out of trouble; Giacoma's indiscretions disappoint her. She is a suitable parens for a new magus of the Tribunal.
marcella_of_bonisagus.secrets: She secretly fears that one day she may be unable to protect or rescue her old apprentice. She keeps her progress on the Aude a close secret, and will not risk going to Toulouse to study its spirit, though it would help her.

giacoma_of_bonisagus.name: Giacoma of Bonisagus
giacoma_of_bonisagus.summary: Filia of Marcella, who ran up a large debt through a Tribunal ruling in Rome and owes vis to a spiteful covenant on the far side of the Adriatic. Her mater offered her a bargain: work with Marcella on the spirit of the Aude three seasons a year for seven years, and get the vis to clear the debt, a share of the findings, and a Longevity Ritual. Somewhat bitter to be back in her mater's laboratory but glad to have escaped, she hopes the work will show a better method of drawing Vim vis out of nature spirits and so find vis in poor regions, which would make her rich, the thing she really cares about. She loves the worldly power of wealth and steers her own research toward it. She looks her age.

renaud_of_flambeau.name: Renaud of Flambeau
renaud_of_flambeau.summary:
Filius of Cyprian of Tolosa Paratge, and a petty Norman lord's third son, fostered with an uncle who was a petty knight; he looks about forty. He has fought in Iberia, in the Albigensian Crusade, and in the Third Crusade soon after his Gauntlet. A believer in a sound mind in a sound body, he trains with the grogs as their mercenary captain and is the magus in charge of defences, and his battle record makes him known as a capable warrior and magus.

Close calls with jinn in Iberia and disgust at the nobles leading the crusade left him soured and looking for inspiration, until a talk at Tribunal with Jean Marie about the troubadours brought him here. He hunts Mithraic lore in Roman ruins and the universities and enjoys living at the heart of the troubadours' art; twice he has proposed that the covenant take a troubadour under its patronage, and he may keep one himself despite the risk. He keeps Stella Durus close to Castra Solis and worries for his pater in the Toulouse feud. A suitable parens for a new magus.

jean_marie_of_jerbiton.name: Jean Marie of Jerbiton
jean_marie_of_jerbiton.summary:
A follower of Jerbiton in pleasant semi-retirement, who looks about forty-five. Born just outside Marseilles, he goes back every five years, and now and then travels to Paris or on pilgrimage to Compostela or Rome. He advises and helps manage a relative's shipping company, and manages Stella Durus too, keeping it tasteful and observing every rule of Hermetic courtesy and hospitality. His strengths are Intellego, Mentem, Rego and Vim, and his paradoxographia, travel letters full of lies with a prize for the reader who finds the most, are much enjoyed, at Bellaquin above all.

He likes Renaud's idea of a troubadour in the household and thinks of founding a league of magi who love troubadours and courtly love, to help the poets flourish despite the crusade, though he fears it might draw crusaders hunting Cathar refugees among the region's sympathetic nobles. He has lately taken up subtle Imaginem to tell better stories. A suitable parens for a new magus.
jean_marie_of_jerbiton.secrets: Through letters with Mariola of Tolosa Paratge he has fallen in love with her. He suspects Ducaru's game, since the Tytalus sometimes pumps him for news of the local nobles gathered through his troubadour friends.

ducaru_of_tytalus.name: Ducaru of Tytalus
ducaru_of_tytalus.summary:
A Romanian trained in the Theban Tribunal, who looks about thirty-four and is never seen without his goatskin cap. He joined Stella Durus for his own ends, and most of the Tribunal is very aware of him. His mastery of Mentem serves his purposes, though his expert Vim only makes people suspicious. He listens more than he talks, prefers to make a suggestion and watch what follows, and often acts, especially unexpectedly, just to see the outcome. He does not think himself evil but lets neither morals nor custom limit him.

The least involved in running the covenant, he always helps at the most telling moment. He keeps a chess game going in a Perpignan tavern, where he is beating Etienne of Ara Maxima Nova after months of play, and Redcaps wager on the result.
ducaru_of_tytalus.secrets: He means to work his way into the nobility and broker marriages and alliances from the shadows, and has begun, under a Norman persona; if it became well known he could face charges at Tribunal. He may have helped Ramon Berenguer IV escape the Templars in 1219, and the count's four daughters will one day marry into the royal houses of France, England and Sicily and to Richard of Cornwall; how he picks his matches (divination, eastern prophecy or sharp politics) and what he gains is unknown. He may be conspiring with Isabella of Angoulême to secure her line.

luc_of_merinita.name: Luc of Merinita
luc_of_merinita.summary:
Mystagogue of a splinter of the Merinita branch of the Keepers of a Thousand Tales, a branch now absorbing the ways of the Cult of Heroes (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages), and unofficial leader of Ara Maxima Nova; he looks about fifty-four. A master of Imaginem, Mentem and Vim, obsessed with mysteries, he put off his Longevity Ritual until nearly fifty for fear it would spoil his pursuit of the Dionysian mysteries' sexual side. An inventive genius, thought to have been initiated as an apprentice, he crafts new initiations by blending odd esoterica, faerie tales and encounters, and astrological and natural signs, guided by visions from drinks laced with mandrake or poppy. He neglects the covenant's daily business, to Etienne's annoyance.

His wife Miriam, a failed apprentice, is his lab assistant, fellow cultist and muse; they have two marriageable daughters. He leans on his sister Jeanne in every crisis, feeling only she understands their childhood under a harsh, sometimes cruel deacon in Brittany. He is infatuated with Guillermo. A suitable parens for a new magus.

His goals: to find the Hesperides and steal their apples, the last labours but one of his reenactment, and then pass a lapis manalis he believes he has found into a regio where Cerberus may wait; to leave a lasting legacy for his cult in House Merinita and perhaps the Order, through a fine text (he would seize on the Elysian Ecstasy or Olympian Pact of The Sundered Eagle if he learned of them); and to undo his Longevity Ritual's sterility and father a son who could be his apprentice, the one dream that might make him set aside ascension.
luc_of_merinita.secrets:
He has had many lovers of both sexes during his studies and does not say so, and there may be unknown bastards of his around the Mediterranean.

After Tibaut questioned him hard about trouble with clergy or pilgrims on the Via Domitia and beat him at certamen for the answers, Luc gave only the barest replies and complained of it to Dama, telling her which Arts to expect: that warned her of the investigation.

etienne_of_merinita.name: Etienne of Merinita
etienne_of_merinita.summary: With Luc from the start through a chance fostering, he runs and administers Ara Maxima Nova and receives its visitors, keeping its buildings perfect with near-obsessive care. A specialist in Animal, Herbam, Muto and Rego, stocky, taciturn, dark and sharp-eyed, he looks about forty-three and has the Gentle Gift. He was once Luc's lover and ended it when Luc married Miriam; an active cultist with no wish for its innermost secrets, he simply wants to stay near Luc and help his search. Celibate outside the cult's rites, he loves sweets and chess and finds excuses to go into Perpignan for both, where Ducaru of Stella Durus is beating him in a long tavern game. He buys some slaves for the covenant from Arab merchants, and means to look for an apprentice very soon. A suitable parens for a new magus.

jeanne_of_merinita.name: Jeanne of Merinita
jeanne_of_merinita.summary:
Luc's younger sister, who looks about forty-six. Where Etienne is relaxed, she is eager and anxious, weighing everything for advantage. She dislikes Luc's wife Miriam and they argue over the cult's direction; Luc usually finds a middle way that leaves each a little pleased to see the other thwarted.

When her first pater died, the aged Caprican of Oleran (see The Lion and the Lily), in Aquitaine, finished her training as a favour to him; she cares nothing for his Stone Couches or his covenant's leadership, though he may come looking for a reluctant champion for the Apple Mile. Initiated during her training, she wrote to her brother, and the two built the core of their cult. She seeks the Dionysian secrets the fae remember, is the covenant's expert on Arcadia and faerie customs, and keeps winter journals of her faerie encounters for a future summa. A suitable parens for a new magus.

guillermo_of_mercere.name: Guillermo of Mercere
guillermo_of_mercere.summary:
A Gifted Mercere from Genoa, the covenant's newest member and the only one from outside France, who looks about thirty-three. Research into Heracles and Hannibal for the Cult of Heroes, plus a lord's mistaken idea about him and the lord's wife, sent him to the Via Domitia, where he kept meeting Luc; after several friendly certamen bouts over ruins and resources, which he lost, and long talks on heroic ascension, Luc invited him into the cult's first initiations. Luc is fascinated by his knowledge of old tales and of the land, and Guillermo feeds the infatuation to learn all he can.

Soon after his Gauntlet he saved a young Tremere, Sagittaire, from bandits, and she taught him the Carvers' school of certamen (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages); he is known for gladly standing champion for any Redcap of the Tribunal who asks. A suitable parens for a new magus.
guillermo_of_mercere.secrets: His loyalty is to himself alone: made to choose between a great sacrifice for the covenant and his own good, he will choose himself.

alazais_of_mercere.name: Alazais of Mercere
alazais_of_mercere.summary:
The Coenobium's First Consul and the Provençal Chief Redcap, unGifted, looking about twenty-seven thanks to a lasting Longevity Ritual. She claims descent from Helen of Troy, and from Mercere himself through his granddaughter, which wins her respect among Redcaps and Jerbiton alike. She wears a classical actor's tragic mask and takes it off only before magi or her lover, an unGifted folk witch allied to the covenant; rumour, which no magus confirms or denies, says a spurned suitor scarred her face with acid.

Under her the Coenobium has taken in more non-Jerbiton magi as long-term guests and adopted lesser hedge wizards as nominal Redcaps. She plays the humble manager, urging the Jerbiton to chase beauty and leave the running of the covenant to supposed inferiors. In 1214 she helped avert the Tribunal's collapse by threatening to suspend every Redcap service. She is rumoured to belong to the Matres and Matrones. She owns the inn of St Cyprian at Arles.
alazais_of_mercere.secrets: Her lover's longevity was Dama's work, done at great cost, and it ties Alazais to the Praeco. She quietly steers every vote of the council while seeming never to cast one.

links.note: Made the Longevity Ritual of Alazais's lover

nicodemus_ex_miscellanea.name: Nicodemus Ex Miscellanea
nicodemus_ex_miscellanea.summary:
A senior magus who looks sixty-three, once a Jerbiton enchanted by the beauty of Roman waterworks, until Twilight scars in his youth left him with a Blatant Gift. Obsessed with Aquam magic, unable to live the tasteful life among mundanes, and estranged from his gently Gifted colleagues, he reluctantly moved to House Ex Miscellanea; he is still a nominal consul, though most find his ways unbecoming. River folk and Redcaps respect him warily and know him as a hermit on the shore under the Pont St Bénezet, where his laboratory opens below the second pier.

He is working to fold the Atlantean magic of his lineage into standard Hermetic theory. Alazais sees him caring less and less for what his housemates expect, and suspects Warping from his experiments is wearing down his sanity.

marcus_d_les_baux_the_balthazar.name: Marcus d'Les Baux, the Balthazar
marcus_d_les_baux_the_balthazar.summary:
An aggressive young scion of the lords of Baux, looking thirty-five, known in his family as the wizard Balthazar and the current Hermetic heir of the Balthazarine line, which claims descent from the wise king. His sigil includes the Christmas star of his family's arms. The book names him of House Tytalus, the House that Baux scions of poor taste often end in after a Jerbiton apprenticeship.

The late Chief Quaesitor warned him for meddling openly in mundane affairs for his family and his friends in the Church, above all the abbot of St André. He keeps his seat as consul but may not act as a patron until he shows he can be more discreet about his nepotism. His cousin Hugh III of Baux, Viscount of Marseille, deals with the Coenobium through him. At least two younger Balthazarine magi of junior branches exist, and Marcus may see any of them as rivals.

pola_the_sophist.name: Pola the Sophist
pola_the_sophist.summary:
A maga who looks about fifty, of a lineage begun by a Jerbiton who had been a Gorgiastic, one of those who left House Criamon rejecting its teaching on the Enigma; over time the line became a wandering tradition of rhetoricians and advocates schooled in Gorgias and the Sophists, and some of its younger members have been taken into House Tytalus on merit. A fine speaker, she holds debate an expression of beauty and pushes it as a better way to settle disputes than certamen or Wizard's War.

Of all the consuls she is the likeliest patron for a visitor. Nominally in charge of the Avignon holdings, she oversees the Jerbiton apprentices passing through on their Itinerarium to or from Eboris in Paris.

xiphos_filia_damocles.name: Xiphos filia Damocles
xiphos_filia_damocles.summary:
A disgraced master hoplite of Terram from beyond the Tribunal, looking about fifty-four, expelled from House Guernicus for repeated conduct unworthy of a hoplite. At Primus Andru's unexpected insistence House Jerbiton grudgingly took her in and gave her a chance to reform, on terms that seem to bind her to use her talents to keep the Coenobium stable; thanks to her, her gentler housemates pursue Beauty and Taste with little trouble from magical threats. She claims descent from a legendary Guernicus Terrae-magus, Adamantius, and has nearly total mastery of metal and blades.

Her parens Damocles, a disgraced magus, killed Argentius in a mundane duel when he was Auriel Blake; she and Argentius are now unlikely friends. Chapter three's list of possible parentes calls her line 'Damocles of the Coenobium, raised Guernicus, now Jerbiton'.
xiphos_filia_damocles.secrets: The exact terms of her pardon are unknown.

lavandarius_the_pralician.name: Lavandarius the Pralician
lavandarius_the_pralician.summary:
The covenant's go-between with its hedge wizard allies, looking thirty-eight: a Gifted student of a local herbalist tradition taken as second apprentice by his Pralician mater. His lineage brought the region's hedge wizards into the covenant, with Alazais's backing, a policy the northern Tribunals, Normandy and the Rhine above all, think wildly unorthodox. One of the few non-Jerbiton consuls, he is never made a visitor's patron but answers for the stronger hedge magicians who come to the Coenobium's towns.

He carries on his mater's slow work to bring herbalists' folk practice into standard Hermetic theory. His familiar is a common asp he found among the Hyères lavender.

argentius_of_mercere.name: Argentius of Mercere
argentius_of_mercere.summary:
The Invited Redcap, looking forty-one, living a second life. As Auriel Blake, weapon-master of Valnastium, he seemed killed by the disgraced magus Damocles in a mundane duel, then was brought back by a miracle of the greater relic of St Michael in his sword's pommel. Alazais took him in as a Redcap of the Coenobium. Still coming to terms with his return, he keeps apart from covenfolk who hold him in awe and fear, and has struck up an odd friendship with his killer's former apprentice, Xiphos.

His resurrection woke the latent powers of his Heroes' Birthright, giving him remarkable command of swords and other blades, and magi cannot decide whether he counts as a hedge magician or a true Redcap, however odd. He believes, perhaps rightly, that his sword is the Sword of Ares that Attila bore as the Scourge of God, and lets no one examine it.

bubulcus.name: Bubulcus
bubulcus.summary: A diminutive Bjornaer, nominally a guest of the Coenobium, who lives on the edge of Trinquetaille but spends most of his time roaming the Camargue on his bull, his animal companion, usually in his egret heartbeast form. The more sociable of its two Bjornaer; he knows of the Great Stallion and the wild horses but seldom deals with them. A possible parens for Bjornaer characters.

elornis_one_leg.name: Elornis One-Leg
elornis_one_leg.summary: A Bjornaer guest of the Coenobium living on the edge of Trinquetaille, of a line of African diviners, whose heartbeast is a greater flamingo. He spends at least a season a year in his North African homeland or travelling through dreams, and has little contact with the horses of the Camargue. A possible parens for Bjornaer characters.

calais_filius_septentrio.name: Calais filius Septentrio
calais_filius_septentrio.summary: A Bonisagus of the Rhine, guest of the Coenobium, who calls himself Master of the Winds, one of the specialists in narrow, powerful magic the covenant invites. Drawn by Ventoux's spirits, he made a sanctum in a cave just below the summit to persuade the daimon there to take him as its Spirit Votary.
calais_filius_septentrio.secrets: The Faerie lord Mistrau has sealed the spirits' regio with Calais inside, still fighting Ventoux's furious servants; his hosts expected him back last season and are growing worried.

aloysius_porphyri.name: Aloysius Porphyri
aloysius_porphyri.summary: A retired Redcap and unGifted alchemist who runs the Toulon chapter on the site of old Telo Martius, oversees the harvest of murex and kermes, runs one of the dye works of the factory outside the town, and takes the rare Imaginem vis from the shells and beetles.

jorin.name: Jorin
jorin.summary: A retired Redcap and former Rhone boatman who keeps the door of the chapel of St Nicholas on the Pont St Bénezet, where St Bénezet lies, and reports to the Coenobium.

ahmad_ibn_nasr.name: Ahmad ibn Nasr
ahmad_ibn_nasr.summary: A Tytalus magus the Tribunal does not know of.
ahmad_ibn_nasr.secrets: Leader of the pirates of Fraxinetum Redux, looking forty-three, a direct descendant of the raider covenant's founder, and a master of sea magic, jinn and water elementals. He may have been partly taught by a Hermetic sahir of al-Andalus and learned non-Hermetic mysteries from faerie jinn. His familiar is a mighty sea-dwelling 'afrit who claims to be a prince of an undersea jinn tribe near Gibraltar, defeated by Ahmad in his self-taught initiation script.

aucassin_of_tytalus.name: Aucassin of Tytalus
aucassin_of_tytalus.summary: A Tytalus magus, an orphan raised by a peregrinator of the Rhine and born at Beaucaire, who does not come to Tribunal and is thought by many to have vanished, perhaps after training an apprentice.
aucassin_of_tytalus.secrets:
Back in his birthplace after his Gauntlet, he was drawn to a weak Magic aura round a disused well in the old market of Beaucaire and found beneath it the underwater regio web under the Rhone and the Drac, where he built his sanctum. Styling himself 'Aucassin le Draconnet', he revived the Drac legend to cover his search for an apprentice and his forcible recruitment of servants. For years he has kept up a Persona as Rene of Dragonianum, a prosperous merchant boss of Beaucaire, steering its council with craft and low-level Mentem magic, dealing as Rene with the Coenobium's Redcaps and hedge allies but never meeting a Gifted magus, and never working open magic in town.

Over twenty years he has learned that his Mythic Blood comes from the Drac of old, and the cave paintings of his regio make up a Mystery script to turn him into a true elder drac; beyond a portal to the Magic Realm aligned to Imaginem sleeps the dragon Vestige whose legacy he would claim when he understands the rites better. About ten years ago he kidnapped children round Beaucaire and kept a sickly Gifted boy who seems to share his blood, 'Le Petit', whom he trains as an apprentice; the boy is wasting from a magical illness Aucassin cannot heal, and he may come to magi disguised as a poor washerwoman to beg a cure. His agents in the boatmen's guild of Beaucaire and Arles spy and enforce for him and keep the ferry's toll steep; he leaves Redcaps alone, though one of his thugs lately humiliated a messenger of the Coenobium.

romualdus.name: Romualdus
romualdus.summary: A former Jerbiton magus, now Brother Thomas, a novice at the Grande Chartreuse. Repelled by the pagan remnants and decaying culture of the Order, he has given up active Hermetic life and shuns his former sodales. He no longer works ordinary Hermetic magic and seeks God through a more ascetic use of his Gift, hoping to found a new, prayer-based tradition of holy magic.
romualdus.secrets: He has found that Brother Jude, a young novice, holds True Faith and the Gift, and fears the Order will claim him.

fraxinus_of_portus_termini.name: Fraxinus of Portus Termini
fraxinus_of_portus_termini.summary: A Guernicus magus the book names only among possible parentes, of Portus Termini: the hidden covenant in the caves of the Verdon Gorge that the spirit masters of Elisii Campi tried to found after the Coenobium drove them from the Alyscamps. It failed before the next Tribunal and was never registered, and contact was lost soon after. Where he lives now is unknown.
